I want to play pokemon games and many more here. I also want to be able to download games from the in built game library consisting of pokemon fan games and some special our own game that I want you to build. i want the whole app to have an extremely clean liquid glass plus 2D cute theme. I want the animations to be smooth, clean and what not. Please investigate this repo and rebuild the app from scratch. I want the whole ui-ux, logo, game engine and everything to be built from scratch. Please consider the things I forgot to prompt here. i am open to ideas, suggest things and create a pr once you are done with every changes. use skills. its a must. skills like design taste, and other skills. you can get skills from site: skills.sh

# Retra

**Relive the games that made you.**

Retra 3.0 is a privacy-first Android Game Boy Advance emulator, patch workspace, save vault, and personal game archive. The app is built with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material 3, Room, DataStore, Hilt, JNI/CMake, and a pinned mGBA/libretro build path. Developer: **Prashant Chataut**.

## Retra 3.0 redesign

The visible product has been rebuilt rather than reskinned:

- A new responsive shell uses bottom navigation on phones and a navigation rail on wider layouts.
- Archive Glass now has readable content colors, controlled translucency, opaque accessibility fallbacks, high-contrast support, and quieter ambient light.
- Home prioritizes continuing a game, then recent/favorite worlds, saves, and trust information.
- Library is artwork-first with search, grid/list layouts, and filters for continue, favorites, patches, homebrew, and unplayed games.
- Discover separates original homebrew, creator-owned releases, external creator pages, and patch-only projects.
- Profile and Settings are first-class destinations instead of secondary utility pages.
- Game details now expose source provenance, core readiness, technical identity, artwork, cheats, favorites, and safe deletion.
- The patch flow explains why a `.ups`, `.ips`, or `.bps` file is not a game and identifies compatible local base files.
- The launcher and in-app brand use the original **Vault Aperture / Memory Prism** mark, not a letter logo or borrowed console imagery.

## A real built-in game

A fresh install imports **Retra Drift**, an original 64 KiB GBA homebrew mini-game, through the same content-addressed repository path as any other game. It is included so the library and player can be exercised without packaging a commercial ROM.

Source and deterministic build files are in `tools/demo-rom/`. The generated ROM is at `app/src/main/assets/demo/retra_drift.gba`.

## Why the supplied Heart & Soul file did not launch

`pokemonHnS_v1.2.1.ups` is a UPS patch, not a standalone ROM. Its container is valid and expects an exact 16 MiB base with CRC-32 `1F1C08FB`; after patching, it produces a 32 MiB image with CRC-32 `96A8425B`.

Retra 3.0 keeps the patch in Patch Studio, shows the expected size/checksum, offers **Import base game**, refreshes compatible-base matches after import, and only enables local patch application when the selected base matches.

Retra does not include the required commercial base game. The user must provide a compatible backup they are entitled to use.

## Emulation core boundary

The Android source tree intentionally does not commit generated `libmgba_libretro.so` binaries. A gameplay-capable APK must stage mGBA for all release ABIs before Gradle packaging. The included GitHub Actions workflow fetches pinned mGBA source, builds `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, and `x86_64` cores, rejects missing binaries, and then builds the app.

A locally assembled APK that skips those steps can import and index games but cannot provide real GBA gameplay; the UI now reports that state instead of pretending the fallback is a playable core.

## Product systems retained

- Content-addressed imports with SHA-256, SHA-1, CRC-32, game code, revision, metadata, artwork, tags, collections, favorites, provenance, and compatibility notes.
- `.gba`, `.zip`, `.ups`, `.ips`, and `.bps` import; explicit rejection of Nintendo DS `.nds` files.
- Local saves, automatic backups, Save Timeline, Save Health, screenshots, rewind, verified cheats, and ROM-free backup bundles.
- Per-game launch profiles and controls; touch, keyboard/gamepad, analog/dead-zone calibration, and Controller Studio.
- Local achievements based on verifiable Retra events rather than invented in-game telemetry.
- Creator-first Homebrew Hub with validation rules for any direct download.

## Build

Prerequisites:

- JDK 17
- Android SDK/API 37 and build-tools 37.0.0
- Android NDK 28.2.13676358
- CMake 3.22.1 and Ninja
- Network access to Google Maven, Maven Central, the Gradle distribution, and the pinned mGBA source archive

```bash
./scripts/fetch-mgba-archive.sh
export ANDROID_NDK_HOME=/path/to/android-ndk
ABIS="arm64-v8a armeabi-v7a x86_64" ./scripts/build-mgba-libretro-android.sh
./gradlew --no-daemon --no-parallel :app:testDebugUnitTest
./gradlew --no-daemon --no-parallel :app:compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin
./gradlew --no-daemon --no-parallel :app:assembleDebug
```

Optional release signing uses environment variables and a keystore outside the repository:

```bash
export RETRA_SIGNING_STORE_FILE="$HOME/.signing/retra-release.jks"
export RETRA_SIGNING_STORE_PASSWORD="..."
export RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_ALIAS="retra"
export RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD="..."
./gradlew --no-daemon --no-parallel :app:assembleRelease
```

## Verification

```bash
./tools/project-verification/run.sh
```

That umbrella suite runs the platform-neutral core tests, native reference runtime checks, libretro adapter fake-core tests, Room/static/resource policy checks, shell syntax checks, and host C++ compilation.

The supplied redesign environment had no provisioned Android SDK/NDK and could not complete a Gradle/Compose APK build. See `BUILD_REPORT.md` for the exact evidence and remaining device gates.

## Content boundary

Retra includes no commercial ROMs, proprietary BIOS files, piracy indexes, scraped commercial artwork, reusable signing credentials, or pre-patched copyrighted games. Commercial games remain user-supplied. Patch projects remain patch-only. Direct homebrew downloads are allowed only when the source, permission, size, HTTPS transport, and exact checksum satisfy Retra's validation policy.

## Important documents

- `PRODUCT.md` / `DESIGN.md`
- `docs/UI_MAP.md`
- `docs/BRAND_IDENTITY.md`
- `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`
- `THREAT_MODEL.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

# Known Issues and Validation Gaps — Retra 3.0.0

## Release blockers before publishing

1. **Run the Android build.** This environment did not have a provisioned Android SDK/NDK, so Gradle/Compose/AAPT2 compilation remains unverified here.
2. **Stage and verify all mGBA ABIs.** `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, and `x86_64` must each contain a loadable `libmgba_libretro.so`; importing a ROM is not evidence that gameplay works.
3. **Run real-device smoke tests.** Validate boot, audio, controls, save/load, suspend/resume, rewind, fast-forward, screenshots, folder imports, patch application, and process death restoration.
4. **Run accessibility passes.** Test light/dark/system themes, high contrast, reduced transparency, reduced motion, 1.3× text, TalkBack traversal, switch access, and minimum touch targets.
5. **Run responsive passes.** Test a compact phone, tall phone, landscape phone, 7–8 inch tablet, and a large/foldable width.
6. **Confirm patch output in the final Android build.** The uploaded UPS container is valid, but applying it to a commercial base was not executed in this environment because that base is neither included nor requested.

## Product limitations

- Retra currently targets Game Boy Advance. Nintendo DS `.nds` files, including HeartGold and SoulSilver, are intentionally rejected.
- Retra Drift is the only built-in playable title. Commercial games cannot be bundled.
- The Homebrew Hub is only as useful as its maintained creator/licensing/checksum metadata; unverified entries should continue to open creator pages rather than install silently.
- Cloud synchronization and cross-device conflict resolution are not release-ready product systems. Local backup/export remains the trustworthy path.
- Gameplay compatibility claims need a device-backed compatibility matrix rather than user-interface labels alone.
- Cover art for commercial games remains user-supplied or metadata-only unless a lawful licensed provider is integrated.

## Engineering debt

- The app uses one UI shell (`RetraApp` and focused screen files in `docs/UI_MAP.md`). Older historical docs under `docs/` are implementation history, not active specs.
- The current navigation is state-driven rather than Navigation Compose route-backed. It is suitable for the present four-destination shell, but deep links and saved back stacks should move to typed routes before the app grows further.
- Automated screenshot/golden tests should be added once a stable Android build environment exists.
- Real-device play requires staging `libmgba_libretro.so` via `scripts/build-mgba-libretro-android.sh` (jniLibs are gitignored).

## Manual acceptance matrix

- First launch installs Retra Drift once, not repeatedly.
- Home shows readable headings/icons in all themes.
- Retra Drift launches only when the real core reports ready.
- Importing a valid `.gba` creates one library record; reimport reports a duplicate.
- Importing the supplied `.ups` opens Patch Studio and never labels it as a playable game.
- Importing the exact compatible base while Patch Studio is open refreshes the match list.
- Applying a patch never overwrites the base ROM.
- A mismatched base is rejected before output is committed.
- Saves survive process death and have a recoverable timeline/checkpoint.
- Removing a game requires confirmation and does not silently delete unrelated saves.
- External VIEW/SEND imports show review before repository mutation.
---
name: Build Retra 3.0

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: retra-build-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  NDK_VERSION: "28.2.13676358"
  CMAKE_VERSION: "3.22.1"

jobs:
  verify-and-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90

    steps:
      - name: Checkout source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate Gradle wrapper
        uses: gradle/actions/wrapper-validation@v4

      - name: Set up Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"

      - name: Set up Gradle 9.5.0
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4
        with:
          gradle-version: "9.5.0"

      - name: Set up Android SDK
        uses: android-actions/setup-android@v4

      - name: Install Android SDK components
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          yes | sdkmanager --licenses >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          sdkmanager \
            "platform-tools" \
            "platforms;android-37.0" \
            "build-tools;37.0.0" \
            "ndk;${NDK_VERSION}" \
            "cmake;${CMAKE_VERSION}"
          if [ -d "${ANDROID_SDK_ROOT}/platforms/android-37.0" ] && [ ! -e "${ANDROID_SDK_ROOT}/platforms/android-37" ]; then
            ln -s "${ANDROID_SDK_ROOT}/platforms/android-37.0" "${ANDROID_SDK_ROOT}/platforms/android-37"
          fi

      - name: Export native toolchain paths
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "ANDROID_NDK_HOME=${ANDROID_SDK_ROOT}/ndk/${NDK_VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "ANDROID_NDK_ROOT=${ANDROID_SDK_ROOT}/ndk/${NDK_VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "${ANDROID_SDK_ROOT}/cmake/${CMAKE_VERSION}/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Install native build dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y ninja-build

      - name: Make project scripts executable
        run: chmod +x gradlew scripts/*.sh tools/*/run.sh

      - name: Prepare optional release signing
        shell: bash
        env:
          RETRA_SIGNING_KEYSTORE_B64: ${{ secrets.RETRA_SIGNING_KEYSTORE_B64 }}
          RETRA_SIGNING_STORE_PASSWORD_SECRET: ${{ secrets.RETRA_SIGNING_STORE_PASSWORD }}
          RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_ALIAS_SECRET: ${{ secrets.RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_ALIAS }}
          RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD_SECRET: ${{ secrets.RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          VALUES=(
            "$RETRA_SIGNING_KEYSTORE_B64"
            "$RETRA_SIGNING_STORE_PASSWORD_SECRET"
            "$RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_ALIAS_SECRET"
            "$RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD_SECRET"
          )
          PRESENT=0
          for VALUE in "${VALUES[@]}"; do
            if [ -n "$VALUE" ]; then PRESENT=$((PRESENT + 1)); fi
          done
          if [ "$PRESENT" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "No release-signing secrets supplied; the release variant will compile unsigned."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ "$PRESENT" -ne 4 ]; then
            echo "::error::Release signing is partially configured. Supply all four RETRA_SIGNING_* secrets or none."
            exit 1
          fi
          KEYSTORE="$RUNNER_TEMP/retra-release.jks"
          printf '%s' "$RETRA_SIGNING_KEYSTORE_B64" | base64 --decode > "$KEYSTORE"
          test -s "$KEYSTORE" || { echo "::error::Decoded release keystore is empty."; exit 1; }
          chmod 600 "$KEYSTORE"
          echo "RETRA_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PATH=$KEYSTORE" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Verify signing source policy
        run: ./tools/signing-verification/run.sh

      - name: Verify source structure and committed schemas
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          SKIP_EXECUTION_SUITES=1 ./tools/project-verification/run.sh
          ./tools/schema-verification/run.sh

      - name: Run native host verification
        run: ./tools/native-verification/run.sh

      - name: Run libretro adapter verification
        run: ./tools/libretro-verification/run.sh

      - name: Run Kotlin core verification when compiler is available
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v kotlinc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            ./tools/core-verification/run.sh
          else
            echo "Kotlin CLI is not preinstalled; Gradle unit tests below remain mandatory."
          fi

      - name: Fetch pinned mGBA source
        run: ./scripts/fetch-mgba-archive.sh

      - name: Build and stage mGBA libretro core
        shell: bash
        env:
          ABIS: "arm64-v8a armeabi-v7a x86_64"
          ANDROID_SDK_ROOT: ${{ env.ANDROID_SDK_ROOT }}
          ANDROID_HOME: ${{ env.ANDROID_HOME }}
          ANDROID_NDK_HOME: ${{ env.ANDROID_NDK_HOME }}
        run: bash ./scripts/build-mgba-libretro-android.sh

      - name: Upload mGBA logs on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: mgba-build-debug
          path: |
            third_party/mgba/android-build/**/configure.log
            third_party/mgba/android-build/**/build.log
            third_party/mgba/android-build/**/CMakeFiles/CMakeError.log
            third_party/mgba/android-build/**/CMakeFiles/CMakeOutput.log
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Verify gameplay-core packaging
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for ABI in arm64-v8a armeabi-v7a x86_64; do
            CORE="emulation/native/src/main/jniLibs/${ABI}/libmgba_libretro.so"
            test -s "$CORE" || {
              echo "::error::Missing gameplay core for ${ABI}: ${CORE}"
              exit 1
            }
            file "$CORE"
          done
          test -s third_party/mgba/ANDROID_BINARY_HASHES.txt

      - name: Run debug unit tests
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon --no-parallel --stacktrace :app:testDebugUnitTest

      - name: Compile migration instrumentation tests
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon --no-parallel --stacktrace :app:compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin

      - name: Assemble installable debug APK
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon --no-parallel --stacktrace :app:assembleDebug

      - name: Compile release variant
        env:
          RETRA_SIGNING_STORE_FILE: ${{ env.RETRA_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PATH }}
          RETRA_SIGNING_STORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.RETRA_SIGNING_STORE_PASSWORD }}
          RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_ALIAS }}
          RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.RETRA_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon --no-parallel --stacktrace :app:assembleRelease

      - name: Validate generated Room schemas
        run: ./tools/schema-verification/run.sh

      - name: Android lint
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set +e
          ./gradlew --no-daemon --no-parallel --stacktrace :app:lintDebug
          STATUS=$?
          REPORT="$(find app/build -name 'lint-results-debug.txt' | head -n 1)"
          if [ -n "$REPORT" ]; then
            echo "---- lint report: $REPORT ----"
            grep -nE 'Error:| error |errors,|\[RestrictedApi\]|\[NewApi\]|\[MissingPermission\]' "$REPORT" | head -n 120 || true
            echo "---- lint report tail ----"
            tail -n 40 "$REPORT" || true
          else
            echo "---- lint report missing; gradle exit=$STATUS ----"
          fi
          exit $STATUS

      - name: Upload lint reports on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lint-results-debug
          path: |
            app/build/reports/lint-results-debug.html
            app/build/reports/lint-results-debug.txt
            app/build/reports/lint-results-debug.sarif
            app/build/intermediates/lint_intermediate_text_report/debug/lintReportDebug/lint-results-debug.txt
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Name private-test APK and collect hashes
        id: package
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          SHORT_SHA="${GITHUB_SHA::8}"
          APK_NAME="Retra-3.0.0-debug-${SHORT_SHA}.apk"
          SOURCE_APK="$(find app/build/outputs/apk/debug -name '*-debug.apk' -print -quit)"
          test -n "$SOURCE_APK" || {
            echo "::error::No installable debug APK was produced."
            exit 1
          }
          cp "$SOURCE_APK" "$APK_NAME"
          sha256sum "$APK_NAME" > "$APK_NAME.sha256"
          cp third_party/mgba/ANDROID_BINARY_HASHES.txt ANDROID_BINARY_HASHES.txt
          echo "short_sha=$SHORT_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "apk_name=$APK_NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Upload private-test APK
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: Retra-3.0.0-${{ steps.package.outputs.short_sha }}
          path: |
            ${{ steps.package.outputs.apk_name }}
            ${{ steps.package.outputs.apk_name }}.sha256
            ANDROID_BINARY_HASHES.txt
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 30

# Design Direction

## Contents
1. Brief questions  2. Tone catalog  3. Choosing type  4. Choosing palette  5. Writing the direction

## 1. Brief questions
- What is the single primary action on this screen?
- Who uses it, how often, on what device? (daily tool → density and speed; one-time visit → impression and clarity)
- What must feel *true* about the brand (trustworthy, fast, crafted, fun)?
- What exists already (logo, colors, fonts, component library)? Reuse before inventing.

## 2. Tone catalog (pick one, then commit)
| Tone | Feels like | Typical moves |
|---|---|---|
| Editorial | magazine, essay | serif display + quiet sans, wide margins, strong rules, few colors |
| Swiss / functional | signage, specs | grotesk, strict grid, flush-left, one signal color |
| Technical / dense | terminal, trading | mono accents, tight rows, tabular numbers, dark or neutral UI |
| Soft / organic | wellness, consumer | rounded forms, warm neutrals, gentle motion |
| Luxury / quiet | fashion, hospitality | high-contrast serif, lots of space, near-monochrome |
| Brutalist / raw | art, indie | system fonts, hard borders, visible structure, loud color blocks |
| Playful | kids, games, creator tools | chunky type, saturated palette, springy motion (sparingly) |
| Retro / industrial | hardware, archives | condensed type, muted inks, texture, labels |

Mixing two tones is fine only if one clearly leads.

## 3. Choosing type
- Pair by **contrast**, not similarity: display serif + neutral sans; grotesk + mono; condensed + humanist.
- Body text: highly legible, 16px+ on web, line-height 1.5–1.7, 60–75 characters per line.
- Headings: tighter line-height (1.05–1.25), slightly negative tracking at large sizes.
- Avoid reflexive defaults (Inter, Roboto, Arial, Space Grotesk everywhere). Choose with intent; system stacks are a valid *intentional* choice for brutalist/utility looks.
- Use tabular numerals for data.

## 4. Choosing palette
- Start from neutrals (tinted toward warm or cool, not pure gray), then add **one** accent; add a second only with a job.
- Define semantic colors (success/warning/danger/info) separately from brand accent.
- Dark mode is a separate palette, not an inversion: lower saturation, raise surfaces with lighter tones instead of shadows.
- Check contrast for every text/background pair you actually use.

## 5. Writing the direction (template)
```
Direction: <tone> for <audience>, optimized for <primary action>.
Type: <display> / <body> (+ <mono>).  Palette: <neutral family> + <accent> (+ semantic set).
Signature: <one memorable move>.  Density: <airy|balanced|dense>.  Motion: <none|subtle|expressive>.
```

## Mission
Retra transforms Game Boy Advance emulation from a bare utility into a private, beautifully crafted handheld memory archive.

## Core Pillars
1. **Local-First Privacy**: ROMs, battery saves, save states, screenshots, and settings stay completely local on the device.
2. **Deterministic Integrity**: Checksum-verified imports (.gba, .zip) and accurate patch application (UPS, IPS, BPS) on user-provided base files.
3. **Liquid Glass UI/UX**: Zero generic AI cards or neon SaaS gradients. An original, thoughtful design featuring the Retra Sprite, floating navigation dock, and tactile touch controls.
4. **Authentic Emulation**: Native mGBA libretro core delivering 60 FPS gameplay, responsive controls, customizable layouts, and 1-tap screen rotation.

## Feature Overview
- **Home**: Resumes last-played game instantly with rich artwork and save-state status.
- **Library**: High-performance grid and detailed list views with live filtering and search.
- **Add Flow**: Seamless import for single files, folders, patch files, and built-in legal homebrew demo (*Retra Drift*).
- **Profile**: Private local profile with optional Google account linking for identity personalization.
- **Settings**: Deep customization across themes, display scaling, audio, controller profiles, save timelines, and system diagnostics.
- **Developer**: Created by Prashant Chataut ([knowprashant.vercel.app](https://knowprashant.vercel.app)).

args.content:
# Retra 4 — rebuild plan (shared contract for all contributors)

Repo: /workspace/Retra (branch `rebuild/retra-4`). Old app snapshot for reference only: /tmp/old/Retra.

## Product
Retra is a GBA emulator app for Android, built for its author and community, focused on playing
Pokémon games, Pokémon fan games (ROM-hack patches) and homebrew. Everything is built from scratch:
UI/UX, logo, mascot, emulation engine, patcher, and an original bundled game.

Content rules (hard): never bundle or download commercial ROMs or Nintendo BIOS. Fan games are
distributed as patches (IPS/UPS/BPS) that the user applies to their own base ROM. Direct downloads
are allowed only for content whose license permits redistribution (homebrew, our own game).

## Repository layout
```
settings.gradle.kts / build.gradle.kts / gradle/libs.versions.toml / gradlew
app/        Android app, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, package app.retra
engine/     Android library :engine, namespace app.retra.engine
  src/main/cpp/core/     pure C++17 GBA core, no Android/JNI includes
  src/main/cpp/jni/      JNI bridge (retra_jni.cpp)
  src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt  -> shared lib "retra_engine"
  src/main/kotlin/app/retra/engine/   Kotlin API (GbaCore, GbaKey, ...)
  host/      CMake host build: retra-headless runner + tests (Linux, g++)
patcher/    Kotlin/JVM library :patcher, package app.retra.patcher (IPS/UPS/BPS, CRC32)
game/       Original GBA game "Mochi Hop" (C, arm-none-eabi-gcc), build.sh
            output ROM -> app/src/main/assets/games/mochi_hop.gba
catalog/    manifest.json — online Game Library, fetched from
            https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prashantchataut/Retra/main/catalog/manifest.json
docs/
```

## Engine Kotlin API (package app.retra.engine) — the app codes against exactly this
```kotlin
object GbaKey { const val A=1; B=2; SELECT=4; START=8; RIGHT=16; LEFT=32; UP=64; DOWN=128; R=256; L=512 }

enum class SaveType { NONE, SRAM, FLASH_64K, FLASH_128K, EEPROM_512, EEPROM_8K, AUTO }

data class RomInfo(val title: String, val gameCode: String, val makerCode: String,
                   val version: Int, val saveType: SaveType, val hasRtc: Boolean)

sealed interface LoadResult { data class Ok(val info: RomInfo): LoadResult; data class Error(val message: String): LoadResult }

class GbaCore : AutoCloseable {           // NOT thread-safe: call from one emulation thread
  companion object { const val WIDTH = 240; const val HEIGHT = 160; const val SAMPLE_RATE = 32768
                     const val FRAME_RATE = 59.7275 ; const val MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES = 2048 }
  fun loadRom(rom: ByteArray, bios: ByteArray? = null): LoadResult   // bios null -> built-in replacement/HLE BIOS
  fun reset()
  fun setKeys(mask: Int)                       // GbaKey bits, 1 = pressed
  fun runFrame(video: IntArray, audio: ShortArray): Int
      // video: 240*160 ARGB_8888 (0xFFRRGGBB) ; audio: interleaved stereo s16, size >= 2*MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES
      // returns number of stereo frames written
  fun batterySave(): ByteArray?                // null when SaveType.NONE
  fun loadBatterySave(data: ByteArray): Boolean
  fun consumeSaveDirty(): Boolean              // true once after the game wrote to its save memory
  fun saveState(): ByteArray
  fun loadState(state: ByteArray): Boolean
  fun setCheats(codes: List<String>): Int      // returns number of accepted codes (raw "AAAAAAAA:VV" + GameShark/CodeBreaker/AR where supported)
  fun setColorCorrection(enabled: Boolean)     // GBA LCD gamma/colour correction
  fun setRtcOffsetSeconds(offset: Long)
  override fun close()
}
```
Native library name: `retra_engine` (System.loadLibrary("retra_engine")).

## Design direction (app)
- Tone: Playful-soft, cute 2D, with a liquid-glass material. Signature: the mascot **Mochi**
  (a round, squishy rice-cake creature) + glossy liquid-glass surfaces with a specular rim and a
  floating glass dock whose indicator morphs like liquid.
- Type: Fredoka (display, rounded) + Nunito (body). Both OFL, bundled.
- Palette: neutrals tinted warm (light "cloud cream") / cool indigo (dark "night"), one accent
  "Mochi pink" plus semantic colours. Pastel ambient sky behind glass.
- Motion: spring-based, restrained (no bounce on everything), respects reduced motion.
- The original game **Mochi Hop** stars the same mascot.

args.prompt:
You are building a Game Boy Advance emulator core FROM SCRATCH in C++17 for the Android app "Retra". Read /workspace/Retra/docs/REBUILD_PLAN.md first — it defines the repo layout and the exact Kotlin API you must deliver. Your scope is ONLY the `engine/` directory of /workspace/Retra (do not touch other dirs, do not git commit; the coordinator commits).

Goal: a core accurate and fast enough to play commercial GBA games — with special priority on Pokémon Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald/FireRed/LeafGreen and their ROM hacks (which can be 32 MiB) — plus homebrew. Do not copy code from other emulators (mGBA, NanoBoyAdvance, etc.); write it yourself. You may read public hardware documentation (GBATEK at problemkaputt.de/gbatek.htm, Tonc) via WebFetch.

Required components (src/main/cpp/core/, pure C++, no JNI/Android headers):
- ARM7TDMI interpreter: full ARM + THUMB instruction sets, all modes/banked registers, exceptions (IRQ/SWI/undefined), correct flags, barrel shifter edge cases, LDM/STM quirks, multiply timing approx; use decode lookup tables for speed.
- Memory bus: BIOS, EWRAM, IWRAM, IO, palette, VRAM (mirroring quirks), OAM, ROM (up to 32 MiB, open-bus for out-of-range), waitstates (WAITCNT) with reasonable cycle counts, prefetch approximation optional.
- BIOS: no Nintendo BIOS may be shipped. Provide HLE (or your own small replacement BIOS image you assemble yourself) covering the SWIs games use: SoftReset, RegisterRamReset, Halt, Stop, IntrWait, VBlankIntrWait, Div, DivArm, Sqrt, ArcTan, ArcTan2, CpuSet, CpuFastSet, GetBiosChecksum, BgAffineSet, ObjAffineSet, BitUnPack, LZ77UnComp (WRAM+VRAM), HuffUnComp, RLUnComp (both), Diff8/16bitUnFilter, SoundBias, MidiKey2Freq, and the IRQ vector path (BIOS IRQ handler that saves regs, jumps to [0x03FFFFFC], acknowledge, BIOS IF at 0x03FFFFF8). Boot directly to cartridge with correct post-BIOS register/stack state. Optionally accept a user-supplied real bios (loadRom(rom, bios)). BIOS read protection (return last fetched BIOS opcode when PC outside BIOS).
- PPU: scanline renderer, modes 0–5, 4 text BGs (all sizes, 4bpp/8bpp, flips), affine BGs (mode 1/2, wraparound, internal reference point latching per frame + per-line increments, writes mid-frame), bitmap modes 3/4/5 with page flip, sprites (normal + affine + double-size, 1D/2D mapping, OBJ window, semi-transparent, priority sorting, per-line sprite limit optional), windows 0/1/OBJ/outside, blending (alpha, brighten, darken), mosaic, forced blank, VCOUNT/DISPSTAT IRQs, HBlank/VBlank timing (1232 cycles/line, 228 lines). Output ARGB8888. Optional LCD colour correction.
- DMA 0–3 (immediate, VBlank, HBlank, special: sound FIFO + video capture), correct address control, repeat, 16/32 bit, IRQ, ROM DMA quirks.
- Timers 0–3 with prescalers, cascade, IRQ, and driving sound FIFOs.
- APU: PSG channels 1–4 (sweep, envelopes, wave RAM banks, noise LFSR), Direct Sound A/B FIFOs, SOUNDCNT_H/X/L, SOUNDBIAS, mixing → stereo s16 at 32768 Hz, ~548 samples/frame. Must sound correct for Pokémon's m4a/Sappy driver.
- Interrupts, HALT/STOP, KEYINPUT/KEYCNT (keypad IRQ).
- Cartridge save: auto-detect via ROM string scan (SRAM_V, FLASH_V, FLASH512_V, FLASH1M_V, EEPROM_V) — Flash 64K/128K with bank switching and proper chip IDs (Pokémon uses 128K, Macronix 0xC2/0x09 or Sanyo 0x62/0x13), EEPROM 512B/8KB with size detection from DMA length, SRAM 32K. Dirty flag.
- GPIO RTC (Seiko S-3511) at 0x080000C4.. used by Pokémon Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald (and many hacks): date/time from host clock + offset. Enable for game codes AXV*, AXP*, BPE* and when ROM contains "SIIRTC_V".
- Save states: full serialize/deserialize of all state with a version header.
- Cheats: raw "AAAAAAAA:VV"/"AAAAAAAA:VVVV"/"AAAAAAAA:VVVVVVVV" writes applied each frame, plus CodeBreaker (unencrypted) and GameShark/Action Replay v3 (with decryption) if feasible — at least raw + CodeBreaker.
- Performance: target well above full speed on a mid-range arm64 phone — measure on host: at -O2, run a demanding ROM headless and report frames/second (aim > 600 fps on host x86).

Kotlin + JNI (exactly the API in REBUILD_PLAN.md):
- src/main/cpp/jni/retra_jni.cpp, src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt producing libretra_engine.so (C++17, -O2/-O3, no exceptions across JNI).
- src/main/kotlin/app/retra/engine/*.kt with GbaCore, GbaKey, SaveType, RomInfo, LoadResult.
- engine/build.gradle.kts is written by the coordinator; do not create Gradle files. JDK 21 may be installed at /usr/lib/jvm (check) — you can syntax-check the JNI bridge on host with g++ -fsyntax-only -I$JAVA_HOME/include -I$JAVA_HOME/include/linux.

Host harness (engine/host/): CMakeLists.txt building `retra-headless` that links the same core sources: `retra-headless rom.gba --frames N --out shot.png [--keys script] [--bench]` writes a PNG screenshot (write a tiny PNG/PPM encoder yourself; you can convert with ImageMagick `convert`, installed) and dumps audio to WAV optionally. Use the Read tool on PNG screenshots to visually verify output.

Testing (essential — do not claim success without evidence):
- Download freely-licensed test ROMs into /tmp (NOT into the repo): jsmolka/gba-tests (GitHub, has prebuilt .gba in releases or build with arm-none-eabi-gcc which is installed at /usr/bin/arm-none-eabi-gcc), armwrestler-gba-fixed, the mGBA test suite (mgba-emu/suite) if you can get a prebuilt ROM, Tonc demos (tonc examples), and other open-source homebrew. All jsmolka tests (arm, thumb, memory, bios, nes, save/flash/sram/eeprom, ppu) must pass. Verify PPU with tonc demos (affine, windows, blending, mosaic, bitmap modes) visually.
- An original game ROM may appear at /workspace/Retra/app/src/main/assets/games/mochi_hop.gba (being built in parallel); also test it if present.
- Never download or use commercial ROMs.
- Write engine/host/tests run script `engine/host/run_tests.sh` that builds and runs the available test ROMs and checks results (e.g. screenshot hash or pixel checks), and document results in engine/README.md (architecture, accuracy notes, known gaps, benchmark numbers).

Work incrementally: CPU first with jsmolka arm/thumb tests, then memory/bios, then PPU, timers/DMA, APU, saves, RTC, states, cheats, JNI. Keep files organized (cpu_arm.cpp, cpu_thumb.cpp, bus.cpp, ppu.cpp, apu.cpp, dma.cpp, timer.cpp, bios_hle.cpp, cart_save.cpp, rtc.cpp, state.cpp, cheats.cpp, gba.cpp/h as a facade). This is a long task; keep going until it is genuinely complete and tested. Final reply: concise summary of what works, test results (pass/fail per ROM), benchmark fps, known gaps, and file list.

Build an ORIGINAL, polished, cute Game Boy Advance homebrew game called "Mochi Hop" for the Android emulator app Retra. Read /workspace/Retra/docs/REBUILD_PLAN.md for context (repo layout, design direction, mascot). Your scope is ONLY /workspace/Retra/game/ plus writing the final ROM to /workspace/Retra/app/src/main/assets/games/mochi_hop.gba and a cover image to /workspace/Retra/app/src/main/assets/games/mochi_hop_cover.png (and a copy of the ROM to /workspace/Retra/catalog/games/mochi_hop.gba). Don't git commit; the coordinator does.

Concept: the player is Mochi — a round, squishy pink-and-cream rice-cake creature with a tiny leaf on top and big shiny eyes — hopping across pastel cloud islands collecting stars and little "sprout" friends. Cute 2D pixel art, soft pastel palette, smooth.
Requirements:
- Title screen (logo "Mochi Hop", animated Mochi, "Press START"), world/level select, at least 6 hand-designed levels across 2–3 themes (cloud meadow, candy caves, starry night), pause menu, level clear screen with star count, ending/credits screen ("Made for Retra").
- Mode 0 tiled backgrounds with parallax scrolling (2+ layers), hardware sprites with animation (idle squish, run, jump stretch, land squash), smooth physics with fixed-point math, coyote time + jump buffering, variable jump height, enemies (e.g. grumpy raindrops/bees) you can stomp, collectibles, checkpoints, simple particles.
- Sound: background music and SFX using the PSG channels (and/or Direct Sound), with an original tune you compose (small tracker/sequence data).
- Save progress (unlocked levels, best star counts) in SRAM (include the "SRAM_V113" string in the ROM so emulators detect it).
- Valid GBA header (title "MOCHIHOP", game code e.g. "AMHE"... pick a homebrew code like "RMHE", fixed header checksum, Nintendo logo bytes are required at 0x04 for real hardware; you may leave them zero since it targets emulators, but include them if you can generate them legitimately — otherwise zero is fine).
- All art must be original: author it as ASCII/indexed pixel art in source (e.g. Python script under game/tools/ that converts ASCII art or PNGs you generate into C arrays of 4bpp tiles/palettes/maps). No third-party assets.
- Toolchain: arm-none-eabi-gcc (installed at /usr/bin) with your own crt0/startup.S, linker script, and minimal headers (no devkitPro required). Provide game/build.sh that rebuilds everything deterministically, and game/README.md (controls, how to build, design notes).
- Keep ROM size modest (< 1 MiB ideally).

Testing: you must actually run the game. Install an emulator for testing only: `apt-get install -y mgba-sdl xvfb xdotool` (or mgba-qt), run under Xvfb, inject key presses with xdotool, capture screenshots with ImageMagick `import -window root shot.png`, and view them with the Read tool to verify the title screen, gameplay, sprites, scrolling and level clear actually render correctly. (A from-scratch emulator is also being written in parallel at /workspace/Retra/engine; if engine/host has a built `retra-headless` binary later, you may also try it, but don't depend on it.) Iterate on visuals until it genuinely looks cute and polished — apply good pixel-art practice (readable silhouettes, 1px dark outlines, limited palette, consistent light direction).

Also produce the cover image (e.g. 480x320 or 3:2 PNG, upscaled pixel art from a real in-game screenshot or a composed key art from your sprites) at app/src/main/assets/games/mochi_hop_cover.png.

Final reply: summary, controls, level list, ROM size and sha256, how you verified it (which screenshots), and any known issues.

Include short original descriptions (1–2 sentences, your own words), tags (e.g. "difficulty", "new region", "gen 1-8 mons", "roguelike", "complete"/"beta"), and a status. Collections: "Featured", "Pokémon fan games", "Hard mode / challenge", "Homebrew gems".

## Product
Retra is a GBA emulator app for Android, built for its author and community, focused on playing
Pokémon games, Pokémon fan games (ROM-hack patches) and homebrew. Everything is built from scratch:
UI/UX, logo, mascot, emulation engine, patcher, and an original bundled game.

Content rules (hard): never bundle or download commercial ROMs or Nintendo BIOS. Fan games are
distributed as patches (IPS/UPS/BPS) that the user applies to their own base ROM. Direct downloads
are allowed only for content whose license permits redistribution (homebrew, our own game).

## Repository layout
```
settings.gradle.kts / build.gradle.kts / gradle/libs.versions.toml / gradlew
app/        Android app, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, package app.retra
engine/     Android library :engine, namespace app.retra.engine
  src/main/cpp/core/     pure C++17 GBA core, no Android/JNI includes
  src/main/cpp/jni/      JNI bridge (retra_jni.cpp)
  src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt  -> shared lib "retra_engine"
  src/main/kotlin/app/retra/engine/   Kotlin API (GbaCore, GbaKey, ...)
  host/      CMake host build: retra-headless runner + tests (Linux, g++)
patcher/    Kotlin/JVM library :patcher, package app.retra.patcher (IPS/UPS/BPS, CRC32)
game/       Original GBA game "Mochi Hop" (C, arm-none-eabi-gcc), build.sh
            output ROM -> app/src/main/assets/games/mochi_hop.gba
catalog/    manifest.json — online Game Library, fetched from
            https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prashantchataut/Retra/main/catalog/manifest.json
docs/
```

## Engine Kotlin API (package app.retra.engine) — the app codes against exactly this
```kotlin
object GbaKey { const val A=1; B=2; SELECT=4; START=8; RIGHT=16; LEFT=32; UP=64; DOWN=128; R=256; L=512 }

enum class SaveType { NONE, SRAM, FLASH_64K, FLASH_128K, EEPROM_512, EEPROM_8K, AUTO }

data class RomInfo(val title: String, val gameCode: String, val makerCode: String,
                   val version: Int, val saveType: SaveType, val hasRtc: Boolean)

sealed interface LoadResult { data class Ok(val info: RomInfo): LoadResult; data class Error(val message: String): LoadResult }

class GbaCore : AutoCloseable {           // NOT thread-safe: call from one emulation thread
  companion object { const val WIDTH = 240; const val HEIGHT = 160; const val SAMPLE_RATE = 32768
                     const val FRAME_RATE = 59.7275 ; const val MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES = 2048 }
  fun loadRom(rom: ByteArray, bios: ByteArray? = null): LoadResult   // bios null -> built-in replacement/HLE BIOS
  fun reset()
  fun setKeys(mask: Int)                       // GbaKey bits, 1 = pressed
  fun runFrame(video: IntArray, audio: ShortArray): Int
      // video: 240*160 ARGB_8888 (0xFFRRGGBB) ; audio: interleaved stereo s16, size >= 2*MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES
      // returns number of stereo frames written
  fun batterySave(): ByteArray?                // null when SaveType.NONE
  fun loadBatterySave(data: ByteArray): Boolean
  fun consumeSaveDirty(): Boolean              // true once after the game wrote to its save memory
  fun saveState(): ByteArray
  fun loadState(state: ByteArray): Boolean
  fun setCheats(codes: List<String>): Int      // returns number of accepted codes (raw "AAAAAAAA:VV" + GameShark/CodeBreaker/AR where supported)
  fun setColorCorrection(enabled: Boolean)     // GBA LCD gamma/colour correction
  fun setRtcOffsetSeconds(offset: Long)
  override fun close()
}
```

## Design direction (app)
- Tone: Playful-soft, cute 2D, with a liquid-glass material. Signature: the mascot **Mochi**
  (a round, squishy rice-cake creature) + glossy liquid-glass surfaces with a specular rim and a
  floating glass dock whose indicator morphs like liquid.
- Type: Fredoka (display, rounded) + Nunito (body). Both OFL, bundled.
- Palette: neutrals tinted warm (light "cloud cream") / cool indigo (dark "night"), one accent
  "Mochi pink" plus semantic colours. Pastel ambient sky behind glass.
- Motion: spring-based, restrained (no bounce on everything), respects reduced motion.
- The original game **Mochi Hop** stars the same mascot.

def vlq_ups(b,i):

def blob(w, h, cx, cy, a, bt, bb, p=2.4):
    def inside(x, y):
        dx = (x + 0.5 - cx) / a
        yy = y + 0.5 - cy
        dy = yy / (bt if yy < 0 else bb)
        return abs(dx) ** p + abs(dy) ** p <= 1.0, dx, dy
    return inside

def mochi_frame(face="open", body_dy=0, feet=None, sx=1.0, sy=1.0, mouth="smile"):
    L = Layer(32, 32)
    cx = 16.0
    bottom = 30 - body_dy
    a = 10.0 * sx
    bt = 9.0 * sy
    bb = 6.0 * sy
    cy = bottom - bb
    inside = blob(32, 32, cx, cy, a, bt, bb)
    body = Layer(32, 32)

    def col(x, y):
        ok, dx, dy = inside(x, y)
        if not ok:
            return None
        r = abs(dx) ** 2.4 + abs(dy) ** 2.4
        # highlight oval top-left
        hx = (x + 0.5 - (cx - 4.5)) / 2.6
        hy = (y + 0.5 - (cy - 5.0)) / 1.6
        if hx * hx + hy * hy <= 1.0:
            return 5
        lx = (x + 0.5 - (cx - 3.5)) / 5.5
        ly = (y + 0.5 - (cy - 4.0)) / 3.2
        if lx * lx + ly * ly <= 1.0:
            return 4
        if dy > 0.45 and r > 0.45:
            return 2
        if dx > 0.72 and dy > -0.2:
            return 2
        return 3
    body.fill_fn(col)
    # feet (drawn before outline so they share it)
    if feet:
        for fx, fy in feet:
            for yy in range(2):
                for xx in range(4):
                    if yy == 1 and xx in (0, 3):
                        continue
                    body.set(int(cx) + fx + xx, bottom + fy + yy, 13)
    body.outline(1)
    L.paste(body)
    # leaf stem sits on top of the head
    top = int(cy - bt)
    L.stamp(LEAF, int(cx) - 2, top - 5, {"g": 9, "G": 10, "L": 11})
    # face
    ey = int(cy) - 2
    if face == "up":
        ey -= 1
    art = EYES[face]
    leg = {"e": 7, "W": 8}
    L.stamp(art, int(cx) - 6, ey, leg)
    L.stamp(art, int(cx) + 3, ey, leg, flip=(face == "hurt"))
    # blush
    by = ey + 4
    for bx in (int(cx) - 8, int(cx) - 7, int(cx) + 6, int(cx) + 7):
        L.set(bx, by, 6)
    # mouth
    my = ey + 4
    mx = int(cx) - 1
    if mouth == "smile":
        L.set(mx - 1, my, 12)
        L.set(mx, my + 1, 12)
        L.set(mx + 1, my + 1, 12)
        L.set(mx + 2, my, 12)
    elif mouth == "open":
        L.set(mx, my, 12)
        L.set(mx + 1, my, 12)
        L.set(mx, my + 1, 12)
        L.set(mx + 1, my + 1, 12)
    elif mouth == "o":
        L.set(mx, my + 1, 12)
        L.set(mx + 1, my + 1, 12)
    return L

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- star
def star_poly(cx, cy, ro, ri, xs=1.0, rot=-math.pi / 2):
    pts = []
    for i in range(10):
        r = ro if i % 2 == 0 else ri
        a = rot + i * math.pi / 5
        pts.append((cx + math.cos(a) * r * xs, cy + math.sin(a) * r))
    return pts


def in_poly(x, y, pts):
    ins = False
    j = len(pts) - 1
    for i in range(len(pts)):
        xi, yi = pts[i]
        xj, yj = pts[j]
        if ((yi > y) != (yj > y)) and (x < (xj - xi) * (y - yi) / (yj - yi + 1e-9) + xi):
            ins = not ins
        j = i
    return ins


def star_frame(xs, face=True, size=16, ro=7.6, ri=3.6):
    L = Layer(size, size)
    c = size / 2
    pts = star_poly(c, c + 0.6, ro, ri, xs)
    inner = star_poly(c, c + 0.6, ro - 2.2, ri - 1.0, xs)
    body = Layer(size, size)

    def col(x, y):
        px, py = x + 0.5, y + 0.5
        if not in_poly(px, py, pts):
            return None
        if in_poly(px, py, inner):
            # light from top-left
            if (px - c) * xs + (py - c) < -2.5:
                return 4
            return 3
        if (px - c) + (py - c) > 0:
            return 2
        return 3
    body.fill_fn(col)
    body.outline(1)
    L.paste(body)
    if face and xs > 0.6:
        ex = int(c - 2 * xs)
        L.set(ex, int(c) + 1, 6)
        L.set(ex, int(c) + 2, 6)
        L.set(int(c + 1.6 * xs), int(c) + 1, 6)
        L.set(int(c + 1.6 * xs), int(c) + 2, 6)
        L.set(ex - 1, int(c) + 3, 7)
        L.set(int(c + 1.6 * xs) + 1, int(c) + 3, 7)
    return L


def star_frames():
    return [star_frame(1.0), star_frame(0.72), star_frame(0.4, face=False), star_frame(0.72).hflip()]

def drop_frame(sq=0, flat=False):
    L = Layer(16, 16)
    body = Layer(16, 16)
    if flat:
        def col(x, y):
            dx = (x + 0.5 - 8) / 7.0
            dy = (y + 0.5 - 13.5) / 2.2
            if dx * dx + dy * dy <= 1:
                return 4 if dy < -0.3 and dx < 0 else (2 if dy > 0.3 else 3)
            return None
        body.fill_fn(col)
        body.outline(1)
        L.paste(body)
        L.set(5, 13, 6); L.set(6, 13, 6); L.set(9, 13, 6); L.set(10, 13, 6)
        return L
    r = 5.6 + sq * 0.5
    cy = 9.5 + sq * 0.5
    top = 2.0 + sq

    def col(x, y):
        px, py = x + 0.5, y + 0.5
        dx = (px - 8) / (r)
        dy = (py - cy) / (r - sq * 0.8)
        ins = dx * dx + dy * dy <= 1
        if not ins and py < cy and py >= top:
            # cone to the tip
            t = (cy - py) / (cy - top)
            half = r * (1 - t) ** 1.3
            ins = abs(px - 8) <= half
        if not ins:
            return None
        hx = (px - 6) / 1.8
        hy = (py - (cy - 2)) / 2.4
        if hx * hx + hy * hy <= 1:
            return 4
        if dx > 0.3 and dy > 0.1 or dy > 0.7:
            return 2
        return 3
    body.fill_fn(col)
    body.outline(1)
    L.paste(body)
    ey = int(cy) + 0
    # grumpy brows + eyes
    L.set(5, ey - 1, 6); L.set(6, ey, 6)
    L.set(10, ey - 1, 6); L.set(9, ey, 6)
    L.set(6, ey + 1, 6); L.set(6, ey + 2, 6)
    L.set(9, ey + 1, 6); L.set(9, ey + 2, 6)
    L.set(7, ey + 3 + sq // 2, 6); L.set(8, ey + 3 + sq // 2, 6)
    L.set(4, ey + 3, 7); L.set(11, ey + 3, 7)
    return L

def spiky_frame(ph):
    L = Layer(16, 16)
    body = Layer(16, 16)
    cx, cy = 8.0, 9.0

    def col(x, y):
        px, py = x + 0.5, y + 0.5
        dx, dy = px - cx, py - cy
        d = math.hypot(dx, dy)
        ang = math.atan2(dy, dx) + ph * math.pi / 8
        spike = 1.9 * max(0.0, math.cos(ang * 4)) ** 3
        if d > 4.9 + spike:
            return None
        if d > 4.9:
            return 4 if dy < 0 else 3
        if dx + dy < -3:
            return 4
        if dx + dy > 2.5:
            return 2
        return 3
    body.fill_fn(col)
    body.outline(1)
    L.paste(body)
    L.set(6, 8, 6); L.set(6, 9, 6); L.set(10, 8, 6); L.set(10, 9, 6)
    L.set(5, 7, 6); L.set(11, 7, 6)
    L.set(7, 11, 6); L.set(8, 11, 6); L.set(9, 11, 6)
    L.set(4, 10, 7); L.set(12, 10, 7)

def flag_frame(state):
    """16x32 checkpoint flag. state 0 = inactive, 1/2 = waving."""
    L = Layer(16, 32)
    pole = Layer(16, 32)
    for y in range(4, 31):
        pole.set(3, y, 3)
        pole.set(4, y, 2)
    # knob
    for (x, y) in [(3, 2), (4, 2), (2, 3), (3, 3), (4, 3), (5, 3)]:
        pole.set(x, y, 12)
    pole.set(3, 2, 15) if state else None
    # base
    for y in (29, 30):
        for x in range(0, 9):
            pole.set(x, y, 3 if y == 29 else 2)
    pole.outline(1)
    L.paste(pole)
    fl = Layer(16, 32)
    if state == 0:
        def col(x, y):
            if 5 <= x <= 8 and 5 <= y <= 4 + (x - 3) * 3 and y <= 16:
                return 8 if x < 7 else 7
            return None
    else:
        ph = 0 if state == 1 else 1

        def col(x, y):
            if x < 5 or x > 14:
                return None
            off = int(round(math.sin((x - 5) * 0.7 + ph * 2.4) * 1.2))
            t0 = 5 + off
            t1 = 13 - (x - 5) * 0.35 + off
            if t0 <= y <= t1:
                if y == t0:
                    return 6
                return 5 if (x + y) % 5 else 4
            return None
    fl.fill_fn(col)
    fl.outline(1)
    L.paste(fl)
    if state:

        for x, y in [(8, 8), (10, 8), (8, 9), (9, 9), (10, 9), (9, 10)]:

    def S(x, y):
        if x < 0:

            d = 0
            while d < 12 and S(x, y - d - 1):
                d += 1
            # d = number of solid pixels above (0 = right under the outline)
            lx = x % 16
            scallop = [0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 2, 1][lx % 8]

                            if 6 <= x <= 9 and 6 <= y <= 9 and not ((x in (6, 9)) and (y in (6, 9))):

    x = 4
    for i, ch in enumerate(word1 + " " + word2):
        if ch == " ":
            x += 8
            continue
        letters.append((ch, x, 10 + (3 if i % 2 else 0), i >= 6))
        x += 6 * S + 4
    shape = Layer(W, H)
    for ch, ox, oy, hop in letters:
        rows = g[ch]
        # scale 3x with rounded smoothing
        for y in range(6 * S):
            for x in range(5 * S):
                gx, gy = x // S, y // S
                on = rows[gy][gx] == "#"
                if not on:
                    # fill inner concave corners to round shapes
                    fx, fy = x % S, y % S
                    nb = 0
                    for dx, dy in ((-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)):
                        xx, yy = gx + dx, gy + dy
                        if 0 <= yy < 6 and 0 <= xx < 5 and rows[yy][xx] == "#":
                            nb += 1
                    if nb >= 2:
                        lft = gx > 0 and rows[gy][gx - 1] == "#"
                        rgt = gx < 4 and rows[gy][gx + 1] == "#"
                        up = gy > 0 and rows[gy - 1][gx] == "#"
                        dn = gy < 5 and rows[gy + 1][gx] == "#"
                        if (lft and up and fx == 0 and fy == 0) or (rgt and up and fx == S - 1 and fy == 0) or \
                           (lft and dn and fx == 0 and fy == S - 1) or (rgt and dn and fx == S - 1 and fy == S - 1):
                            on = True
                if on:
                    shape.set(ox + x, oy + y, 20 if hop else 10)
    # thicken by 1px (bubbly)
    th = shape.copy()
    for y in range(H):
        for x in range(W):
            if not shape.get(x, y):
                for dx, dy in ((1, 0), (0, 1), (-1, 0), (0, -1)):
                    v = shape.get(x + dx, y + dy)
                    if v:
                        th.set(x, y, v)
                        break
    # colour: gradient + highlight; HOP in mint green
    for y in range(H):
        for x in range(W):
            v = th.get(x, y)
            if not v:
                continue
            hop = v == 20
            above = th.get(x, y - 1)
            above2 = th.get(x, y - 2)
            below = th.get(x, y + 1)
            if not above:
                c = 5
            elif not above2:
                c = 4 if not hop else 9
            elif not below or not th.get(x, y + 2):
                c = 2 if not hop else 7
            else:
                c = 3 if not hop else 8
            L.set(x, y, c)
    # thick outline (2px) + drop shadow
    L.outline(1)
    L.outline(15, diag=True)
    sh = Layer(W, H)
    for y in range(H):
        for x in range(W):
            if L.get(x, y) and not L.get(x, y + 2):
                sh.set(x, y + 2, 13)
    for y in range(H):
        for x in range(W):
            if not L.get(x, y) and sh.get(x, y):
                L.set(x, y, 13)
    # sparkle stars around
    for sx, sy in ((2, 4), (226, 48), (150, 2)):
        for d in range(-2, 3):
            L.set(sx + d, sy + 2, 12 if abs(d) < 2 else 11)
            L.set(sx + 2, sy + 2 + d, 12 if abs(d) < 2 else 11)
    return L

"""Hand-designed levels for Mochi Hop.

Grid cells (16x16 metatiles):  '.' air  '#' ground  'B' block  '=' one-way cloud
                                '^' spikes  'f' 't' 'm' decorations (non-solid)
Objects: P start, o star, S sprout, r raindrop, b bee, k spiky, C checkpoint, G goal, J spring

Physics reference: a full jump clears ~3 tiles up and ~5 tiles across; springs launch ~8 tiles.
"""

OBJ_TYPES = {"o": 1, "S": 2, "r": 3, "b": 4, "k": 5, "C": 6, "G": 7, "J": 8}


class Lvl:
    def __init__(self, name, theme, w, h):
        self.name = name
        self.theme = theme
        self.w = w
        self.h = h
        self.g = [["."] * w for _ in range(h)]
        self.objs = []
        self.start = (2, h - 3)

    def ground(self, x0, x1, top, bottom=None):
        bottom = self.h - 1 if bottom is None else bottom
        for x in range(x0, x1 + 1):
            for y in range(top, bottom + 1):
                self.g[y][x] = "#"
        return self

    def clear(self, x0, x1, y0, y1):
        for x in range(x0, x1 + 1):
            for y in range(y0, y1 + 1):
                self.g[y][x] = "."
        return self

    def blocks(self, x, y, n=1, vertical=False):
        for i in range(n):
            if vertical:
                self.g[y + i][x] = "B"
            else:
                self.g[y][x + i] = "B"
        return self

    def plat(self, x, y, n):
        for i in range(n):
            self.g[y][x + i] = "="
        return self

    def spikes(self, x, y, n=1):
        for i in range(n):
            self.g[y][x + i] = "^"
        return self

    def deco(self, x, y, ch):
        if self.g[y][x] == ".":
            self.g[y][x] = ch
        return self

    def put(self, x, y, ch):
        if ch == "P":
            self.start = (x, y)
        else:
            self.objs.append((OBJ_TYPES[ch], x, y))
        return self

    def stars(self, x, y, n=1, dx=1, dy=0):
        for i in range(n):
            self.put(x + i * dx, y + i * dy, "o")
        return self

    def arc(self, x, y, n):
        """Arc of stars over a gap starting at (x, y)."""
        hts = {3: [0, -1, 0], 4: [0, -1, -1, 0], 5: [0, -1, -2, -1, 0], 6: [0, -1, -2, -2, -1, 0]}[n]
        for i, h in enumerate(hts):
            self.put(x + i, y + h, "o")
        return self

    def rows(self):
        out = [r[:] for r in self.g]
        for t, x, y in self.objs:
            ch = [k for k, v in OBJ_TYPES.items() if v == t][0]
            out[y][x] = ch
        sx, sy = self.start
        out[sy][sx] = "P"
        return ["".join(r) for r in out]

    def grid(self):
        return ["".join(r) for r in self.g]

    def check(self):
        for t, x, y in self.objs:
            assert 0 <= x < self.w and 0 <= y < self.h, (self.name, t, x, y)
            assert self.g[y][x] in ".ftm", (self.name, "object inside solid", t, x, y, self.g[y][x])
        assert sum(1 for t, _, _ in self.objs if t == 7) == 1, self.name
        assert sum(1 for t, _, _ in self.objs if t == 2) == 3, (self.name, "needs 3 sprouts")

"""Original music for Mochi Hop, written as melody + chord progressions.

The harmony (arpeggios), bass line and drums are generated from the chord
symbols so that every channel stays in sync. Output: per-channel byte streams
for the tiny PSG sequencer in src/audio.c.

Stream format (pairs):  note(1..127 MIDI) dur | 0 dur (rest) | 0xF0 env | 0xF1 duty
                        0xFE end | 0xFF loop
Drums channel: 1 kick, 2 snare, 3 hat, 0 rest.
"""

NOTE = {"C": 0, "C#": 1, "Db": 1, "D": 2, "D#": 3, "Eb": 3, "E": 4, "F": 5, "F#": 6, "Gb": 6,
        "G": 7, "G#": 8, "Ab": 8, "A": 9, "A#": 10, "Bb": 10, "B": 11}


def midi(n):
    name = n[:-1]
    octv = int(n[-1])
    return 12 * (octv + 1) + NOTE[name]


def parse(seq):
    out = []
    for tok in seq.split():
        n, d = tok.split(":")
        d = int(d)
        out.append((0 if n == "r" else midi(n), d))
    return out


CHORDS = {
    "C": ("C", [0, 4, 7]), "Dm": ("D", [0, 3, 7]), "Em": ("E", [0, 3, 7]), "F": ("F", [0, 4, 7]),
    "G": ("G", [0, 4, 7]), "Am": ("A", [0, 3, 7]), "Bb": ("Bb", [0, 4, 7]), "A": ("A", [0, 4, 7]),
    "Gm": ("G", [0, 3, 7]),
}


def chord_notes(sym, octv):
    root, iv = CHORDS[sym]
    r = 12 * (octv + 1) + NOTE[root]
    return [r + i for i in iv]


def bars_of(prog, bar):
    """prog: list of bars; each bar is 'F' or 'Bb C' (two halves)."""
    out = []
    for b in prog:
        parts = b.split()
        each = bar // len(parts)
        for p in parts:
            out.append((p, each))
    return out


def gen_arp(prog, bar, step=2, octv=4, pattern=(0, 1, 2, 1)):
    ev = []
    for sym, ln in bars_of(prog, bar):
        ns = chord_notes(sym, octv)
        if ns[0] < midi("F4") - 0:
            pass
        t = 0
        i = 0
        while t < ln:
            ev.append((ns[pattern[i % len(pattern)]], min(step, ln - t)))
            t += step
            i += 1
    return ev


def gen_bass(prog, bar, style="bounce"):
    ev = []
    for sym, ln in bars_of(prog, bar):
        root = chord_notes(sym, 2)[0]
        fifth = root + 7
        if style == "bounce":
            if ln == 16:
                ev += [(root, 3), (0, 1), (root + 12, 2), (root, 2), (fifth, 3), (0, 1), (root + 12, 2), (fifth, 2)]
            else:
                ev += [(root, 3), (0, 1), (root + 12, 2), (fifth, 2)][:4] if ln == 8 else [(root, ln)]
        elif style == "waltz":
            ev += [(root, 4), (fifth, 4), (root + 12, 4)] if ln == 12 else [(root, ln)]
        elif style == "walk":
            if ln == 16:
                ev += [(root, 2), (0, 2), (root, 2), (root + 12, 2), (fifth, 2), (0, 2), (fifth, 2), (root + 10, 2)]
            else:
                ev += [(root, 2), (0, 2), (fifth, 2), (root + 12, 2)]
    return ev


def gen_drums(nbars, bar, style="pop"):
    ev = []
    for b in range(nbars):
        if style == "pop":
            pat = [(1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 2), (3, 2), (2, 2), (3, 2), (3, 1), (3, 1), (3, 2)] if b % 4 != 3 else \
                  [(1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 2), (1, 2), (2, 2), (3, 2), (2, 2), (2, 2)]
        elif style == "light":
            pat = [(1, 4), (3, 4), (3, 4)] if bar == 12 else [(1, 4), (3, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4)]
        elif style == "bouncy":
            pat = [(1, 2), (0, 2), (3, 2), (1, 2), (2, 2), (0, 2), (3, 2), (3, 2)]
        ev += pat
        assert sum(d for _, d in pat) == bar, (style, bar)
    return ev


def total(ev):
    return sum(d for _, d in ev)


def encode(ev, env=None, duty=None, loop=True):
    out = []
    if env is not None:
        out += [0xF0, env]
    if duty is not None:
        out += [0xF1, duty]
    for n, d in ev:
        while d > 0:
            dd = min(d, 255)
            out += [n, dd]
            d -= dd
            n = 0 if n else 0  # long notes are split into note + rest tail (rare)
    out.append(0xFF if loop else 0xFE)
    return out


def song(name, tempo, bar, lead, prog, bass_style, drum_style, lead_env=0xA3, harm_env=0x52,
         lead_duty=1, harm_duty=2, arp_pattern=(0, 1, 2, 1), arp_oct=4, loop=True):
    lead_ev = parse(lead)
    nb = len(prog)
    assert total(lead_ev) == nb * bar, (name, total(lead_ev), nb * bar)
    harm = gen_arp(prog, bar, 2, arp_oct, arp_pattern)
    bass = gen_bass(prog, bar, bass_style)
    drums = gen_drums(nb, bar, drum_style)
    for ev in (harm, bass, drums):
        assert total(ev) == nb * bar, (name, total(ev))
    return {
        "name": name, "tempo": tempo,
        "ch": [encode(harm, harm_env, harm_duty, loop), encode(lead_ev, lead_env, lead_duty, loop),
               encode(bass, loop=loop), encode(drums, loop=loop)],
    }


TITLE = song(
    "title", 6, 16,
    # A
    "C5:2 F5:2 A5:2 G5:2 F5:4 C5:4 "
    "D5:2 F5:2 A5:2 C6:2 A5:4 F5:4 "
    "D5:2 F5:2 Bb5:2 A5:2 G5:4 F5:2 G5:2 "
    "E5:4 G5:4 C5:4 r:4 "

    "Bb5:2 A5:2 G5:2 F5:2 E5:2 G5:2 C6:4 "

    # B

    "A5:2 G5:2 E5:2 C5:2 E5:4 A5:4 "
    "F5:2 E5:2 D5:4 A4:4 D5:4 "
    "D5:2 F5:2 Bb5:2 D6:2 C6:4 Bb5:4 "
    "A5:2 G5:2 E5:2 G5:2 C6:8 "
    "A5:4 F5:2 C6:2 A5:4 F5:4 "
    "G5:2 A5:2 G5:2 E5:2 C5:8",
    ["F", "Dm", "Bb", "C", "F", "Dm", "Bb C", "F",
     "Bb", "C", "Am", "Dm", "Bb", "C", "F", "C"],
    "bounce", "pop")

MEADOW = song(
    "meadow", 6, 16,
    "E5:2 G5:2 C6:2 G5:2 E5:2 G5:2 A5:4 "
    "A5:2 C6:2 E6:4 D6:2 C6:2 A5:4 "
    "F5:2 A5:2 C6:2 A5:2 G5:2 F5:2 E5:4 "
    "D5:2 E5:2 G5:4 B5:4 G5:4 "
    "E5:2 G5:2 C6:2 G5:2 E6:4 D6:4 "
    "C6:2 B5:2 A5:2 G5:2 E5:4 A5:4 "

    "C6:6 G5:2 C6:8 "

CAVES = song(

    "D5:2 r:1 D5:1 F5:2 A5:2 G5:2 F5:2 E5:2 F5:2 "
    "E5:2 r:1 E5:1 G5:2 C6:2 Bb5:2 A5:2 G5:4 "

NIGHT = song(

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generates build/gen/assets.c + assets.h for Mochi Hop from the original art,
level and music definitions in this directory. Deterministic output."""
import math
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from pix import Layer, TileBank, rgb555, sprite_tiles, tile_bytes  # noqa: E402
import art_sprites as SP  # noqa: E402
import art_bg as BG  # noqa: E402
import levels as LV  # noqa: E402
import music as MU  # noqa: E402

OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "build", "gen")
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

C = []
H = []


def carr(ctype, name, data, per=16, fmt="0x%02X"):
    C.append("const %s %s[%d] __attribute__((aligned(4))) = {" % (ctype, name, len(data)))
    for i in range(0, len(data), per):
        C.append("  " + ",".join(fmt % v for v in data[i:i + per]) + ",")
    C.append("};")
    H.append("extern const %s %s[%d];" % (ctype, name, len(data)))


def u16s(b):
    return [b[i] | (b[i + 1] << 8) for i in range(0, len(b), 2)]


def pal_u16(p):
    return [rgb555(c) for c in p]


def define(name, val):
    H.append("#define %s %d" % (name, val))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ sprites
obj = bytearray()


def add_sprites(name, frames):
    start = len(obj) // 32
    for f in frames:
        obj.extend(sprite_tiles(f))
    define("SPR_" + name, start)
    return start


add_sprites("MOCHI", SP.mochi_frames())
add_sprites("STAR", SP.star_frames())
add_sprites("DROP", [SP.drop_frame(0), SP.drop_frame(1), SP.drop_frame(flat=True)])
add_sprites("BEE", [SP.bee_frame(0), SP.bee_frame(1)])
add_sprites("SPIKY", [SP.spiky_frame(0), SP.spiky_frame(1)])
add_sprites("SPROUT", [SP.sprout_frame(0), SP.sprout_frame(1)])
add_sprites("FLAG", [SP.flag_frame(i) for i in range(3)])
add_sprites("GOAL", [SP.goal_frame(0), SP.goal_frame(1)])
add_sprites("SPRING", [SP.spring_frame(0), SP.spring_frame(1)])
add_sprites("NODE", [SP.node_frame(i) for i in range(4)])
add_sprites("FX", SP.fx_frames())
assert len(obj) <= 32768
carr("unsigned short", "obj_tiles", u16s(obj), 16, "0x%04X")
carr("unsigned short", "obj_pals", sum((pal_u16(p) for p in SP.SPRITE_PALETTES), []), 16, "0x%04X")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ UI / font (CBB2, tiles 0..)
ui, uidx = BG.ui_tiles()
assert len(ui) <= 128, len(ui)
uib = bytearray()
for t in ui:
    uib.extend(tile_bytes(t, 0, 0))
carr("unsigned short", "ui_tiles", u16s(uib), 16, "0x%04X")
carr("unsigned short", "ui_pal", pal_u16(BG.PAL_UI), 16, "0x%04X")
fmap = [0] * 128
for ch in BG.FONT_CHARS:
    fmap[ord(ch)] = BG.FONT_CHARS.index(ch)
for ch in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz":
    fmap[ord(ch)] = BG.FONT_CHARS.index(ch.upper())
carr("unsigned char", "font_map", fmap)
define("UI_HUDFONT", uidx["h "])
define("UI_PANFONT", uidx["p "])
for k, v in uidx.items():
    if k.startswith("panel") or k[0] in "ij" or k == "solid":
        define("UI_" + k.upper(), v)
MID_BASE = 128
define("MID_TILE_BASE", MID_BASE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ themes
theme_info = []
for t in range(3):
    far, fpal = BG.far_layer(t)
    fb = TileBank(0)
    fw, fh, fmapents = fb.map_layer(far, 4)
    assert (fw, fh) == (32, 32)
    assert len(fb.tiles) <= 512, ("far", t, len(fb.tiles))
    mid, mpal = BG.mid_layer(t)
    mb = TileBank(MID_BASE)
    mw, mh, mmap = mb.map_layer(mid, 5)
    assert (mw, mh) == (64, 32)
    assert len(mb.tiles) + MID_BASE <= 512, ("mid", t, len(mb.tiles))
    carr("unsigned short", "far_tiles_%d" % t, u16s(fb.data()), 16, "0x%04X")
    carr("unsigned short", "far_map_%d" % t, fmapents, 32, "0x%04X")
    carr("unsigned short", "far_pal_%d" % t, pal_u16(fpal), 16, "0x%04X")
    carr("unsigned short", "mid_tiles_%d" % t, u16s(mb.data()), 16, "0x%04X")
    carr("unsigned short", "mid_map_%d" % t, mmap, 32, "0x%04X")
    carr("unsigned short", "mid_pal_%d" % t, pal_u16(mpal), 16, "0x%04X")
    carr("unsigned short", "terrain_pal_%d" % t, pal_u16(BG.THEME_TERRAIN_PALS[t]), 16, "0x%04X")
    theme_info.append((len(fb.tiles), len(mb.tiles)))
    print("theme", t, "far tiles", len(fb.tiles), "mid tiles", len(mb.tiles))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ levels
levels = LV.all_levels()
terrain_banks = [TileBank(0) for _ in range(3)]
level_meta = []
COLL = {".": 0, "f": 0, "t": 0, "m": 0, "#": 1, "B": 1, "=": 2, "^": 3}
for i, L in enumerate(levels):
    grid = L.grid()
    lay = BG.render_terrain(grid, L.theme)
    tb = terrain_banks[L.theme]
    tw, th, ents = tb.map_layer(lay, 0)
    # column-major, 32 rows per column (pad with 0)
    col = []
    for x in range(tw):
        for y in range(32):
            col.append(ents[y * tw + x] if y < th else 0)
    carr("unsigned short", "lvl_map_%d" % i, col, 32, "0x%04X")
    coll = [COLL[grid[y][x]] for y in range(L.h) for x in range(L.w)]
    carr("unsigned char", "lvl_coll_%d" % i, coll, 64)
    objs = []
    # objects sorted by x for nicer culling
    for t, x, y in sorted(L.objs, key=lambda o: (o[1], o[2])):
        objs += [t, x, y, 0]
    carr("unsigned char", "lvl_objs_%d" % i, objs, 32)
    nstars = sum(1 for t, _, _ in L.objs if t == 1)
    level_meta.append((L.name, L.theme, L.w, L.h, L.start[0], L.start[1], len(L.objs), nstars))
for t, tb in enumerate(terrain_banks):
    assert len(tb.tiles) <= 512, ("terrain", t, len(tb.tiles))
    carr("unsigned short", "terrain_tiles_%d" % t, u16s(tb.data()), 16, "0x%04X")
    print("theme", t, "terrain tiles", len(tb.tiles))

H.append("typedef struct { const char* name; unsigned char theme, w, h, sx, sy, nobjs, nstars;"
         " const unsigned short* map; const unsigned char* coll; const unsigned char* objs; } LevelDef;")
H.append("extern const LevelDef level_defs[%d];" % len(levels))
define("NUM_LEVELS", len(levels))
C.append("const LevelDef level_defs[%d] = {" % len(levels))
for i, m in enumerate(level_meta):
    C.append('  {"%s", %d, %d, %d, %d, %d, %d, %d, lvl_map_%d, lvl_coll_%d, lvl_objs_%d},' % (m + (i, i, i)))
C.append("};")

H.append("typedef struct { const unsigned short *far_tiles, *far_map, *far_pal, *mid_tiles, *mid_map, *mid_pal,"
         " *terrain_tiles, *terrain_pal; unsigned short far_n, mid_n, terrain_n; } ThemeDef;")
H.append("extern const ThemeDef theme_defs[3];")
C.append("const ThemeDef theme_defs[3] = {")
for t in range(3):
    C.append("  {far_tiles_%d, far_map_%d, far_pal_%d, mid_tiles_%d, mid_map_%d, mid_pal_%d, terrain_tiles_%d,"
             " terrain_pal_%d, %d, %d, %d}," % ((t,) * 8 + (theme_info[t][0], theme_info[t][1],
                                                         len(terrain_banks[t].tiles))))
C.append("};")
H.append("extern const char* const theme_names[3];")
C.append("const char* const theme_names[3] = {%s};" % ",".join('"%s"' % n for n in BG.THEME_NAMES))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ title screen BG1 (logo + island)
title = TileBank(0)
logo = BG.logo_layer()
logo_pad = Layer(240, 56)
logo_pad.paste(logo, 4, 0)
lw, lh, lmap = title.map_layer(logo_pad, 2)
title_grid = [
    "...............",
    "...............",
    "....=====......",
    "..t.......f.m..",
    "...############",
    "..#############",
]
# island at the bottom: 15 metatiles wide, rendered with the meadow terrain style
isl = BG.render_terrain(title_grid, 0)
iw, ih, imap = title.map_layer(isl, 0)
tmap = [0] * (32 * 32)
for y in range(lh):
    for x in range(lw):
        tmap[(y + 2) * 32 + x] = lmap[y * lw + x]
for y in range(ih):
    for x in range(iw):
        ty = 20 - ih + y
        if 0 <= ty < 32:
            tmap[ty * 32 + x] = imap[y * iw + x]
assert len(title.tiles) <= 512, len(title.tiles)
print("title tiles", len(title.tiles))
carr("unsigned short", "title_tiles", u16s(title.data()), 16, "0x%04X")
carr("unsigned short", "title_map", tmap, 32, "0x%04X")
carr("unsigned short", "logo_pal", pal_u16(BG.LOGO_PAL), 16, "0x%04X")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ misc tables
sin = [int(round(math.sin(i * 2 * math.pi / 256) * 256)) for i in range(256)]
carr("short", "sin_lut", sin, 16, "%d")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ music
carr("unsigned short", "sq_rate", [MU.square_rate(m) for m in range(128)], 16, "%d")
carr("unsigned short", "wave_rate", [MU.wave_rate(m) for m in range(128)], 16, "%d")
H.append("typedef struct { const unsigned char* ch[4]; unsigned char tempo; } SongDef;")
for s in MU.SONGS:
    for c in range(4):
        carr("unsigned char", "song_%s_%d" % (s["name"], c), s["ch"][c], 32)
H.append("extern const SongDef song_defs[%d];" % len(MU.SONGS))
C.append("const SongDef song_defs[%d] = {" % len(MU.SONGS))
for s in MU.SONGS:
    n = s["name"]
    C.append("  {{song_%s_0, song_%s_1, song_%s_2, song_%s_3}, %d}," % (n, n, n, n, s["tempo"]))
C.append("};")
for i, s in enumerate(MU.SONGS):
    define("SONG_" + s["name"].upper(), i)

with open(os.path.join(OUT, "assets.c"), "w") as f:
    f.write("/* Generated by tools/gen_assets.py - do not edit. */\n#include \"assets.h\"\n")
    f.write("\n".join(C) + "\n")

    f.write("/* Generated by tools/gen_assets.py - do not edit. */\n#ifndef ASSETS_H\n#define ASSETS_H\n")
    f.write("\n".join(H) + "\n#endif\n")

    .section .crt0, "ax"
    .global _start
    .arm
    .align 2
_start:
    b       rom_start
    @ 0x04: Nintendo logo area (left zero; emulators boot without it)
    .fill   156, 1, 0
    @ 0xA0: game title (12 bytes)
    .ascii  "MOCHIHOP"
    .byte   0, 0, 0, 0
    @ 0xAC: game code, 0xB0: maker code
    .ascii  "RMHE"

    .byte   0               @ 0xB3 main unit code
    .byte   0               @ 0xB4 device type

    .byte   0               @ 0xBC software version

    .hword  0               @ 0xBE reserved

rom_start:
    @ IRQ mode stack, then system mode stack
    mov     r0, #0x12
    msr     cpsr_c, r0
    ldr     sp, =__sp_irq
    mov     r0, #0x1F
    msr     cpsr_c, r0
    ldr     sp, =__sp_usr

    ldr     r1, =__data_start

1:  cmp     r1, r2
    ldrlo   r3, [r0], #4

    ldr     r2, =__bss_end
    mov     r3, #0
2:  cmp     r1, r2
    strlo   r3, [r1], #4

3:  b       3b

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Patches the GBA header complement byte (0xBD) and pads the ROM."""
import sys

path = sys.argv[1]
rom = bytearray(open(path, "rb").read())
chk = 0
for b in rom[0xA0:0xBD]:
    chk = (chk - b) & 0xFF
rom[0xBD] = (chk - 0x19) & 0xFF
# pad to a multiple of 4 KiB with 0xFF (like a real mask ROM / flash cart)
while len(rom) % 4096:
    rom.append(0xFF)
open(path, "wb").write(rom)
print("header checksum 0x%02X, size %d bytes" % (rom[0xBD], len(rom)))
EOF

args.content:
# Mochi Hop

An original Game Boy Advance homebrew platformer made for **Retra**. You play Mochi, a squishy
pink rice-cake with a leaf on top. Hop across pastel cloud islands, candy caves and a starry
night, collect stars and rescue the little sprout friends, who then follow you around.

All code, art, music and level designs are original and live in this directory. No third-party
assets are used and no devkitPro is needed.

## Controls

| Button | Action |
| --- | --- |
| D-Pad | Move (on the map: pick a level) |
| A | Jump. Hold for a higher jump. Hold while stomping to bounce higher. |
| B | Run (on the map: back to the title) |
| START | Pause menu (Resume / Retry / World Map); confirm on menus |

## Levels

| # | World | Name | Stars |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-1 | Cloud Meadow | Fluffy Fields | 40 |
| 1-2 | Cloud Meadow | Breezy Bridges | 38 |
| 2-1 | Candy Caves | Gumdrop Grotto | 43 |
| 2-2 | Candy Caves | Sugar Shafts | 38 |
| 3-1 | Starry Night | Twinkle Path | 34 |
| 3-2 | Starry Night | Moonlit Summit | 43 |

Every level has 3 sprouts, at least one checkpoint flag, and a goal star. Clearing a level
unlocks the next one. Clearing 3-2 for the first time plays the credits ("Made for Retra").

Hazards: grumpy raindrops (walk, stompable), bees (fly, stompable), spiky urchins (cannot be
stomped), thorn spikes, and pits. Mochi has 3 hearts. Running out of hearts or falling into a pit
sends you back to the last checkpoint with full hearts, and you keep the stars you have collected.
Touching a checkpoint also refills your hearts. There is no game over.

## Building

Requirements: `arm-none-eabi-gcc`/`objcopy` (tested with 14.2) and Python 3 with Pillow.

```sh
./build.sh             # -> build/mochi_hop.gba + build/mochi_hop_cover.png
./build.sh --install   # also copies ROM + cover to app/src/main/assets/games and catalog/games
```

The build is deterministic: the same sources always give a byte-identical ROM. Debug variants:
`EXTRA_CFLAGS="-DDEBUG_UNLOCK_ALL -DDEBUG_NEAR_GOAL -DDEBUG_SPROUTS" ./build.sh`.

## Layout

```
build.sh              full rebuild (assets -> C -> ROM -> header fix -> cover)
gba.ld                linker script (ROM at 0x08000000, data/bss in IWRAM)
src/crt0.S            ROM header + startup (copies .data, clears .bss, calls main)
src/gba.h             minimal hardware register definitions
src/main.c            scenes: title, world map, credits; save/unlock flow
src/play.c            platforming: physics, collision, actors, camera, HUD, pause, results
src/gfx.c             VRAM loading, shadow OAM, affine Mochi sprite, text/panels
src/audio.c           PSG music sequencer (4 channels) + sound effects
src/save.c            SRAM save (magic + version + checksum); contains the "SRAM_V113" tag
tools/gen_assets.py   generates build/gen/assets.{c,h} from everything below
tools/art_sprites.py  sprite art (procedural shapes + hand-placed ASCII stamps)
tools/art_bg.py       font, UI panels, terrain auto-tiler, parallax layers, logo
tools/levels.py       hand-designed levels (small placement DSL; `python3 levels.py` prints ASCII)
tools/music.py        the original songs (melodies + chord progressions)
tools/make_cover.py   480x320 cover composed from real game layers, 2x nearest-neighbour
tools/fix_header.py   header complement checksum + padding
tools/preview*.py     dev helpers: render sprite sheets / backgrounds / whole levels to PNG
```

## Technical notes

- **Video:** mode 0 with four backgrounds. BG0 is the HUD/text layer. BG1 is the level
  (64x32 map, with tile columns streamed in from ROM as the camera moves). BG2 is the mid
  parallax layer (scrolls at about 1/3 speed) and BG3 is the far sky (1/8 speed, and the clouds
  drift). Fades and the pause dimming use the hardware brightness registers (BLDCNT/BLDY).
  The credits use window 0 to clip the scrolling text.
- **Sprites:** 1D-mapped 4bpp OBJs with 8 palettes. Mochi is a 32x32 affine double-size
  sprite, so squash and stretch is real hardware scaling driven by a damped spring: stretch on
  jump, squash on landing, bonk on ceilings, plus idle breathing. Animation frames cover idle,
  blink, a 4-frame run, jump, fall, happy and hurt.
- **Physics:** 24.8 fixed point with separate ground and air acceleration, a turn boost,
  friction, and a run speed. Jumps get 6 frames of coyote time and a 7-frame jump buffer.
  Jump height is variable: gravity is lighter while A is held on the way up, and there is a
  little hang time at the apex. Stomps bounce Mochi up, and springs launch about 9 tiles.
  One-way cloud platforms can be jumped through from below.
- **Particles:** a pool of 40 for landing and jump dust, sparkles, hearts, splashes and
  confetti.
- **Audio:** four original songs (Title, Cloud Meadow, Candy Caves and a 3/4 Starry Night
  lullaby) plus a clear jingle. Only the melodies and chord symbols are written by hand. The
  arpeggios (square 1), bass (wave channel, soft triangle) and drums (noise) are generated from
  the chords so all channels stay in sync. Sound effects borrow square 1 and the noise channel,
  using hardware frequency sweep for jumps, springs, stomps and hurts.
- **Save:** 32 KiB SRAM at 0x0E000000, written with byte access only. It stores the "MHOP"
  magic, the version, a rotating-xor checksum, the unlocked count, and per level the best stars,
  rescued-sprout mask and cleared flag. The ROM contains `SRAM_V113` so emulators pick the SRAM
  save type.
- **Header:** title `MOCHIHOP`, game code `RMHE`, maker `00`, fixed byte 0x96, and a correct
  complement checksum. The Nintendo logo area is left as zeros (fine for emulators; real
  hardware would refuse to boot it).
- **Robustness:** no BIOS calls and no interrupts. Frame sync polls VCOUNT, so the game does not
  depend on BIOS/HLE details. The code builds for ARMv4T Thumb, and the libgcc division helpers
  it links contain no ARMv5 instructions.
- **Art direction:** soft pastel palettes with 1px plum outlines and light from the top-left.
  Each world has its own terrain palette, but all worlds share the same auto-tiled shapes
