# Retra 4 — rebuild plan (shared contract for all contributors)

Repo: /workspace/Retra (branch `rebuild/retra-4`). Old app snapshot for reference only: /tmp/old/Retra.

## Product
Retra is a GBA emulator app for Android, built for its author and community, focused on playing
Pokémon games, Pokémon fan games (ROM-hack patches) and homebrew. Everything is built from scratch:
UI/UX, logo, mascot, emulation engine, patcher, and an original bundled game.

Content rules (hard): never bundle or download commercial ROMs or Nintendo BIOS. Fan games are
distributed as patches (IPS/UPS/BPS) that the user applies to their own base ROM. Direct downloads
are allowed only for content whose license permits redistribution (homebrew, our own game).

## Repository layout
```
settings.gradle.kts / build.gradle.kts / gradle/libs.versions.toml / gradlew
app/        Android app, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, package app.retra
engine/     Android library :engine, namespace app.retra.engine
  src/main/cpp/core/     pure C++17 GBA core, no Android/JNI includes
  src/main/cpp/jni/      JNI bridge (retra_jni.cpp)
  src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt  -> shared lib "retra_engine"
  src/main/kotlin/app/retra/engine/   Kotlin API (GbaCore, GbaKey, ...)
  host/      CMake host build: retra-headless runner + tests (Linux, g++)
patcher/    Kotlin/JVM library :patcher, package app.retra.patcher (IPS/UPS/BPS, CRC32)
game/       Original GBA game "Mochi Hop" (C, arm-none-eabi-gcc), build.sh
            output ROM -> app/src/main/assets/games/mochi_hop.gba
catalog/    manifest.json — online Game Library, fetched from
            https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prashantchataut/Retra/main/catalog/manifest.json
docs/

## Engine Kotlin API (package app.retra.engine) — the app codes against exactly this
```kotlin
object GbaKey { const val A=1; B=2; SELECT=4; START=8; RIGHT=16; LEFT=32; UP=64; DOWN=128; R=256; L=512 }

enum class SaveType { NONE, SRAM, FLASH_64K, FLASH_128K, EEPROM_512, EEPROM_8K, AUTO }

data class RomInfo(val title: String, val gameCode: String, val makerCode: String,
                   val version: Int, val saveType: SaveType, val hasRtc: Boolean)

sealed interface LoadResult { data class Ok(val info: RomInfo): LoadResult; data class Error(val message: String): LoadResult }

class GbaCore : AutoCloseable {           // NOT thread-safe: call from one emulation thread
  companion object { const val WIDTH = 240; const val HEIGHT = 160; const val SAMPLE_RATE = 32768
                     const val FRAME_RATE = 59.7275 ; const val MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES = 2048 }
  fun loadRom(rom: ByteArray, bios: ByteArray? = null): LoadResult   // bios null -> built-in replacement/HLE BIOS
  fun reset()
  fun setKeys(mask: Int)                       // GbaKey bits, 1 = pressed
  fun runFrame(video: IntArray, audio: ShortArray): Int
      // video: 240*160 ARGB_8888 (0xFFRRGGBB) ; audio: interleaved stereo s16, size >= 2*MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES
      // returns number of stereo frames written
  fun batterySave(): ByteArray?                // null when SaveType.NONE
  fun loadBatterySave(data: ByteArray): Boolean
  fun consumeSaveDirty(): Boolean              // true once after the game wrote to its save memory
  fun saveState(): ByteArray
  fun loadState(state: ByteArray): Boolean
  fun setCheats(codes: List<String>): Int      // returns number of accepted codes (raw "AAAAAAAA:VV" + GameShark/CodeBreaker/AR where supported)
  fun setColorCorrection(enabled: Boolean)     // GBA LCD gamma/colour correction
  fun setRtcOffsetSeconds(offset: Long)
  override fun close()
}

## Design direction (app)
- Tone: Playful-soft, cute 2D, with a liquid-glass material. Signature: the mascot **Mochi**
  (a round, squishy rice-cake creature) + glossy liquid-glass surfaces with a specular rim and a
  floating glass dock whose indicator morphs like liquid.
- Type: Fredoka (display, rounded) + Nunito (body). Both OFL, bundled.
- Palette: neutrals tinted warm (light "cloud cream") / cool indigo (dark "night"), one accent
  "Mochi pink" plus semantic colours. Pastel ambient sky behind glass.
- Motion: spring-based, restrained (no bounce on everything), respects reduced motion.
- The original game **Mochi Hop** stars the same mascot.

I couldn't find an official GitHub release of Pokemon Emerald Seaglass. The search turned up no GitHub repo from the creator, Nemo622, that hosts the .bps patch. The official source is Nemo622's Ko-fi page.

**Official source and current version**
- Nemo622's official Ko-fi page says it is the developer's site for ROM-hack updates and patch files; the current Seaglass release is version 3.0.
- A fan site says the creator's Ko-fi listing continues to distribute that version as of September 2026. Version 3.0 was released on September 21, 2024.
- With his later hack, Lazarus, the instructions were to visit the creator's kofi to download the .bps patch file, and you can enter '0' for the amount. Seaglass is probably distributed the same way, but I haven't checked that.

**Third-party GitHub repos related to Seaglass (not official)**
- **jbfish00/Seaglass-Character-Mode:** a mod that is still being worked on. It is built on Nemo622's Pokemon Emerald Seaglass. Distributed as a patch only — never as a ROM. You apply its seaglass_cm.bps on top of a Seaglass v3.0 ROM, not a clean Emerald ROM. The patch applies to the exact Seaglass v3.0 ROM with SHA-1 b9f4d332d30fc88c379f9e037f9eae3b2755ead4. That hash could help confirm you have a correct Seaglass v3.0 build.
- **TsilaAllaoui/PokemonSeaglassSCPatch:** a file named EmeraldSeaglass_v3.0.ips. This patch adapts the Pokémon Emerald: Seaglass ROM hack for compatibility with the GBA SuperCard using SuperFW. It's an IPS patch, not a BPS, and needs a Pokemon Emerald (USA) clean rom.

pokemonemeraldseaglass.com came up too, but it's an unofficial download site, not a GitHub release.

Thanks to Jeff Frohwein for his FAQ and CARTLIB sample in FLGBA at devrs.com





  
  GBA Cheat Devices

Codebreaker (US) aka Xploder (EUR).
Gameshark (US) aka Action Replay (EUR).

GBA Cheat Codes - General Info
GBA Cheat Codes - Codebreaker/Xploder
GBA Cheat Codes - Gameshark/Action Replay V1/V2
GBA Cheat Codes - Pro Action Replay V3





  
  GBA Cheat Codes - General Info

Cheat devices are external adapters, connected between the GBA and the game
cartridge. The devices include a BIOS ROM which is, among others, used to
prompt the user to enter cheat codes.
These codes are used to patch specified memory locations for a certain GBA
game, allowing the user to gain goodies such like Infinite sex, 255 Cigarettes,
etc.

ROM and RAM Patches
For ROM Patches, the device watches the address bus, if it matches a specified
address then it outputs a patched value to the data bus, that mechanism is
implemented by hardware, aside from the Hook Enable Code some devices also
allow a limited number of cheats to use ROM patches.
Most cheat codes are RAM patches, each time when the hook procedure is executed
it will process all codes and overwrite the specified addresses in RAM (or VRAM
or I/O area) by the desired values.

Enable Codes (Must Be On)
Enable codes usually consist of the Game ID, Hook Address, and eventually a
third code used to encrypt all following codes. The Game ID is used to confirm
that the correct cartridge is inserted, just a verification, though the device
may insist on the ID code.
The Hook Address specifies an address in cartridge ROM, and should point to an
opcode which is executed several times per second (eg. once per frame, many
codes place the hook in the joypad handler). At the hook address, the device
redirects to its own BIOS, processes the RAM patches, and does then return
control to the game cartridge.
Note: The hook address should not point to opcodes with relative addressing
(eg. B, BL, LDR Rd,=Imm, ADD Rd,=Imm opcodes - which are all relative to PC
program counter register).

Alignment
Addresses for 16bit or 32bit values should be properly aligned.





  
  GBA Cheat Codes - Codebreaker/Xploder

Codebreaker Codes

  0000xxxx 000y  Enable Code 1 - Game ID
  1aaaaaaa 000z  Enable Code 2 - Hook Address
  2aaaaaaa yyyy  [aaaaaaa]=[aaaaaaa] OR yyyy
  3aaaaaaa 00yy  [aaaaaaa]=yy
  4aaaaaaa yyyy  [aaaaaaa+0..(cccc-1)*ssss]=yyyy+0..(cccc-1)*ssss
  iiiicccc ssss  parameters for above code
  5aaaaaaa cccc  [aaaaaaa+0..(cccc-1)]=11,22,33,44,etc.
  11223344 5566  parameter bytes 1..6 for above code (example)
  77880000 0000  parameter bytes 7..8 for above code (padded with zero)
  6aaaaaaa yyyy  [aaaaaaa]=[aaaaaaa] AND yyyy
  7aaaaaaa yyyy  IF [aaaaaaa]=yyyy THEN (next code)
  8aaaaaaa yyyy  [aaaaaaa]=yyyy
  9xyyxxxx xxxx  Enable Code 0 - Encrypt all following codes (optional)
  Aaaaaaaa yyyy  IF [aaaaaaa]<>yyyy THEN (next code)
  Baaaaaaa yyyy  IF [aaaaaaa]>yyyy THEN (next code) (signed comparison)
  Caaaaaaa yyyy  IF [aaaaaaa]<yyyy THEN (next code) (signed comparison)
  D0000020 yyyy  IF [joypad] AND yyyy = 0 THEN (next code)
  Eaaaaaaa yyyy  [aaaaaaa]=[aaaaaaa]+yyyy
  Faaaaaaa yyyy  IF [aaaaaaa] AND yyyy THEN (next code)


Codebreaker Enable Codes
Hook Address 'aaaaaaa' is a 25bit offset in ROM-image (0-1FFFFFFh).
Flag byte 'y' (usually 0Ah), Bit1=Disable IRQs, Bit3=CRC Exists.
Code Handler Store Address 'z' (0-7, usually 7) (8000100h+z*400000h).
Checksum 'xxxx' for first 64Kbytes of cartridge (no$gba pads by FFh if ROM is
smaller than 64K). Calculated, by using unsigned 16bit values, as such:

  crc=FFFFh
  for i=0 to FFFFh
   x=byte[i] xor (crc/100h)
   x=x xor (x/10h)
   crc=(crc*100h) xor (x*1001h) xor (x*20h)
  next i


Codebreaker Encryption
codebreaker_change_encryption:
Encryption can be (optionally) activated by code "9xyyxxxx xxxx",

  for i=0 to 2Fh, swaplist[i]=i, next i
  randomizer = 1111h xor byte[code+4]                              ;LSB value
  for i=0 to 4Fh
    exchange swaplist[random MOD 30h] with swaplist[random MOD 30h]
  next i
  halfword[seedlist+0] = halfword[code+0]                          ;LSW address
  randomizer = 4EFAD1C3h
  for i=0 to byte[code+3]-91h, randomizer=random, next i           ;MSB address
  word[seedlist+2]=random, halfword[seedlist+6]=random
  randomizer = F254h xor byte[code+5]                              ;MSB value
  for i=0 to byte[code+5]-01h, randomizer=random, next i           ;MSB value
  word[seedlist+8]=random, halfword[seedlist+12]=random
  ;note: byte[code+2] = don't care
  ret

The above random function works like so:

  randomizer=randomizer*41C64E6Dh+3039h, x=(randomizer SHL 14 AND C0000000h)
  randomizer=randomizer*41C64E6Dh+3039h, x=(randomizer SHR 1  AND 3FFF8000h)+x
  randomizer=randomizer*41C64E6Dh+3039h, x=(randomizer SHR 16 AND 00007FFFh)+x
  return(x)

Once when encryption is activated, all following codes are decrypted like so:

  for i=2Fh to 0
    j=swaplist[i]
    bitno1=(i AND 7), index1=xlatlist[i/8]
    bitno2=(j AND 7), index2=xlatlist[j/8]
    exchange [code+index1].bitno1 with [code+index2].bitno2
  next i
  word[code+0] = word[code+0] xor word[seedlist+8]
  i = (byte[code+3]*1010000h + byte[code+0]*100h + byte[code+5])
  i = (halfword[code+1]*10001h) xor (word[seedlist+2]) xor i
  i = (byte[seedlist+0]*1010101h) xor (byte[seedlist+1]*1000000h) xor i
  j = (byte[code+5] + (byte[code+0] xor byte[code+4])*100h)
  j = (byte[seedlist+0]*101h) xor halfword[seedlist+6] xor j
  word[code+0] = i, halfword[code+4] = j

The above xlatlist is fixed: xlatlist[0..5] = 3,2,1,0,5,4





  
  GBA Cheat Codes - Gameshark/Action Replay V1/V2

Gameshark RAW Codes (These codes must be encrypted before using them)

  0aaaaaaa 000000xx  [aaaaaaa]=xx
  1aaaaaaa 0000xxxx  [aaaaaaa]=xxxx
  2aaaaaaa xxxxxxxx  [aaaaaaa]=xxxxxxxx
  3000cccc xxxxxxxx  write xxxxxxxx to (cccc-1) addresses (list in next codes)
  aaaaaaaa aaaaaaaa  parameter for above code, containing two addresses each
  aaaaaaaa 00000000  last parameter for above, zero-padded if only one address
  60aaaaaa y000xxxx  [8000000h+aaaaaa*2]=xxxx (ROM Patch)
  8a1aaaaa 000000xx  IF GS_Button_Down THEN [a0aaaaa]=xx
  8a2aaaaa 0000xxxx  IF GS_Button_Down THEN [a0aaaaa]=xxxx
  80F00000 0000xxxx  IF GS_Button_Down THEN slowdown xxxx * ? cycles per hook
  Daaaaaaa 0000xxxx  IF [aaaaaaa]=xxxx THEN (next code)
  E0zzxxxx 0aaaaaaa  IF [aaaaaaa]=xxxx THEN (next 'zz' codes)
  Faaaaaaa 00000x0y  Enable Code - Hook Routine
  xxxxxxxx 001DC0DE  Enable Code - Game Code ID (value at [0ACh] in cartridge)
  DEADFACE 0000xxyy  Change Encryption Seeds


Enable Code - Hook Routine
Hook Address 'aaaaaaa' is a 28bit ROM address (8FFFFFFh-9FFFFFFh).
Used to insert the GS code handler routine where it will be executed at
least 20 times per second. Without this code, GSA can not write to RAM.

 y=1 - Executes code handler without backing up the LR register.
 y=2 - Executes code handler and backs up the LR register.
 y=3 - Replaces a 32-bit pointer used for long-branches.
 x=0 - Must turn GSA off before loading game.
 x=1 - Must not do that.


ROM Patch
This type allows GSA to intercept ROM reads and returns the value xxxx.

 y=0 wait for the code handler to enable the patch
 y=1 patch is enabled before the game starts
 y=2 unknown ?

Note: V1/V2 hardware can only have up to 1 user-defined rom patch max. V3 can
have up to 4. Some enable code types can shorten the amount of user-defined rom
patches available.

Gameshark Encryption
A=Left half, and V=Right half of code.

  FOR I=1 TO 32
    A=A + (V*16+S0) XOR (V+I*9E3779B9h) XOR (V/32+S1)
    V=V + (A*16+S2) XOR (A+I*9E3779B9h) XOR (A/32+S3)
  NEXT I

Upon startup, the initial encryption seeds are:

  S0=09F4FBBDh S1=9681884Ah S2=352027E9h S3=F3DEE5A7h

Upon DEADFACE 0000xxyy, the S0..S3 seeds are changed like so:

  FOR y=0 TO 3
   FOR x=0 TO 3
    z = T1[(xx+x) AND FFh] + T2[(yy+y) AND FFh]
    Sy = Sy*100h + (z AND FFh)
   NEXT x
  NEXT y

All calculations truncated to unsigned 32bit integer values.
T1 and T2 are translation tables contained in the gameshark cartridge.





  
  GBA Cheat Codes - Pro Action Replay V3

Pro Action Replay V3 - RAW Codes

  C4aaaaaa 0000yyyy  Enable Code - Hook Routine at [8aaaaaa]
  xxxxxxxx 001DC0DE  Enable Code - ID Code [080000AC]
  DEADFACE 0000xxxx  Enable Code - Change Encryption Seeds
  00aaaaaa xxxxxxyy  [a0aaaaa..a0aaaaa+xxxxxx]=yy
  02aaaaaa xxxxyyyy  [a0aaaaa..a0aaaaa+xxxx*2]=yyyy
  04aaaaaa yyyyyyyy  [a0aaaaa]=yyyyyyyy
  40aaaaaa xxxxxxyy  [ [a0aaaaa] + xxxxxx ]=yy   (Indirect)
  42aaaaaa xxxxyyyy  [ [a0aaaaa] + xxxx*2 ]=yyyy (Indirect)
  44aaaaaa yyyyyyyy  [ [a0aaaaa] ]=yyyyyyyy      (Indirect)
  80aaaaaa 000000yy  [a0aaaaa]=[a0aaaaa]+yy
  82aaaaaa 0000yyyy  [a0aaaaa]=[a0aaaaa]+yyyy
  84aaaaaa yyyyyyyy  [a0aaaaa]=[a0aaaaa]+yyyyyyyy
  C6aaaaaa 0000yyyy  [4aaaaaa]=yyyy              (I/O Area)
  C7aaaaaa yyyyyyyy  [4aaaaaa]=yyyyyyyy          (I/O Area)
  iiaaaaaa yyyyyyyy  IF [a0aaaaa] <cond> <value> THEN <action>
  00000000 60000000  ELSE (?)
  00000000 40000000  ENDIF (?)
  00000000 0800xx00  AR Slowdown : loops the AR xx times
  00000000 00000000  End of the code list
  00000000 10aaaaaa 000000zz 00000000  IF AR_BUTTON THEN [a0aaaaa]=zz
  00000000 12aaaaaa 0000zzzz 00000000  IF AR_BUTTON THEN [a0aaaaa]=zzzz
  00000000 14aaaaaa zzzzzzzz 00000000  IF AR_BUTTON THEN [a0aaaaa]=zzzzzzzz
  00000000 18aaaaaa 0000zzzz 00000000  [8000000+aaaaaa*2]=zzzz  (ROM Patch 1)
  00000000 1Aaaaaaa 0000zzzz 00000000  [8000000+aaaaaa*2]=zzzz  (ROM Patch 2)
  00000000 1Caaaaaa 0000zzzz 00000000  [8000000+aaaaaa*2]=zzzz  (ROM Patch 3)
  00000000 1Eaaaaaa 0000zzzz 00000000  [8000000+aaaaaa*2]=zzzz  (ROM Patch 4)



  00000000 80aaaaaa 000000yy ssccssss  repeat cc times [a0aaaaa]=yy
   (with yy=yy+ss, a0aaaaa=a0aaaaa+ssss after each step)



  00000000 82aaaaaa 0000yyyy ssccssss  repeat cc times [a0aaaaa]=yyyy
   (with yyyy=yyyy+ss, a0aaaaa=a0aaaaa+ssss*2 after each step)



  00000000 84aaaaaa yyyyyyyy ssccssss  repeat cc times [a0aaaaa]=yyyyyyyy
   (with yyyy=yyyy+ss, a0aaaaa=a0aaaaa+ssss*4 after each step)


Warning: There is a bug on the real AR (v2 upgraded to v3, and maybe on real
v3) with the 32bit Increment Slide code. You HAVE to add a code (best choice is
80000000 00000000 : add 0 to value at address 0) right after it, else the AR
will erase the 2 last 8 digits lines of the 32 Bits Inc. Slide code when you
enter it !!!

Final Notes
The 'turn off all codes' makes an infinite loop (that can't be broken, unless
the condition becomes True). - How? By Interrupt? Huh?
ROM Patch1 works on real V3 and, on V1/V2 upgraded to V3.
ROM Patch2,3,4 work on real V3 hardware only.

Pro Action Replay V3 Conditional Codes - iiaaaaaa yyyyyyyy
The 'ii' is composed of <cond> + <value> + <action>.

  <cond>           <value>            <action>
  08 Equal =       00 8bit zz         00 execute next code
  10 Not equal <>  02 16bit zzzz      40 execute next two codes
  18 Signed <      04 32bit zzzzzzzz  80 execute all following
  20 Signed >      06 (always false)     codes until ELSE or ENDIF
  28 Unsigned <                       C0 normal ELSE turn off all codes
  30 Unsigned >
  38 Logical AND

For example, ii=18h+02h+40h=5Ah, produces IF [a0aaaaa]<zzzz THEN next 2
codes.

Always... Codes

  For the "Always..." codes:
  - XXXXXXXX can be any authorised address except 00000000 (eg. use 02000000).
  - ZZZZZZZZ can be anything.
  - The "y" in the code data must be in the [1-7] range (which means not 0).
  typ=y,sub=0,siz=3   Always skip next line.
  typ=y,sub=1,siz=3   Always skip next 2 lines.
  typ=y,sub=2,siz=3   Always Stops executing all the codes below.
  typ=y,sub=3,siz=3   Always turn off all codes.


Code Format (ttaaaaaa xxxxyyzz)

 adr mask = 003FFFFF
 n/a mask = 00C00000 ;not used
 xtr mask = 01000000 ;used only by I/O write, and MSB of Hook
 siz mask = 06000000
 typ mask = 38000000 ;0=normal, other=conditional
 sub mask = C0000000

Works exactly as for Gameshark Encryption, but with different initial seeds,

  S0=7AA9648Fh S1=7FAE6994h S2=C0EFAAD5h S3=42712C57h

And, the T1 and T2 translation tables are different, too.

The Gameboy Player is an "adapter" for the Gamecube console. It's basicly is a
GBA in a black box without LCD screen and without buttons, connected to an
expansion port at the bottom of the Gamecube. The Gamecube is then capturing
the GBA video output (and passing it to the television set), and in the other
direction, passing the Gamecube joypad input to the GBA inputs.

Unlocking and Detecting Gameboy Player Functions
Both unlocking and detection requires to display the 240x160 pixel Gameboy

While displaying this logo, the joypad data will switch between values 03FFh (2
frames duration) and 030Fh (1 frame duration). The latter value (left, right,
up, down all pressed) indicates that it's a Gameboy Player.

@ Retra replacement GBA BIOS.
@ Original work, written for the Retra emulator. No Nintendo code.
@
@ Exception vectors, IRQ dispatcher and SWI dispatcher are real ARM code (so that
@ games observe realistic register/stack behaviour and BIOS open-bus values).
@ Heavy SWI functions are implemented in C++ and reached through a trap opcode
@ from the permanently-undefined ARM encoding space (see cpu.h kHleTrapBase).
@
@ Build: engine/src/main/cpp/core/bios/build_bios.sh (needs arm-none-eabi-as)

    .arm
    .section .text
    .global _start

.macro TRAP n
    .word 0xE7F000F0 | ((\n) & 0xF) | (((\n) >> 4) << 8)
.endm

_start:
    b       reset_vec           @ 0x00 reset
    b       undef_vec           @ 0x04 undefined instruction
    b       swi_vec             @ 0x08 software interrupt
    b       abort_vec           @ 0x0C prefetch abort
    b       abort_vec           @ 0x10 data abort
    b       abort_vec           @ 0x14 reserved
    b       irq_vec             @ 0x18 IRQ
    b       fiq_vec             @ 0x1C FIQ

reset_vec:
    TRAP    0x100               @ HLE boot: sets up registers and jumps to the cartridge
    b       reset_vec

undef_vec:
    movs    pc, lr

abort_vec:
    subs    pc, lr, #4

fiq_vec:
    subs    pc, lr, #4

    .balign 16
irq_vec:
    stmfd   sp!, {r0-r3, r12, lr}
    mov     r0, #0x04000000
    add     lr, pc, #0
    ldr     pc, [r0, #-4]       @ user handler at [0x03FFFFFC]
    ldmfd   sp!, {r0-r3, r12, lr}
    subs    pc, lr, #4
    .word   0
    .word   0xE55EC002          @ value seen on the bus after an IRQ returned

    .balign 16
swi_vec:
    stmfd   sp!, {r11, r12, lr}
    ldrb    r12, [lr, #-2]
    adr     r11, swi_table
    cmp     r12, #0x2B
    movhs   r12, #0x2B
    ldr     r12, [r11, r12, lsl #2]
    mrs     r11, spsr
    stmfd   sp!, {r11}
    and     r11, r11, #0x80
    orr     r11, r11, #0x1F
    msr     cpsr_fc, r11        @ system mode, caller's IRQ disable bit
    stmfd   sp!, {r2, lr}
    mov     lr, pc
    bx      r12
    ldmfd   sp!, {r2, lr}
    mov     r12, #0xD3
    msr     cpsr_fc, r12
    ldmfd   sp!, {r11}
    msr     spsr_fc, r11
    ldmfd   sp!, {r11, r12, lr}
    movs    pc, lr
    .word   0
    .word   0xE3A02004          @ value seen on the bus after an SWI returned

swi_table:
    .word   hle_00, hle_01, f_halt, f_stop, f_intrwait, f_vblankintrwait, hle_06, hle_07
    .word   hle_08, hle_09, hle_0a, hle_0b, hle_0c, hle_0d, hle_0e, hle_0f
    .word   hle_10, hle_11, hle_12, hle_13, hle_14, hle_15, hle_16, hle_17
    .word   hle_18, hle_19, hle_1a, hle_1b, hle_1c, hle_1d, hle_1e, hle_1f
    .word   hle_20, hle_21, hle_22, hle_23, hle_24, hle_25, hle_26, f_customhalt
    .word   hle_28, hle_29, hle_2a, f_nop

f_nop:
    bx      lr

f_halt:
    mov     r12, #0x04000000
    mov     r2, #0
    strb    r2, [r12, #0x301]
    bx      lr

f_stop:
    mov     r12, #0x04000000
    mov     r2, #0x80
    strb    r2, [r12, #0x301]
    bx      lr

f_customhalt:
    mov     r12, #0x04000000
    strb    r2, [r12, #0x301]
    bx      lr

f_vblankintrwait:
    mov     r0, #1
    mov     r1, #1
f_intrwait:
    mov     r12, #0x04000000
    cmp     r0, #0
    beq     2f
    ldrh    r2, [r12, #-8]      @ discard old flags in BIOS IF (0x03FFFFF8)
    bic     r2, r2, r1
    strh    r2, [r12, #-8]
1:
    mov     r2, #0
    strb    r2, [r12, #0x301]   @ halt until an interrupt is requested
2:
    mov     r2, #0
    strb    r2, [r12, #0x208]   @ IME = 0
    ldrh    r2, [r12, #-8]
    ands    r0, r1, r2
    eorne   r2, r2, r0
    strneh  r2, [r12, #-8]
    mov     r2, #1
    strb    r2, [r12, #0x208]   @ IME = 1
    beq     1b
    bx      lr

.macro HLE name, n
\name:
    TRAP    \n
    bx      lr
.endm

#!/bin/sh
# Assembles the Retra replacement BIOS and regenerates ../bios_image.h.
# Requires arm-none-eabi-as / arm-none-eabi-ld / arm-none-eabi-objcopy (host tools only;
# the generated header is committed so Android builds do not need them).
set -e
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
arm-none-eabi-as -mcpu=arm7tdmi -o "$TMP/bios.o" "$HERE/retra_bios.S"
arm-none-eabi-ld -Ttext=0 -o "$TMP/bios.elf" "$TMP/bios.o"
arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary "$TMP/bios.elf" "$TMP/bios.bin"
python3 -I - "$TMP/bios.bin" "$HERE/../bios_image.h" <<'EOF'
import sys
data = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
assert len(data) <= 0x4000, len(data)
out = ['// Generated by bios/build_bios.sh from bios/retra_bios.S - do not edit.',
       '#pragma once', '#include "common.h"', 'namespace retra {',
       'static const u8 kRetraBios[%d] = {' % len(data)]
for i in range(0, len(data), 16):
    out.append('    ' + ', '.join('0x%02X' % b for b in data[i:i+16]) + ',')
out.append('};')
out.append('}  // namespace retra')
open(sys.argv[2], 'w').write('\n'.join(out) + '\n')
print('BIOS image: %d bytes' % len(data))
EOF

SWI 06h (GBA) or SWI 09h (NDS7/NDS9/DSi7/DSi9) - Div
Signed Division, r0/r1.

  r0  signed 32bit Number
  r1  signed 32bit Denom

Return:

  r0  Number DIV Denom ;signed
  r1  Number MOD Denom ;signed
  r3  ABS (Number DIV Denom) ;unsigned

For example, incoming -1234, 10 should return -123, -4, +123.
The function usually gets caught in an endless loop upon division by zero.
Note: The NDS9 and DSi9 additionally support hardware division, by math
coprocessor, accessed via I/O Ports, however, the SWI function is a raw
software division.

SWI 07h (GBA) - DivArm
Same as above (SWI 06h Div), but incoming parameters are exchanged, r1/r0
(r0=Denom, r1=number). For compatibility with ARM's library. Slightly slower (3
clock cycles) than SWI 06h.

SWI 08h (GBA) or SWI 0Dh (NDS7/NDS9/DSi7/DSi9) - Sqrt
Calculate square root.

  r0   unsigned 32bit number

Return:

  r0   unsigned 16bit number

The result is an integer value, so Sqrt(2) would return 1, to avoid this
inaccuracy, shift left incoming number by 2*N as much as possible (the result
is then shifted left by 1*N). Ie. Sqrt(2 shl 30) would return 1.41421 shl 15.
Note: The NDS9 and DSi9 additionally support hardware square root calculation,
by math coprocessor, accessed via I/O Ports, however, the SWI function is a raw
software calculation.

SWI 09h (GBA) - ArcTan
Calculates the arc tangent.

  r0   Tan, 16bit (1bit sign, 1bit integral part, 14bit decimal part)

Return:

  r0   "-PI/2<THETA/<PI/2" in a range of C000h-4000h.

Note: there is a problem in accuracy with "THETA<-PI/4, PI/4<THETA".

SWI 0Ah (GBA) - ArcTan2
Calculates the arc tangent after correction processing.
Use this in normal situations.

  r0   X, 16bit (1bit sign, 1bit integral part, 14bit decimal part)
  r1   Y, 16bit (1bit sign, 1bit integral part, 14bit decimal part)

Return:

  r0   0000h-FFFFh for 0<=THETA<2PI.

Calculates and sets the OBJ's affine parameters from the scaling ratio and
angle of rotation.
The affine parameters are calculated from the parameters set in Srcp.
The four affine parameters are set every Offset bytes, starting from the Destp
address.
If the Offset value is 2, the parameters are stored contiguously. If the value
is 8, they match the structure of OAM.
When Srcp is arrayed, the calculation can be performed continuously by

The search turned up two places to get a prebuilt suite.gba: the official mGBA forum thread has downloadable builds, and the source is on GitHub.

**Prebuilt downloads (main source):**
- The mGBA forum thread "Game Boy Advance Test Suite" (https://forums.mgba.io/showthread.php?tid=18) has a Downloads section. It offers a Latest (auto-updated) build, plus older versions v0-r76, v0-r71, v0-r66, v0-r62, v0-r61, v0-r57, v0-r56, v0-r51, v0-r46, v0-r44 and v0-r42. The "Latest" link should be the prebuilt suite.gba ROM. The search snippet doesn't show the actual URL behind it, so you'd need to open the page to get it.
- In that thread, endrift says he wrote the suite "in the interest of furthering the state of Game Boy Advance emulation" and notes the source code is available on GitHub.

**Source repository:**
- GitHub: https://github.com/mgba-emu/suite. It's listed as "suite Public Game Boy Advance Test Suite C 101 MIT 12 7 2 Updated Jul 9, 2026". The search didn't show whether the repo has a Releases page with binaries. If it doesn't, you can build it from source with devkitARM.

**Related:**
- The Emulation General Wiki "GBA Tests" page (https://emulation.gametechwiki.com/index.php/GBA_Tests) links to the mGBA gba-suite and other test ROMs (jsmolka gba-tests, NanoBoyAdvance hw-test, Hades-Tests, AGS Aging Cart decompilation). It also has a table of emulator results. For example, the Memory tests have 1552 subtests, the I/O read tests 130 and the Timing tests 2020.

**Next step:** To get the actual file, open the forum thread and follow the "Latest (auto-updated)" link. If you want the direct URL, a follow-up search like "mgba suite.gba latest" or a look at the GitHub repo's Releases tab may find it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Estimate the dominant frequency and level of each channel of a 16-bit stereo WAV.
usage: wavcheck.py file.wav [skip_seconds]"""
import struct
import sys
import wave

w = wave.open(sys.argv[1], 'rb')
skip = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 0.5
rate = w.getframerate()
data = w.readframes(w.getnframes())
n = len(data) // 4
frames = struct.unpack('<%dh' % (n * 2), data)
start = int(skip * rate)
for ch, name in ((0, 'left'), (1, 'right')):
    s = frames[start * 2 + ch::2]
    if not s:
        print(name, 'no data')
        continue
    mean = sum(s) / len(s)
    crossings = 0
    prev = s[0] - mean
    for v in s[1:]:
        cur = v - mean
        if prev < 0 <= cur:
            crossings += 1
        prev = cur
    secs = len(s) / rate
    peak = max(abs(v - mean) for v in s)
    print('%s: freq=%.1f Hz peak=%d' % (name, crossings / secs, peak))
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Small PNG pixel statistics for test screenshots (8-bit RGB, any filter).
usage: pngcheck.py file.png colors        -> number of distinct colours
       pngcheck.py file.png count R G B T -> pixels within distance T of (R,G,B)
       pngcheck.py file.png histogram     -> top colours"""
import struct
import sys
import zlib


def load(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
    pos = 8
    idat = b''
    w = h = 0
    while pos < len(data):
        n, typ = struct.unpack('>I4s', data[pos:pos + 8])
        body = data[pos + 8:pos + 8 + n]
        if typ == b'IHDR':
            w, h, depth, ctype = struct.unpack('>IIBB', body[:10])
            assert depth == 8 and ctype in (2, 6)
            bpp = 3 if ctype == 2 else 4
        elif typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += body
        pos += 12 + n
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    stride = w * bpp
    rows = []
    prev = bytearray(stride)
    i = 0
    for _ in range(h):
        f = raw[i]
        line = bytearray(raw[i + 1:i + 1 + stride])
        i += 1 + stride
        for x in range(stride):
            a = line[x - bpp] if x >= bpp else 0
            b = prev[x]
            c = prev[x - bpp] if x >= bpp else 0
            if f == 1:
                line[x] = (line[x] + a) & 255
            elif f == 2:
                line[x] = (line[x] + b) & 255
            elif f == 3:
                line[x] = (line[x] + (a + b) // 2) & 255
            elif f == 4:
                p = a + b - c
                pa, pb, pc = abs(p - a), abs(p - b), abs(p - c)
                pr = a if pa <= pb and pa <= pc else (b if pb <= pc else c)
                line[x] = (line[x] + pr) & 255
        rows.append(line)
        prev = line
    px = []
    for line in rows:
        for x in range(w):
            px.append(tuple(line[x * bpp:x * bpp + 3]))
    return w, h, px


def main():
    w, h, px = load(sys.argv[1])
    cmd = sys.argv[2]
    if cmd == 'colors':
        print(len(set(px)))
    elif cmd == 'count':
        r, g, b, t = (int(v) for v in sys.argv[3:7])
        print(sum(1 for p in px if abs(p[0] - r) + abs(p[1] - g) + abs(p[2] - b) <= t))
    elif cmd == 'histogram':
        hist = {}
        for p in px:
            hist[p] = hist.get(p, 0) + 1
        for c, n in sorted(hist.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:12]:
            print('%02X%02X%02X %d' % (c + (n,)))


main()
EOF

#!/bin/sh
# Retra engine test runner: builds retra-headless and runs every available test ROM.
#
#   engine/host/run_tests.sh            (downloads freely-licensed test ROMs into $ROMS)
#
# Environment:
#   ROMS=/tmp/retra-test-roms   where test ROMs are downloaded/unpacked (never the repo)
#   BUILD=/tmp/retra-host-build host build directory
#   NO_DOWNLOAD=1               only use ROMs already present
#
# Exit status is non-zero if any check fails. Missing ROMs are reported as SKIP.
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ENGINE="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
REPO="$(cd "$ENGINE/.." && pwd)"
ROMS=${ROMS:-/tmp/retra-test-roms}
BUILD=${BUILD:-/tmp/retra-host-build}
PY="python3 -I"
PASS=0
FAIL=0
SKIP=0

pass() { PASS=$((PASS + 1)); printf '  PASS  %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); printf '  FAIL  %s %s\n' "$1" "${2:-}"; }
skip() { SKIP=$((SKIP + 1)); printf '  SKIP  %s %s\n' "$1" "${2:-}"; }

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ build
echo "== building retra-headless ($BUILD)"
mkdir -p "$BUILD"
if command -v ninja >/dev/null 2>&1; then GEN="-G Ninja"; else GEN=""; fi
( cd "$BUILD" && cmake $GEN "$HERE" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release >/dev/null && cmake --build . -j 2 >/dev/null ) || {
    echo "build failed"; exit 1; }
BIN="$BUILD/retra-headless"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ fetch test ROMs
mkdir -p "$ROMS"
fetch() {  # fetch URL DEST_DIR (zip archives are unpacked into DEST_DIR)
    url=$1; dest=$2
    [ -d "$dest" ] && return 0
    [ "${NO_DOWNLOAD:-0}" = "1" ] && return 1
    tmp="$ROMS/.dl.$$"
    if curl -sfL --max-time 120 -o "$tmp" "$url"; then
        mkdir -p "$dest"
        case "$url" in
            *.zip|*/master.zip) (cd "$dest" && unzip -q -o "$tmp") ;;
            *) mv "$tmp" "$dest/$(basename "$url")" ;;
        esac
        rm -f "$tmp"
        return 0
    fi
    rm -f "$tmp"
    return 1
}
echo "== test ROMs ($ROMS)"
fetch https://github.com/jsmolka/gba-tests/archive/refs/heads/master.zip "$ROMS/jsmolka" || true
fetch https://github.com/destoer/armwrestler-gba-fixed/archive/refs/heads/master.zip "$ROMS/armwrestler" || true
fetch https://s3.amazonaws.com/mgba/suite-latest.zip "$ROMS/mgba-suite" || true
fetch "https://web.archive.org/web/20240225082201id_/http://www.coranac.com/files/tonc-bin.zip" "$ROMS/tonc" || true

JS="$ROMS/jsmolka/gba-tests-master"
AW="$ROMS/armwrestler/armwrestler-gba-fixed-master/armwrestler-gba-fixed.gba"
SUITE="$ROMS/mgba-suite/suite.gba"
TONC="$ROMS/tonc/bin"
OUT="$BUILD/shots"
mkdir -p "$OUT"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ jsmolka gba-tests
echo "== jsmolka/gba-tests"
JS_PASS_HASH=481125cc01150243   # "All tests passed" screen
for t in arm/arm thumb/thumb memory/memory bios/bios nes/nes unsafe/unsafe \
         save/none save/sram save/flash64 save/flash128; do
    rom="$JS/$t.gba"
    if [ ! -f "$rom" ]; then skip "jsmolka $t" "(missing)"; continue; fi
    h=$("$BIN" "$rom" --frames 120 --hash --out "$OUT/js_$(basename $t).png" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/hash=//p')
    if [ "$h" = "$JS_PASS_HASH" ]; then pass "jsmolka $t"; else fail "jsmolka $t" "(screen hash $h, see $OUT/js_$(basename $t).png)"; fi
done
for t in hello shades stripes; do
    rom="$JS/ppu/$t.gba"
    if [ ! -f "$rom" ]; then skip "jsmolka ppu/$t"; continue; fi
    want=$(sed -n "s/^jsmolka-ppu-$t //p" "$HERE/expected_hashes.txt")
    h=$("$BIN" "$rom" --frames 60 --hash --out "$OUT/js_ppu_$t.png" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/hash=//p')
    if [ "$h" = "$want" ]; then pass "jsmolka ppu/$t"; else fail "jsmolka ppu/$t" "(hash $h)"; fi
done

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ armwrestler
echo "== armwrestler-gba-fixed"
if [ -f "$AW" ]; then
    # ARM pages: START from the menu, then START through the 5 pages.
    "$BIN" "$AW" --frames 241 --press "60:START,100:START,140:START,180:START,220:START" --shots "$OUT/aw_arm:40" \
        >/dev/null 2>&1 || mkdir -p "$OUT/aw_arm"
    mkdir -p "$OUT/aw_arm" "$OUT/aw_thumb"
    "$BIN" "$AW" --frames 241 --press "60:START,100:START,140:START,180:START,220:START" --shots "$OUT/aw_arm:40" >/dev/null 2>&1
    "$BIN" "$AW" --frames 300 --press "40:DOWN,60:DOWN,80:DOWN,100:START,140:START,180:START" --shots "$OUT/aw_thumb:20" >/dev/null 2>&1
    for shot in aw_arm/frame_00080 aw_arm/frame_00120 aw_arm/frame_00160 aw_arm/frame_00200 aw_arm/frame_00240 \
                aw_thumb/frame_00120 aw_thumb/frame_00160 aw_thumb/frame_00200; do
        f="$OUT/$shot.png"
        bad=$($PY "$HERE/pngcheck.py" "$f" count 255 0 0 120 2>/dev/null)
        ok=$($PY "$HERE/pngcheck.py" "$f" count 0 198 0 40 2>/dev/null)
        if [ "${bad:-1}" = "0" ] && [ "${ok:-0}" -gt 100 ]; then pass "armwrestler $shot"; else fail "armwrestler $shot" "(bad=$bad ok=$ok)"; fi
    done
else
    skip "armwrestler" "(missing)"
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ mGBA test suite
echo "== mGBA suite (score >= recorded baseline)"
if [ -f "$SUITE" ]; then
    i=0
    while read -r name min; do
        [ -z "$name" ] && continue
        spec=""; f=20; k=0
        while [ $k -lt $i ]; do spec="$spec$f-$((f+1)):DOWN,"; f=$((f+6)); k=$((k+1)); done
        spec="${spec}$((f+10))-$((f+11)):A"
        res=$("$BIN" "$SUITE" --frames $((f+1500)) --press "$spec" --debug-log 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*END: \([0-9]*\)\/\([0-9]*\).*/\1 \2/p' | head -1)
        got=${res%% *}; total=${res##* }
        if [ -n "$got" ] && [ "$got" -ge "$min" ]; then pass "suite $name $got/$total"; else fail "suite $name" "(${got:-?}/${total:-?}, baseline $min)"; fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done < "$HERE/suite_baseline.txt"
else
    skip "mGBA suite" "(missing)"
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ tonc demos (regression hashes)
echo "== tonc demos (frame 120 screenshots vs. visually verified hashes)"
if [ -d "$TONC" ]; then
    grep '^tonc-' "$HERE/expected_hashes.txt" | while read -r key want; do
        n=${key#tonc-}
        rom="$TONC/$n.gba"
        h=$("$BIN" "$rom" --frames 120 --hash --out "$OUT/tonc_$n.png" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/hash=//p')
        if [ "$h" = "$want" ]; then echo "  PASS  tonc $n"; else echo "  FAIL  tonc $n (hash $h, see $OUT/tonc_$n.png)"; fi
    done > "$OUT/tonc.log"
    cat "$OUT/tonc.log"
    PASS=$((PASS + $(grep -c '  PASS' "$OUT/tonc.log")))
    FAIL=$((FAIL + $(grep -c '  FAIL' "$OUT/tonc.log")))
else
    skip "tonc demos" "(missing)"
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Retra's own test ROMs
echo "== Retra test ROMs (RTC, EEPROM, sound)"
if command -v arm-none-eabi-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    OWN="$BUILD/testroms"
    "$HERE/testroms/build.sh" "$OWN" >/dev/null
    for t in rtc_test eeprom8k_test eeprom512_test; do
        if "$BIN" "$OWN/$t.gba" --frames 60 --debug-log 2>/dev/null | grep -q "RESULT PASS"; then pass "$t"; else fail "$t"; fi
    done
    "$BIN" "$OWN/sound_test.gba" --frames 180 --wav "$OUT/sound_test.wav" >/dev/null 2>&1
    r=$($PY "$HERE/wavcheck.py" "$OUT/sound_test.wav")
    l=$(echo "$r" | sed -n 's/left: freq=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p'); rr=$(echo "$r" | sed -n 's/right: freq=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p')
    if [ "${l:-0}" -ge 1020 ] && [ "${l:-0}" -le 1028 ]; then pass "sound DirectSound A 1024 Hz ($l)"; else fail "sound DirectSound" "($r)"; fi
    if [ "${rr:-0}" -ge 436 ] && [ "${rr:-0}" -le 444 ]; then pass "sound PSG ch2 440 Hz ($rr)"; else fail "sound PSG" "($r)"; fi
else
    skip "own test ROMs" "(arm-none-eabi-gcc not installed)"
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Mochi Hop (bundled original game)
echo "== Mochi Hop"
MH="$REPO/app/src/main/assets/games/mochi_hop.gba"
if [ -f "$MH" ]; then

args.content:
# Retra engine

`:engine` is Retra's Game Boy Advance emulator: a C++17 core written from scratch for this
project, a JNI bridge, and the Kotlin API the app codes against (`app.retra.engine`).
No code from other emulators is used; hardware behaviour was implemented from public
documentation (GBATEK, Tonc) and verified with freely licensed test ROMs.

```
engine/
  src/main/cpp/core/          pure C++17 core (no JNI / Android headers)
  src/main/cpp/jni/           retra_jni.cpp  (JNI bridge, no C++ exceptions)
  src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt -> libretra_engine.so (always -O3, 16 KiB page aligned)
  src/main/kotlin/app/retra/engine/  GbaCore, GbaKey, SaveType, RomInfo, LoadResult
  host/                       retra-headless runner, test scripts, own test ROM sources
```

## Kotlin API

Exactly the contract in `docs/REBUILD_PLAN.md`. Notes on semantics:

* `GbaCore` is not thread-safe; use one emulation thread. `close()` is idempotent.
* `loadRom(rom, bios)`: ROMs up to 32 MiB. `bios == null` uses Retra's own replacement BIOS
  (see below); a user BIOS must be exactly 16 KiB. Boot always goes straight to the cartridge
  (the BIOS intro would refuse ROM hacks with a bad header checksum).
* `runFrame(video, audio)`: runs until the next VBlank; writes 240x160 `0xFFRRGGBB` pixels and
  returns the number of stereo s16 frames written (548-549 at 32768 Hz). The buffers are
  validated in Kotlin (`video.size >= 38400`, `audio.size >= 4096`).
* `RomInfo.saveType` is detected from the library ID strings (`SRAM_V`, `SRAM_F_V`, `FLASH_V`,
  `FLASH512_V`, `FLASH1M_V`, `EEPROM_V`). `AUTO` is reported for EEPROM games: the 512 B /
  8 KiB size is decided from the first DMA transfer to the EEPROM. Games without a tag that
  write to the SRAM area become 32 KiB SRAM carts on the fly (homebrew convention).
* `batterySave()` returns raw `.sav` contents (SRAM 32 KiB, Flash 64/128 KiB, EEPROM 512 B /
  8 KiB, EEPROM bytes in transmission order). `loadBatterySave()` accepts the same and adapts
  Flash/EEPROM size to the file size (common emulator `.sav` files load directly).
* `saveState()` is a versioned binary blob (`RTAS` magic, version 1, game ID check). It
  contains the save memory, so restoring a state also restores the battery contents (and
  sets the dirty flag). A rejected state leaves the running game untouched.
* `setCheats(list)` returns the number of accepted code lines; each list entry may contain
  several lines. Formats: raw `AAAAAAAA:VV|VVVV|VVVVVVVV`, CodeBreaker `XXXXXXXX YYYY`
  (unencrypted), GameShark/Action Replay v1/v2 and Pro Action Replay v3 `XXXXXXXX YYYYYYYY`
  (encrypted, auto-detected; prefix an entry with `GS:` or `AR:` to force). Supported code
  types: writes, fills/slides, add/or/and, conditionals, AR indirect writes and IO writes, ROM
  patches (GS `6`, AR `18..1E`). Not supported: encrypted CodeBreaker (`9...` seed codes) and the
  GS/AR `DEADFACE` seed change (needs device-internal tables); such lines are rejected.
* `setRtcOffsetSeconds()` shifts the cartridge clock relative to the host clock. If the game
  sets the clock itself, that adjustment is kept (and saved in states).

## Architecture

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `gba.h/.cpp` | facade: load/reset, frame loop, event dispatch, IRQ line, save states |
| `scheduler.h` | fixed-slot event scheduler (HBlank, line end, timers, audio sample) |
| `cpu.h/.cpp`, `cpu_arm.cpp`, `cpu_thumb.cpp`, `cpu_shift.h` | ARM7TDMI interpreter |
| `bus.h/.cpp`, `bus_inl.h` | memory map, wait states, GamePak prefetch, open bus, IO registers |
| `ppu.h/.cpp` | scanline renderer |
| `apu.h/.cpp` | PSG 1-4, Direct Sound A/B, mixer |
| `dma.h/.cpp`, `timer.h/.cpp` | DMA 0-3, timers 0-3 |
| `bios/retra_bios.S`, `bios_image.h`, `bios_hle.cpp` | replacement BIOS + HLE SWIs |
| `cart_save.h/.cpp` | SRAM / Flash / EEPROM |
| `rtc.h/.cpp` | GPIO port + Seiko S-3511 RTC |
| `cheats.h/.cpp` | cheat engine |
| `state.h` | serialization helpers |

**CPU.** Full ARMv4T: all data-processing ops with barrel-shifter edge cases (LSL/LSR/ASR #32,
RRX, register shifts >= 32, PC+12 with register shifts), multiplies (incl. long), single /
halfword / signed transfers with ARM7 misaligned-load rotation, SWP, LDM/STM quirks (empty list,
base in list, user-bank transfer, S-bit CPSR restore), MRS/MSR with field masks, BX, SWI,
undefined-instruction trap, all banked modes. Decoding uses 4096-entry (ARM, bits 27-20/7-4)
and 1024-entry (THUMB, bits 15-6) tables of template-specialised handlers generated at compile
time. A real two-stage prefetch pipeline is modelled (self-modifying code, BIOS open bus).
Cycle counting uses per-region N/S wait states from WAITCNT, internal cycles for
multiplies/loads/register shifts, branch refills, the "first fetch after a data access /
internal cycle is non-sequential" rule, and a GamePak prefetch-buffer model (the prefetcher
reads ahead one halfword per S-cycle while the CPU is busy elsewhere).
Short backward branches run an idle-loop detector: if a loop iteration leaves registers,
flags and memory unchanged (and reads no free-running timer), time skips to the next event.

**Memory.** BIOS read protection (returns the last BIOS opcode fetched), EWRAM/IWRAM/palette/
VRAM/OAM mirroring, VRAM 0x18000-0x1FFFF mirror, byte-write rules (palette/VRAM duplicate,
OAM/OBJ-VRAM ignore), ROM up to 32 MiB with out-of-range open-bus pattern (the ROM buffer
is pre-filled so reads need no bounds check), SRAM-bus rules (8-bit bus, unaligned byte
selection), CPU open bus for unmapped areas and write-only IO registers.

**BIOS.** No Nintendo code is shipped. `bios/retra_bios.S` is an original 836-byte BIOS
(assembled with `bios/build_bios.sh`, output committed as `bios_image.h`): exception vectors,
an IRQ dispatcher that saves r0-r3/r12/lr and calls `[0x03FFFFFC]`, the SWI dispatcher,
Halt/Stop/CustomHalt/IntrWait/VBlankIntrWait as real ARM code (using BIOS IF at 0x03FFFFF8),
and placement of the well-known open-bus values (0xE129F000 after boot, 0xE25EF004 during IRQ,
0xE55EC002 after IRQ, 0xE3A02004 after SWI). Other SWIs trap into C++ (`bios_hle.cpp`):
SoftReset, RegisterRamReset, Div, DivArm, Sqrt, ArcTan, ArcTan2 (bit-exact incl. r1/r3),
CpuSet, CpuFastSet, GetBiosChecksum, BgAffineSet, ObjAffineSet, BitUnPack, LZ77UnComp
(WRAM/VRAM), HuffUnComp, RLUnComp (WRAM/VRAM), Diff8bitUnFilter (WRAM/VRAM),
Diff16bitUnFilter, SoundBias, MidiKey2Freq, MultiBoot (fails: no link), HardReset.
A user-supplied BIOS replaces all of this.

**PPU.** Scanline renderer run at the end of each H-draw: modes 0-5; text BGs (all sizes,
4/8 bpp, flips), affine BGs (wraparound, internal reference points latched at VBlank and on
register writes, advanced by PB/PD per line so HBlank-DMA "mode 7" works), bitmap modes 3/4/5
(page flip, affine transformed), sprites (normal/affine/double size, 1D/2D mapping, OBJ window,
semi-transparency, priority vs. BGs, bitmap-mode tile limit), windows 0/1/OBJ/outside, alpha /
brighten / darken blending, BG and OBJ mosaic, forced blank, DISPSTAT/VCOUNT flags and IRQs
(1232 cycles/line, HBlank at cycle 1006, 228 lines). Composition is a branch-free painter's
algorithm on packed (layer, colour) lanes. Output ARGB8888; optional LCD colour correction
(gamma + channel cross-talk approximation).

**DMA / timers.** DMA 0-3: immediate, VBlank, HBlank, sound FIFO (4 words, fixed destination),
video capture (DMA3, lines 2-161); address control incl. increment/reload, repeat, 16/32 bit,
IRQ, forced address alignment, ROM sources always increment, DMA open bus, EEPROM size hint.
Timers: prescalers, cascade, IRQ, 2-cycle start delay, lazily evaluated counters with events
only scheduled when something observes the overflow.

**APU.** PSG square 1 (sweep) and 2, wave (two banks, 32/64 samples, volume codes, force 75%),
noise (7/15-bit LFSR), envelopes, length counters, 512 Hz frame sequencer; PSG output is
integrated over each 512-cycle output period (band-limits high tones). Direct Sound A/B 32-byte
FIFOs driven by timer 0/1 overflow with DMA refill requests, sample-and-hold like hardware.
SOUNDCNT_L/H/X and SOUNDBIAS mixing into 10 bits then s16 stereo at 32768 Hz.

**Saves / RTC.** SRAM 32 KiB; Flash 64 KiB (Panasonic 0x32/0x1B) and 128 KiB (Macronix
0xC2/0x09) with ID mode, chip/sector erase, byte program and bank switching; EEPROM 512 B /
8 KiB serial protocol via DMA with automatic size detection. GPIO RTC (S-3511) at
0x080000C4/C6/C8: status, date/time and time commands, BCD from the host clock + offsets,
writes supported; enabled for game codes AXV*/AXP*/BPE* (and a few other RTC carts) or when the
ROM contains `SIIRTC_V`.

`/tmp/retra-test-roms` (never into the repo) and checks them. Last run: **74 passed, 0 failed**.

## Performance

Host: Intel Xeon @ 2.60 GHz (shared VM), g++ 14 `-O2`, single thread, headless:

| ROM | fps | x realtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mochi Hop gameplay | ~1300 | ~22x |
| Tonc `m7_ex` (mode 7, HBlank IRQ, sprites) | ~1050 | ~18x |

| armwrestler | ~1800 | ~30x |

The Android build uses `-O3`; a mid-range arm64 phone is expected to stay several times above
full speed.

## Known gaps

* Cycle accuracy is approximate (mGBA timing suite 1392/2020): no exact DMA/IRQ latencies,
  no per-scanline sprite cycle budget, the ARM7 multiply carry flag is left unchanged.
* Rendering is per scanline: register changes in the middle of a line take effect on the
  next line (HBlank/VCount raster effects work).
* Serial port: no link cable; transfers complete immediately with 0xFFFF data.
* BIOS sound-driver SWIs (0x1A-0x1E, 0x28-0x2A) are no-ops in the replacement BIOS (games
  using the BIOS music player need a user BIOS); Stop mode behaves like Halt.
* Colour correction is an approximation, not a measured LCD profile.

  **What works**
  - **CPU:** full ARM and THUMB instruction sets with the documented edge cases, all modes and exceptions, and decode lookup tables. Timing models wait states and the cartridge prefetch buffer. A tight loop that provably changes nothing is skipped ahead to the next hardware event, which is where most of the speed comes from.
  - **BIOS:** no Nintendo code. It's my own 836-byte BIOS assembled from `bios/retra_bios.S`, which handles interrupts and the wait/halt calls in real ARM code. Every other SWI on your list is done in C++. Boot goes straight to the cartridge with the post-BIOS register state. A user BIOS can be passed in, but the boot still skips its intro, because the intro refuses ROM hacks with bad header checksums.
  - **Video:** modes 0–5, text/affine/bitmap backgrounds, all sprite types, windows, blending, mosaic, and the VCOUNT/HBlank/VBlank timing. Optional colour correction.
  - **DMA, timers, sound:** all DMA modes including the sound-FIFO and video-capture ones, cascading timers, the four PSG channels plus both Direct Sound FIFOs, output at 32768 Hz stereo (548–549 samples per frame).
  - **Saves:** SRAM, Flash 64K/128K (128K reports Macronix 0xC2/0x09, with bank switching), and EEPROM with size detected from the first DMA. A game with no save tag that writes to SRAM becomes a 32K SRAM cart. The RTC is enabled for AXV/AXP/BPE game codes or a `SIIRTC_V` string.

args.content:
# Retra Game Library catalog

`manifest.json` is the online Game Library. The app fetches it from
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prashantchataut/Retra/main/catalog/manifest.json`.

## Content rules (hard)

- No commercial ROMs, ROM sites, pre-patched ROMs or Nintendo BIOS files. Ever.
- Pokémon fan games are listed only as **patches** (IPS/UPS/BPS). The user applies a patch to a
  base ROM they dumped themselves. The app checks the base ROM's CRC32 before patching.
- A direct `download` for a patch is listed only when the creator hosts the file at a stable HTTPS
  URL (for example a GitHub release asset or the creator's own site). If the patch is only on
  MediaFire, Google Drive, Mega, Ko-fi, PokéCommunity or Discord, `download` is `null` and the app
  opens `homepage` so the user can get it from the creator.
- Homebrew ROMs are direct downloads only when their license allows redistribution. The license is
  given in `license`, and `source` links to the listing that hosts the file.

## Top level

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "updated": "2026-10-19",
  "collections": [ Collection, ... ],
  "entries": [ Entry, ... ]
}
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | int | Format version. Currently `1`. Clients should ignore manifests with a higher major schema they don't understand. |
| `updated` | string | ISO date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) of the last edit. |
| `collections` | array | Shelves shown in the Library UI, in display order. |
| `entries` | array | All catalog items. |

## Collection

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | `featured`, `pokemon`, `challenge` or `homebrew`. |
| `title` | string | Shelf heading. |
| `subtitle` | string | Short line under the heading. |
| `entryIds` | string[] | Entry `id`s in display order. An entry may appear in several collections. |

## Entry

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Stable unique slug (`[a-z0-9-]`). Use it as the key for downloads and saves. |
| `kind` | `"rom"` \| `"patch"` | `rom` is a playable GBA image (or a zip containing one). `patch` must be applied to `base`. |
| `title` | string | Display title. |
| `author` | string | Creator(s). |
| `version` | string \| null | Latest known release. `null` means unknown, so check the homepage. |
| `description` | string | 1–2 sentences written for this catalog. |
| `tags` | string[] | Lower-case, hyphenated. |
| `status` | string | `complete`, `beta`, `in-development` or `archived`. |
| `license` | string \| null | SPDX identifier for redistributable content. `null` for ROM hacks, which are never redistributed by us. |
| `homepage` | string | Creator's official page or thread. Always present. The app opens it when `download` is `null`. |
| `source` | string \| null | Where the file listing or license metadata comes from, such as a Homebrew Hub page. Informational only. |
| `download` | Download \| null | Direct file. `null` means the user has to get it from `homepage`. |
| `patchFormat` | string \| null | Patches only: `ips`, `ups`, `bps`, or `xdelta` (shown for info only, since the app can't apply xdelta). `null` means unknown. Omitted for roms. |
| `base` | Base \| null | Patches only: the clean ROM the patch expects. `null` for roms. |
| `accent` | string | Pastel card colour `#RRGGBB` (upper-case hex). |
| `featured` | bool | Highlighted card. |
| `bundled` | bool | `true` if the APK also ships this file in assets (Mochi Hop), so the app can play it offline without downloading. |

### Download

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | HTTPS URL. |
| `size` | int | Exact byte size of the file at `url`. |
| `sha256` | string | Lower-case hex SHA-256 of the file at `url`. The client must reject a mismatch. |
| `format` | string | `gba`, `zip`, `ips`, `ups` or `bps`. |
| `archiveEntry` | string | Only when `format` is `zip`: the name of the single file to extract (`.gba`, `.ips`, `.ups` or `.bps`). |
| `archiveEntrySize` | int | Only for zip: byte size of `archiveEntry`. |
| `archiveEntrySha256` | string | Only for zip: SHA-256 of `archiveEntry`. |

### Base

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Human-readable name, region and revision. |
| `gameCode` | string | 4-char cartridge code from the ROM header at 0xAC (`BPEE`, `BPRE`, `AXVE`, ...). |
| `crc32` | string | CRC32 of the whole clean ROM, 8 upper-case hex chars. |
| `size` | int | Byte size of the clean ROM. |

Known bases (all 16,777,216 bytes):

| ROM | Code | CRC32 |
|---|---|---|
| Emerald (U) | BPEE | `1F1C08FB` |
| FireRed (U) v1.0 | BPRE | `DD88761C` |
| FireRed (U) v1.1 | BPRE | `84EE4776` |
| LeafGreen (U) v1.0 | BPGE | `D69C96CC` |
| Ruby (U) v1.0 | AXVE | `F0815EE7` |
| Sapphire (U) v1.0 | AXPE | `554DEDC4` |

## Client behaviour

1. If `download` is present, download it, then check `size` and `sha256`. For zips, extract
   `archiveEntry` and check it too.
2. For a `patch`, ask the user for their base ROM and compare its CRC32 with `base.crc32`.
   UPS and BPS patches also carry the source CRC32 in their footer, and it should match.
   If it doesn't match, explain which revision is needed.
3. If `download` is `null`, show a "Get from creator" button that opens `homepage`, then let the
   user import the patch file they downloaded.

## Maintaining

- Every URL must be checked by hand before it is added. PokéCommunity, Ko-fi and romhacking.net
  answer scripted requests with HTTP 403 (bot protection), but they work in a browser.
- Download each new file to a scratch directory outside the repo, record `size` and `sha256`, and
  for UPS/BPS confirm the embedded source CRC32 matches `base.crc32`.
- Bump `updated` on every change. Never add pre-patched ROMs or links to ROM sites.

Write from scratch (no third-party libs) a robust, fast patch engine for GBA ROM hacks (Pokémon fan games are 16–32 MiB):
- IPS (incl. RLE records, EOF marker, optional truncate extension, outputs larger than source)
- UPS (varint, XOR blocks, source/target/patch CRC32 verification)
- BPS (SourceRead/TargetRead/SourceCopy/TargetCopy, metadata, CRC32 checks)
- VCDIFF / xdelta3 decoder (RFC 3284: header indicator, secondary compression flag -> report unsupported if secondary compressor is used, code table default, address cache near/same, VCD_SOURCE windows, VCD_ADLER32 checksum extension xdelta uses) — many fan games ship as .xdelta.
- ZIP handling: given a .zip, find the single patch/ROM entry (by extension .ips/.ups/.bps/.xdelta/.vcdiff/.gba) using java.util.zip.
- CRC32 helper (java.util.zip.CRC32 is fine) and SHA-1/SHA-256 helpers.
- Patch creation for BPS is a nice-to-have (skip if time is short).

Public API (the app codes against exactly this; keep it):
```kotlin
enum class PatchFormat { IPS, UPS, BPS, VCDIFF }
data class PatchInfo(val format: PatchFormat, val sourceSize: Long?, val targetSize: Long?, val sourceCrc32: Long?, val targetCrc32: Long?, val metadata: String?)
sealed interface PatchResult {
  data class Ok(val output: ByteArray, val info: PatchInfo, val warnings: List<String>) : PatchResult
  data class Error(val code: PatchError, val message: String) : PatchResult
}
enum class PatchError { UNKNOWN_FORMAT, CORRUPT_PATCH, SOURCE_MISMATCH, TARGET_MISMATCH, PATCH_CHECKSUM, UNSUPPORTED }
object Patcher {
  fun detect(patch: ByteArray): PatchFormat?
  fun inspect(patch: ByteArray): PatchInfo?
  fun apply(source: ByteArray, patch: ByteArray, strict: Boolean = true, progress: ((Float) -> Unit)? = null): PatchResult
     // strict=false lets the user force-apply when the source CRC doesn't match (returns warning instead of error where possible)
}
object Checksums { fun crc32(b: ByteArray): Long; fun sha1Hex(b: ByteArray): String; fun sha256Hex(b: ByteArray): String; fun crc32Hex(b: ByteArray): String /* 8 uppercase hex */ }
object PatchArchive { fun extractSingle(zip: ByteArray): Pair<String, ByteArray>? /* name, bytes of best entry */ }
```
Error messages must be human-friendly (they're shown in the UI), e.g. "This patch expects a different base game (needs CRC32 1F1C08FB, you picked 7A2F…)".

# :patcher

Pure Kotlin/JVM ROM-hack patch engine (package `app.retra.patcher`), no third-party dependencies.

## Formats

| Format | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| IPS    | Normal + RLE records, `EOF` marker, Lunar IPS truncate extension, growing outputs. A missing `EOF` is a warning. |
| UPS    | Varint/XOR records, source/target/patch CRC32. It can also be applied in reverse (patched ROM -> original). |
| BPS    | All four actions, metadata (`PatchInfo.metadata`), CRC32 checks. `BpsCreator.create()` builds patches. |
| VCDIFF / xdelta3 | RFC 3284 with the default code table, near/same address cache, `VCD_SOURCE`/`VCD_TARGET` windows, xdelta's `VCD_ADLER32` per-window checksum and app header (`metadata`). Supports **LZMA secondary compression**, which Linux/Debian builds of `xdelta3 -e` use by default. DJW/FGK secondary compressors (`-S djw`/`-S fgk`) and custom code tables return `UNSUPPORTED`. |

## API

```kotlin
Patcher.detect(patch)            // PatchFormat? (by magic)
Patcher.inspect(patch)           // PatchInfo? (sizes, CRCs, metadata), no source needed
Patcher.apply(source, patch, strict = true, progress = { f -> })   // PatchResult.Ok / PatchResult.Error
Checksums.crc32 / crc32Hex / sha1Hex / sha256Hex
PatchArchive.extractSingle(zipBytes)   // best entry: .bps > .ups > .xdelta/.vcdiff > .ips > .gba, then any entry that looks like a patch
BpsCreator.create(source, target, metadata)
```

`PatchResult.Error.message` is written for end users and can go straight into the UI. With

# Retra engine

`:engine` is Retra's Game Boy Advance emulator: a C++17 core written from scratch for this
project, a JNI bridge, and the Kotlin API the app codes against (`app.retra.engine`).
No code from other emulators is used; hardware behaviour was implemented from public
documentation (GBATEK, Tonc) and verified with freely licensed test ROMs.

```
engine/
  src/main/cpp/core/          pure C++17 core (no JNI / Android headers)
  src/main/cpp/jni/           retra_jni.cpp  (JNI bridge, no C++ exceptions)
  src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt -> libretra_engine.so (always -O3, 16 KiB page aligned)
  src/main/kotlin/app/retra/engine/  GbaCore, GbaKey, SaveType, RomInfo, LoadResult
  host/                       retra-headless runner, test scripts, own test ROM sources
```

## Kotlin API

Exactly the contract in `docs/REBUILD_PLAN.md`. Notes on semantics:

* `GbaCore` is not thread-safe; use one emulation thread. `close()` is idempotent.
* `loadRom(rom, bios)`: ROMs up to 32 MiB. `bios == null` uses Retra's own replacement BIOS
  (see below); a user BIOS must be exactly 16 KiB. Boot always goes straight to the cartridge
  (the BIOS intro would refuse ROM hacks with a bad header checksum).
* `runFrame(video, audio)`: runs until the next VBlank; writes 240x160 `0xFFRRGGBB` pixels and
  returns the number of stereo s16 frames written (548-549 at 32768 Hz). The buffers are
  validated in Kotlin (`video.size >= 38400`, `audio.size >= 4096`).
* `RomInfo.saveType` is detected from the library ID strings (`SRAM_V`, `SRAM_F_V`, `FLASH_V`,
  `FLASH512_V`, `FLASH1M_V`, `EEPROM_V`). `AUTO` is reported for EEPROM games: the 512 B /
  8 KiB size is decided from the first DMA transfer to the EEPROM. Games without a tag that
  write to the SRAM area become 32 KiB SRAM carts on the fly (homebrew convention).
* `batterySave()` returns raw `.sav` contents (SRAM 32 KiB, Flash 64/128 KiB, EEPROM 512 B /
  8 KiB, EEPROM bytes in transmission order). `loadBatterySave()` accepts the same and adapts
  Flash/EEPROM size to the file size (common emulator `.sav` files load directly).
* `saveState()` is a versioned binary blob (`RTAS` magic, version 1, game ID check). It
  contains the save memory, so restoring a state also restores the battery contents (and
  sets the dirty flag). A rejected state leaves the running game untouched.
* `setCheats(list)` returns the number of accepted code lines; each list entry may contain
  several lines. Formats: raw `AAAAAAAA:VV|VVVV|VVVVVVVV`, CodeBreaker `XXXXXXXX YYYY`
  (unencrypted), GameShark/Action Replay v1/v2 and Pro Action Replay v3 `XXXXXXXX YYYYYYYY`
  (encrypted, auto-detected; prefix an entry with `GS:` or `AR:` to force). Supported code
  types: writes, fills/slides, add/or/and, conditionals, AR indirect writes and IO writes, ROM
  patches (GS `6`, AR `18..1E`). Not supported: encrypted CodeBreaker (`9...` seed codes) and the
  GS/AR `DEADFACE` seed change (needs device-internal tables); such lines are rejected.
* `setRtcOffsetSeconds()` shifts the cartridge clock relative to the host clock. If the game
  sets the clock itself, that adjustment is kept (and saved in states).

## Architecture

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `gba.h/.cpp` | facade: load/reset, frame loop, event dispatch, IRQ line, save states |
| `scheduler.h` | fixed-slot event scheduler (HBlank, line end, timers, audio sample) |
| `cpu.h/.cpp`, `cpu_arm.cpp`, `cpu_thumb.cpp`, `cpu_shift.h` | ARM7TDMI interpreter |
| `bus.h/.cpp`, `bus_inl.h` | memory map, wait states, GamePak prefetch, open bus, IO registers |
| `ppu.h/.cpp` | scanline renderer |
| `apu.h/.cpp` | PSG 1-4, Direct Sound A/B, mixer |
| `dma.h/.cpp`, `timer.h/.cpp` | DMA 0-3, timers 0-3 |
| `bios/retra_bios.S`, `bios_image.h`, `bios_hle.cpp` | replacement BIOS + HLE SWIs |
| `cart_save.h/.cpp` | SRAM / Flash / EEPROM |
| `rtc.h/.cpp` | GPIO port + Seiko S-3511 RTC |
| `cheats.h/.cpp` | cheat engine |
| `state.h` | serialization helpers |

**CPU.** Full ARMv4T: all data-processing ops with barrel-shifter edge cases (LSL/LSR/ASR #32,
RRX, register shifts >= 32, PC+12 with register shifts), multiplies (incl. long), single /
halfword / signed transfers with ARM7 misaligned-load rotation, SWP, LDM/STM quirks (empty list,
base in list, user-bank transfer, S-bit CPSR restore), MRS/MSR with field masks, BX, SWI,
undefined-instruction trap, all banked modes. Decoding uses 4096-entry (ARM, bits 27-20/7-4)
and 1024-entry (THUMB, bits 15-6) tables of template-specialised handlers generated at compile
time. A real two-stage prefetch pipeline is modelled (self-modifying code, BIOS open bus).
Cycle counting uses per-region N/S wait states from WAITCNT, internal cycles for
multiplies/loads/register shifts, branch refills, the "first fetch after a data access /
internal cycle is non-sequential" rule, and a GamePak prefetch-buffer model (the prefetcher
reads ahead one halfword per S-cycle while the CPU is busy elsewhere).
Short backward branches run an idle-loop detector: if a loop iteration leaves registers,
flags and memory unchanged (and reads no free-running timer), time skips to the next event.

**Memory.** BIOS read protection (returns the last BIOS opcode fetched), EWRAM/IWRAM/palette/
VRAM/OAM mirroring, VRAM 0x18000-0x1FFFF mirror, byte-write rules (palette/VRAM duplicate,
OAM/OBJ-VRAM ignore), ROM up to 32 MiB with out-of-range open-bus pattern (the ROM buffer
is pre-filled so reads need no bounds check), SRAM-bus rules (8-bit bus, unaligned byte
selection), CPU open bus for unmapped areas and write-only IO registers.

**BIOS.** No Nintendo code is shipped. `bios/retra_bios.S` is an original 836-byte BIOS
(assembled with `bios/build_bios.sh`, output committed as `bios_image.h`): exception vectors,
an IRQ dispatcher that saves r0-r3/r12/lr and calls `[0x03FFFFFC]`, the SWI dispatcher,
Halt/Stop/CustomHalt/IntrWait/VBlankIntrWait as real ARM code (using BIOS IF at 0x03FFFFF8),
and placement of the well-known open-bus values (0xE129F000 after boot, 0xE25EF004 during IRQ,
0xE55EC002 after IRQ, 0xE3A02004 after SWI). Other SWIs trap into C++ (`bios_hle.cpp`):
SoftReset, RegisterRamReset, Div, DivArm, Sqrt, ArcTan, ArcTan2 (bit-exact incl. r1/r3),
CpuSet, CpuFastSet, GetBiosChecksum, BgAffineSet, ObjAffineSet, BitUnPack, LZ77UnComp
(WRAM/VRAM), HuffUnComp, RLUnComp (WRAM/VRAM), Diff8bitUnFilter (WRAM/VRAM),
Diff16bitUnFilter, SoundBias, MidiKey2Freq, MultiBoot (fails: no link), HardReset.
A user-supplied BIOS replaces all of this.

**PPU.** Scanline renderer run at the end of each H-draw: modes 0-5; text BGs (all sizes,
4/8 bpp, flips), affine BGs (wraparound, internal reference points latched at VBlank and on
register writes, advanced by PB/PD per line so HBlank-DMA "mode 7" works), bitmap modes 3/4/5
(page flip, affine transformed), sprites (normal/affine/double size, 1D/2D mapping, OBJ window,
semi-transparency, priority vs. BGs, bitmap-mode tile limit), windows 0/1/OBJ/outside, alpha /
brighten / darken blending, BG and OBJ mosaic, forced blank, DISPSTAT/VCOUNT flags and IRQs
(1232 cycles/line, HBlank at cycle 1006, 228 lines). Composition is a branch-free painter's
algorithm on packed (layer, colour) lanes. Output ARGB8888; optional LCD colour correction
(gamma + channel cross-talk approximation).

**DMA / timers.** DMA 0-3: immediate, VBlank, HBlank, sound FIFO (4 words, fixed destination),
video capture (DMA3, lines 2-161); address control incl. increment/reload, repeat, 16/32 bit,
IRQ, forced address alignment, ROM sources always increment, DMA open bus, EEPROM size hint.
Timers: prescalers, cascade, IRQ, 2-cycle start delay, lazily evaluated counters with events
only scheduled when something observes the overflow.

**APU.** PSG square 1 (sweep) and 2, wave (two banks, 32/64 samples, volume codes, force 75%),
noise (7/15-bit LFSR), envelopes, length counters, 512 Hz frame sequencer; PSG output is
integrated over each 512-cycle output period (band-limits high tones). Direct Sound A/B 32-byte
FIFOs driven by timer 0/1 overflow with DMA refill requests, sample-and-hold like hardware.
SOUNDCNT_L/H/X and SOUNDBIAS mixing into 10 bits then s16 stereo at 32768 Hz.

**Saves / RTC.** SRAM 32 KiB; Flash 64 KiB (Panasonic 0x32/0x1B) and 128 KiB (Macronix
0xC2/0x09) with ID mode, chip/sector erase, byte program and bank switching; EEPROM 512 B /
8 KiB serial protocol via DMA with automatic size detection. GPIO RTC (S-3511) at
0x080000C4/C6/C8: status, date/time and time commands, BCD from the host clock + offsets,
writes supported; enabled for game codes AXV*/AXP*/BPE* (and a few other RTC carts) or when the
ROM contains `SIIRTC_V`.

## Performance

Host: Intel Xeon @ 2.60 GHz (shared VM), g++ 14 `-O2`, single thread, headless:

| ROM | fps | x realtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mochi Hop gameplay | ~1400 | ~23x |
| Tonc `m7_ex` (mode 7, HBlank IRQ, sprites) | ~1050 | ~18x |
| Tonc `obj_aff` / `bld_demo` | ~1700 / ~1500 | ~28x / 25x |
| armwrestler | ~1800 | ~30x |
| Synthetic worst case (`host/testroms/bench_test.c`: CPU never idles, 4 text BGs, 128 sprites, alpha blending on every pixel) | ~560 | ~9x |

The Android build uses `-O3`; it compiles warning-free with NDK r27c clang for arm64-v8a,
armeabi-v7a and x86_64 (only the 16 JNI symbols are exported, 16 KiB segment alignment).
A mid-range arm64 phone is expected to stay several times above full speed.

## Known gaps

* Cycle accuracy is approximate (mGBA timing suite 1392/2020): no exact DMA/IRQ latencies,
  no per-scanline sprite cycle budget, the ARM7 multiply carry flag is left unchanged.
* Rendering is per scanline: register changes in the middle of a line take effect on the
  next line (HBlank/VCount raster effects work).
* Serial port: no link cable; transfers complete immediately with 0xFFFF data.
* BIOS sound-driver SWIs (0x1A-0x1E, 0x28-0x2A) are no-ops in the replacement BIOS (games
  using the BIOS music player need a user BIOS); Stop mode behaves like Halt.
* Colour correction is an approximation, not a measured LCD profile.
package app.retra.engine

/**
 * Game Boy Advance emulator core (native, `libretra_engine.so`).
 *
 * NOT thread-safe: create it, load ROMs, run frames and query it from a single emulation thread.
 * Call [close] when done to release native memory (~35 MiB while a ROM is loaded).
 */
class GbaCore : AutoCloseable {

    companion object {
        const val WIDTH = 240
        const val HEIGHT = 160
        const val SAMPLE_RATE = 32768
        const val FRAME_RATE = 59.7275
        const val MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES = 2048

        init {
            System.loadLibrary("retra_engine")
        }

        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeCreate(): Long
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeDestroy(handle: Long)
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeLoadRom(handle: Long, rom: ByteArray, bios: ByteArray?): String?
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeRomInfo(handle: Long): Array<String>?
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeEepromSizeUnknown(handle: Long): Boolean
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeReset(handle: Long)
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeSetKeys(handle: Long, mask: Int)
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeRunFrame(handle: Long, video: IntArray, audio: ShortArray): Int
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeBatterySave(handle: Long): ByteArray?
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeLoadBatterySave(handle: Long, data: ByteArray): Boolean
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeConsumeSaveDirty(handle: Long): Boolean
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeSaveState(handle: Long): ByteArray
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeLoadState(handle: Long, state: ByteArray): Boolean
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeSetCheats(handle: Long, codes: Array<String>): Int
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeSetColorCorrection(handle: Long, enabled: Boolean)
        @JvmStatic private external fun nativeSetRtcOffsetSeconds(handle: Long, offset: Long)
    }

    private var handle: Long = nativeCreate()
    private var romLoaded = false

    init {
        check(handle != 0L) { "Unable to allocate the emulator core" }
    }

    private fun requireOpen(): Long {
        check(handle != 0L) { "GbaCore is closed" }
        return handle
    }

    /** Loads a ROM. [bios] null -> built-in replacement BIOS; otherwise a 16 KiB BIOS image. */
    fun loadRom(rom: ByteArray, bios: ByteArray? = null): LoadResult {
        val h = requireOpen()
        val error = nativeLoadRom(h, rom, bios)
        if (error != null) {
            romLoaded = false
            return LoadResult.Error(error)
        }
        romLoaded = true
        val f = nativeRomInfo(h) ?: return LoadResult.Error("ROM information unavailable")
        val saveOrdinal = f[4].toIntOrNull() ?: 0
        var saveType = SaveType.entries.getOrElse(saveOrdinal) { SaveType.NONE }
        if ((saveType == SaveType.EEPROM_8K || saveType == SaveType.EEPROM_512) && nativeEepromSizeUnknown(h)) {
            saveType = SaveType.AUTO
        }
        return LoadResult.Ok(
            RomInfo(
                title = f[0],
                gameCode = f[1],
                makerCode = f[2],
                version = f[3].toIntOrNull() ?: 0,
                saveType = saveType,
                hasRtc = f[5] == "1",
            ),
        )
    }

    /** Power-cycles the console (battery save contents are kept). */
    fun reset() = nativeReset(requireOpen())

    /** Sets the pressed buttons ([GbaKey] bits, 1 = pressed). */
    fun setKeys(mask: Int) = nativeSetKeys(requireOpen(), mask)

    /**
     * Emulates one video frame.
     * @param video at least 240*160 pixels, receives ARGB_8888 (0xFFRRGGBB)
     * @param audio interleaved stereo s16, size >= 2 * [MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES]
     * @return number of stereo audio frames written (about 548-549 per video frame)
     */
    fun runFrame(video: IntArray, audio: ShortArray): Int {
        require(video.size >= WIDTH * HEIGHT) { "video buffer must hold ${WIDTH * HEIGHT} pixels" }
        require(audio.size >= 2 * MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES) { "audio buffer must hold ${2 * MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES} samples" }
        val h = requireOpen()
        if (!romLoaded) return 0
        return nativeRunFrame(h, video, audio)
    }

    /** Current battery save contents, or null when the game has no backup memory. */
    fun batterySave(): ByteArray? = nativeBatterySave(requireOpen())

    /** Imports a battery save (.sav). Returns false if the game has no backup memory. */
    fun loadBatterySave(data: ByteArray): Boolean = nativeLoadBatterySave(requireOpen(), data)

    /** True once after the game wrote to its backup memory (persist [batterySave] then). */
    fun consumeSaveDirty(): Boolean = nativeConsumeSaveDirty(requireOpen())

    /** Serializes the complete machine state (versioned format). */
    fun saveState(): ByteArray = nativeSaveState(requireOpen())

    /** Restores a state produced by [saveState] for the same game. */
    fun loadState(state: ByteArray): Boolean = nativeLoadState(requireOpen(), state)

    /**
     * Replaces the active cheat list. Supports raw "AAAAAAAA:VV/VVVV/VVVVVVVV", CodeBreaker
     * "XXXXXXXX YYYY", and encrypted GameShark v1/v2 / Action Replay v3 "XXXXXXXX YYYYYYYY"
     * (auto-detected; prefix "GS:" or "AR:" to force). An entry may hold several lines.
     * @return number of accepted code lines
     */
    fun setCheats(codes: List<String>): Int = nativeSetCheats(requireOpen(), codes.toTypedArray())

    /** Enables an approximation of the GBA LCD's gamma/colour response. */
    fun setColorCorrection(enabled: Boolean) = nativeSetColorCorrection(requireOpen(), enabled)

    /** Offset added to the host clock for the cartridge real-time clock. */
    fun setRtcOffsetSeconds(offset: Long) = nativeSetRtcOffsetSeconds(requireOpen(), offset)

    override fun close() {
        val h = handle
        if (h != 0L) {
            handle = 0L
            romLoaded = false
            nativeDestroy(h)
        }
    }
}

# Retra 4 — rebuild plan (shared contract for all contributors)

Repo: /workspace/Retra (branch `rebuild/retra-4`). Old app snapshot for reference only: /tmp/old/Retra.

## Product
Retra is a GBA emulator app for Android, built for its author and community, focused on playing
Pokémon games, Pokémon fan games (ROM-hack patches) and homebrew. Everything is built from scratch:
UI/UX, logo, mascot, emulation engine, patcher, and an original bundled game.

Content rules (hard): never bundle or download commercial ROMs or Nintendo BIOS. Fan games are
distributed as patches (IPS/UPS/BPS) that the user applies to their own base ROM. Direct downloads
are allowed only for content whose license permits redistribution (homebrew, our own game).

## Repository layout
```
settings.gradle.kts / build.gradle.kts / gradle/libs.versions.toml / gradlew
app/        Android app, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, package app.retra
engine/     Android library :engine, namespace app.retra.engine
  src/main/cpp/core/     pure C++17 GBA core, no Android/JNI includes
  src/main/cpp/jni/      JNI bridge (retra_jni.cpp)
  src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt  -> shared lib "retra_engine"
  src/main/kotlin/app/retra/engine/   Kotlin API (GbaCore, GbaKey, ...)
  host/      CMake host build: retra-headless runner + tests (Linux, g++)
patcher/    Kotlin/JVM library :patcher, package app.retra.patcher (IPS/UPS/BPS, CRC32)
game/       Original GBA game "Mochi Hop" (C, arm-none-eabi-gcc), build.sh
            output ROM -> app/src/main/assets/games/mochi_hop.gba
catalog/    manifest.json — online Game Library, fetched from
            https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prashantchataut/Retra/main/catalog/manifest.json
docs/
```

## Design direction (app)
- Tone: Playful-soft, cute 2D, with a liquid-glass material. Signature: the mascot **Mochi**
  (a round, squishy rice-cake creature) + glossy liquid-glass surfaces with a specular rim and a
  floating glass dock whose indicator morphs like liquid.
- Type: Fredoka (display, rounded) + Nunito (body). Both OFL, bundled.
- Palette: neutrals tinted warm (light "cloud cream") / cool indigo (dark "night"), one accent
  "Mochi pink" plus semantic colours. Pastel ambient sky behind glass.
- Motion: spring-based, restrained (no bounce on everything), respects reduced motion.
- The original game **Mochi Hop** stars the same mascot.

# Retra Game Library catalog

`manifest.json` is the online Game Library. The app fetches it from
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prashantchataut/Retra/main/catalog/manifest.json`.

## Content rules (hard)

- No commercial ROMs, ROM sites, pre-patched ROMs or Nintendo BIOS files. Ever.
- Pokémon fan games are listed only as **patches** (IPS/UPS/BPS). The user applies a patch to a
  base ROM they dumped themselves. The app checks the base ROM's CRC32 before patching.
- A direct `download` for a patch is listed only when the creator hosts the file at a stable HTTPS
  URL (for example a GitHub release asset or the creator's own site). If the patch is only on
  MediaFire, Google Drive, Mega, Ko-fi, PokéCommunity or Discord, `download` is `null` and the app
  opens `homepage` so the user can get it from the creator.
- Homebrew ROMs are direct downloads only when their license allows redistribution. The license is
  given in `license`, and `source` links to the listing that hosts the file.

## Top level

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "updated": "2026-10-19",
  "collections": [ Collection, ... ],
  "entries": [ Entry, ... ]
}
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | int | Format version. Currently `1`. Clients should ignore manifests with a higher major schema they don't understand. |
| `updated` | string | ISO date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) of the last edit. |
| `collections` | array | Shelves shown in the Library UI, in display order. |
| `entries` | array | All catalog items. |

## Collection

| Field | Type | Notes |

| `id` | string | `featured`, `pokemon`, `challenge` or `homebrew`. |
| `title` | string | Shelf heading. |
| `subtitle` | string | Short line under the heading. |
| `entryIds` | string[] | Entry `id`s in display order. An entry may appear in several collections. |

## Entry

| `id` | string | Stable unique slug (`[a-z0-9-]`). Use it as the key for downloads and saves. |
