| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Stable unique slug (`[a-z0-9-]`). Use it as the key for downloads and saves. |
| `kind` | `"rom"` \| `"patch"` | `rom` is a playable GBA image (or a zip containing one). `patch` must be applied to `base`. |
| `title` | string | Display title. |
| `author` | string | Creator(s). |
| `version` | string \| null | Latest known release. `null` means unknown, so check the homepage. |
| `description` | string | 1–2 sentences written for this catalog. |
| `tags` | string[] | Lower-case, hyphenated. |
| `status` | string | `complete`, `beta`, `in-development` or `archived`. |
| `license` | string \| null | SPDX identifier for redistributable content. `null` for ROM hacks, which are never redistributed by us. |
| `homepage` | string | Creator's official page or thread. Always present. The app opens it when `download` is `null`. |
| `source` | string \| null | Where the file listing or license metadata comes from, such as a Homebrew Hub page. Informational only. |
| `download` | Download \| null | Direct file. `null` means the user has to get it from `homepage`. |
| `patchFormat` | string \| null | Patches only: `ips`, `ups`, `bps`, or `xdelta` (shown for info only, since the app can't apply xdelta). `null` means unknown. Omitted for roms. |
| `base` | Base \| null | Patches only: the clean ROM the patch expects. `null` for roms. |
| `accent` | string | Pastel card colour `#RRGGBB` (upper-case hex). |
| `featured` | bool | Highlighted card. |
| `bundled` | bool | `true` if the APK also ships this file in assets (Mochi Hop), so the app can play it offline without downloading. |

### Download

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | HTTPS URL. |
| `size` | int | Exact byte size of the file at `url`. |
| `sha256` | string | Lower-case hex SHA-256 of the file at `url`. The client must reject a mismatch. |
| `format` | string | `gba`, `zip`, `ips`, `ups` or `bps`. |
| `archiveEntry` | string | Only when `format` is `zip`: the name of the single file to extract (`.gba`, `.ips`, `.ups` or `.bps`). |
| `archiveEntrySize` | int | Only for zip: byte size of `archiveEntry`. |
| `archiveEntrySha256` | string | Only for zip: SHA-256 of `archiveEntry`. |

### Base

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Human-readable name, region and revision. |
| `gameCode` | string | 4-char cartridge code from the ROM header at 0xAC (`BPEE`, `BPRE`, `AXVE`, ...). |
| `crc32` | string | CRC32 of the whole clean ROM, 8 upper-case hex chars. |
| `size` | int | Byte size of the clean ROM. |

Known bases (all 16,777,216 bytes):

| ROM | Code | CRC32 |
|---|---|---|
| Emerald (U) | BPEE | `1F1C08FB` |
| FireRed (U) v1.0 | BPRE | `DD88761C` |
| FireRed (U) v1.1 | BPRE | `84EE4776` |
| LeafGreen (U) v1.0 | BPGE | `D69C96CC` |
| Ruby (U) v1.0 | AXVE | `F0815EE7` |
| Sapphire (U) v1.0 | AXPE | `554DEDC4` |

## Client behaviour

1. If `download` is present, download it, then check `size` and `sha256`. For zips, extract
   `archiveEntry` and check it too.
2. For a `patch`, ask the user for their base ROM and compare its CRC32 with `base.crc32`.
   UPS and BPS patches also carry the source CRC32 in their footer, and it should match.
   If it doesn't match, explain which revision is needed.
3. If `download` is `null`, show a "Get from creator" button that opens `homepage`, then let the
   user import the patch file they downloaded.

## Maintaining

- Every URL must be checked by hand before it is added. PokéCommunity, Ko-fi and romhacking.net
  answer scripted requests with HTTP 403 (bot protection), but they work in a browser.
- Download each new file to a scratch directory outside the repo, record `size` and `sha256`, and
  for UPS/BPS confirm the embedded source CRC32 matches `base.crc32`.
- Bump `updated` on every change. Never add pre-patched ROMs or links to ROM sites.

Keep reading in chunks to the end (review path, Constraints, build path, report, reference map) before you start. # Design Taste Taste here means **one clear direction, few well-chosen tokens, strong hierarchy, and no default-looking filler**. Every mode runs Steps 0–2, then the **review path (R3–R6)** or the **build path (B3–B7)**, then the **final report**. Step labels are for your tracking; don't paste them into the deliverable. ## Step 0 — Intake and mode - **Do:** read the request and artifacts (code, URL, image). Pick one primary mode (+ overlay) below; the full table with mode-specific steps is `references/modes.md`. - **Output:** mode, overlay, path, reference files to load. - **Decision:** critique/score/benchmark only → review path; create or change something visible → build path; Redesign = review path as audit, then build path. No visible output (backend, cleanup) → this skill doesn't apply. | Mode | Path | Load | |---|---|---| | Audit (UI/code review) | Review | `audit.md` | | Site Review (URL, 对标) | Review | `site-review.md`, `benchmarks.md`, run `scripts/review_site.py` | | Image Review (photo/poster/AI image) | Review | `image-aesthetics.md`, run `scripts/review_image.py --type photo\|product\|poster\|social\|ui\|illustration\|figure\|ai` | | Game Art Review | Review | `game-aesthetics.md`, `game-workflows.md`, run `review_image.py --type game-screenshot\|key-art\|capsule\|icon\|game-ui\|concept\|sprite --genre ` | | Redesign | Review → Build | `audit.md`, then `redesign.md` | | Create (page/app/component) | Build | `direction.md`, `principles.md`, `tokens.md` | | Theme (slides/docs) | Build | `theming.md` | | Artifact (poster/cover PNG/PDF) | Build | `artifacts.md` | | Image Restyle / palette / figures | Build | `image-workflows.md` | | Minimalist (overlay) | Same | `minimalist.md` | ## Step 1 — Gather context - **Do:** find stack, CSS approach, existing tokens/design system, brand, constraints. Get baseline numbers: `review_site.py` for URLs, `review_image.py --type … [--genre …]` for images (`--lang zh` for Chinese users). If OCR (`tesseract`) is available, read the text in images with it. - **Output:** short context note + baseline metrics (or "no tooling — visual judgment only"). - **Done when:** you know what exists and must be preserved. Missing artifact → ask for it. ## Step 2 — Decide a direction - **Do:** write 3–5 lines before building or scoring: purpose & audience; **one tone** ("clean and modern" is not a tone); **one signature**; constraints; density. Review path: the direction *as perceived* is the yardstick. - **Output:** the direction block (`direction.md` §5); for build tasks show it to the user before the first file write. - **Done when:** it names one tone and one signature; an existing design system means "follow it well". ## Review path (Audit, Site Review, Image Review, Game Art Review; first half of Redesign) ### R3 — Measure - **Do:** run the mode's measurable checks: `audit.md` §1 grep counts (distinct hex colors, font sizes, radii, shadows), `review_site.py`, or `review_image.py` (+ grayscale/thumbnail for games). Never modify the artifact under review. - **Output:** metrics table with real counts. - **Done when:** every metric the report template needs has a number or "not measurable: why". ### R4 — Score - **Do:** score with the mode's rubric (`audit.md` §2, `site-review.md` §2, `image-aesthetics.md` 8 dims + AI checklist, `game-aesthetics.md` G1–G11); combine metric and visual scores as the reference says. - **Output:** per-dimension scores with concrete evidence. - **Done when:** every dimension has score + evidence; any P0 caps the total per the rubric. ### R5 — Compare (Site Review and Game Art Review only) - **Do:** compare with `benchmarks.md`/`benchmarks.csv` or the genre profile. **Output:** gap table + 2–3 takeaways. **Done when:** each gap names the benchmark value. ### R6 — Prioritize - **Do:** P0/P1/P2 issues, each with what, where (file:line / region), why, concrete fix (token values, HEX, crop, prompt). - **Output:** prioritized list. **Done when:** every item has where/why/fix. Redesign → B3; else → final report. ## Constraints (checked in B6 and in reviews) ### Core rules (always on) - **Commit.** A bold minimal design and a maximal one are both fine; a timid average of everything is not. - **Tokens, not literals.** Every color, size, radius, shadow, and duration comes from a small named scale (see `references/tokens.md`). - **Restraint in counts:** ~1 accent color, 1–2 typefaces, ≤ 6–8 font sizes, one radius family, ≤ 3 shadow levels, one easing curve family. - **Hierarchy through contrast** of size, weight, and space — not more boxes, borders, and colors. - **Spacing on a grid** (4/8px base). Group related things tightly, separate groups generously. - **Accessibility is part of taste:** text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (3:1 large), visible focus, hit targets ≥ 44px on touch, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. - **Real content.** No "John Doe / Acme / Lorem ipsum", no "Elevate your workflow" copy, no emoji as icons. - **Every state exists:** hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, empty, error. ### AI-slop fingerprint (avoid unless the brief explicitly calls for it) - Purple→blue gradients on white; neon glows on dark; gradient text everywhere. - Inter/Roboto/Arial by reflex; one weight for everything. - Centered hero + three identical icon cards + generic CTA band. - Cards nested in cards; every element in a rounded bordered box with a drop shadow. - Glassmorphism for no reason; random decorative blobs. - Uniform `rounded-2xl` + `shadow-lg` on everything; inconsistent radii. - Fake metrics ("10x faster", "99.9%") and stock testimonials. - Bouncy/elastic animation on everything; animating layout properties. Details and alternatives: `references/principles.md`. ## Build path (Create, Redesign, Theme, Artifact, Image Restyle) ### B3 — Budget and plan - **Do:** plan so a **complete, valid first version exists by about 40% of your step/time budget** (roughly 15 tool calls or 8 minutes for a page or poster). Write the main file in 1–3 writes, not dozens of appends. Polish only after the complete version renders. - **Output:** a section list (page), or for a poster the **exact copy written out with a word count** (≤ 25 words total, small print included; don't invent extra details such as prices, addresses, lineups or series numbers the user didn't give) plus 2–4 colors + neutrals. Fonts for either: at most 2 families in total — a monospace or label face counts as one. - **Done when:** the plan fits the budget and the poster copy count is ≤ 25; anything that doesn't fit is cut now, not later. ### B4 — Tokens first - **Do:** a small named scale for color, type, spacing, radius, shadow, motion as CSS variables / theme config (`tokens.md`); Minimalist: `minimalist.md` values. - **Output:** token block. **Done when:** ≈1 accent, 1–2 typefaces, ≤ 6–8 sizes, one radius family, ≤ 3 shadows. ### B5 — Execute the complete version - **Do:** build global layer → every planned section/element → states, using only tokens, in the user's stack; include `prefers-reduced-motion` and the closing tags in the first pass. Artifacts: render the PNG/PDF now. - **Output:** the complete file(s) / rendered artifact. - **Done when:** the whole scope exists and renders (HTML ends with ``, the PDF opens). Then B6 — no polishing before this. ### B6 — Hard checks - **Do:** walk the Constraints line by line, then measure: hex/font-size/radius counts; distinct font families (≤ 2, monospace included); contrast; screenshot at ~375/1280px. **Posters/artifacts:** list every text string on the canvas and count its words (letter-spaced or outlined text still counts; `pdftotext` misses outlined text, so count from your source file) — must be ≤ 25 unless the brief supplies more copy; over → delete lines, don't shrink them; count dominant colors in the render (≥ 2% of pixels, after quantizing) — must be ≤ 4 plus neutrals; fonts embedded or outlined; nothing clipped. Run existing tests/build; Redesign and Image Restyle re-run the Step 1 script and compare before/after numbers. - **Output:** check results with numbers. - **Decision:** any failure → fix in B5 and re-check; all pass → B7. ### B7 — Polish (only with budget left) - **Do:** refine spacing, type, details; re-run B6 after changes. **Output:** improved files. **Done when:** budget is spent or nothing reads generic; never leave the file worse than the last passing version. ## Final step — Report - **Do:** write in the user's language (`--lang zh` gives a Chinese report skeleton; replace every TODO). Build: the direction and trade-offs in 2–4 lines, what was made (file paths), B6 numbers. Review: the mode's template (`audit.md` §3, `site-review.md` §4, `image-aesthetics.md` §7, `game-workflows.md` §2), leading with a direct answer to the user's question. - **Output:** the deliverable message (plus report files/screenshots). - **Done when:** every claim is backed by a number or observation from R3/R4 or B6; nothing unverified is presented as checked. ## Reference map - `references/modes.md` — full mode table with mode-specific steps per reference file. - `references/direction.md` — direction prompts, tone catalog, how to pick fonts/palettes per tone. - `references/principles.md` — color, typography, spacing, radius, shadow, motion, layout rules + anti-patterns. - `references/tokens.md` — 3-tier token system (primitive → semantic → component) with example. - `references/audit.md` — P0/P1/P2 checklist, measurable checks, report format. - `references/redesign.md` — safe upgrade workflow for existing projects. - `references/minimalist.md` — warm-monochrome editorial style spec. - `references/theming.md` — themes for slides/docs/reports; theme recipe. - `references/artifacts.md` — posters and static visual pieces (philosophy → canvas). - `references/site-review.md` — URL review workflow: capture → metrics → 45/55 score → P0/P1/P2 report. - `references/benchmarks.md` — top-company homepage breakdowns, industry playbooks, metric targets, common mistakes. - `scripts/review_site.py` — Playwright capture + metric score + report skeleton; `scripts/benchmarks.csv` — 147 scored sites. - `references/image-aesthetics.md` — image rubric: 8 dimensions × type weights, P0/P1/P2, AI-artifact checklist, metric ranges. - `references/image-workflows.md` — parse → palette → layout → enhance pipeline; zine/collage/product/palette/cover recipes; Nature-style figure checklist; anti-slop prompt templates. - `scripts/review_image.py` — Pillow+numpy image metrics (palette, harmony, tone, sharpness, noise, colorfulness, thirds/centroid, whitespace) → metrics.json, palette.png, thirds-overlay.png, report.md. - `references/game-aesthetics.md` — game rubric: 11 dims (readability, value, gameplay clarity, HUD, VFX…) × asset weights, 21 genre profiles, 9 asset rubrics, AI checks, metric ranges. - `references/game-workflows.md` — grayscale/silhouette/thumbnail/2-second tests, metric interpretation by genre, P0/P1/P2 report, fix recipes, anti-slop game-art prompts. - `scripts/review_image.py --type --genre ` — adds value bands, figure-ground, shape clarity, HUD coverage, color count, store-thumbnail readability → grayscale.png, thumbnail.png. - `references/sources.md` — upstream skills, URLs, and licenses. artifacts.md audit.md benchmarks.md direction.md game-aesthetics.md game-workflows.md image-aesthetics.md image-workflows.md minimalist.md modes.md principles.md redesign.md site-review.md sources.md theming.md tokens.md

# Visual Principles

## Color
- 60/30/10: dominant neutral surface, secondary surface/text, ~10% accent.
- Accent marks *interactive or important* things only. If everything is accented, nothing is.
- Never pure `#000` text on pure `#fff` for long reading; use off-black/off-white.
- Gray text on colored backgrounds: use a tint/shade of the background hue instead.
- Gradients: subtle and purposeful (lighting, depth), not as the brand.
- ❌ purple/indigo→blue hero gradient, neon glow, rainbow charts. ✅ one confident color field, tinted neutrals.

## Typography
- Modular scale (e.g. 1.2–1.333 ratio): 12 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64. Use ≤ 6–8 sizes.
- Weights: 2–3 (e.g. 400 / 500 / 700). Hierarchy = size + weight + color, not all-caps everywhere.
- Max line length ~ 65ch; avoid justified text on web; avoid widows in headings (`text-wrap: balance`).
- ❌ everything 14px medium gray. ✅ clear step from H1 → body → caption.

## Spacing & layout
- 4/8px base scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128.
- Proximity: inner padding < gap between groups < section spacing.
- Use a grid (12-col or content-based); align edges. Asymmetry is fine when intentional.
- Break the "hero + 3 cards" template: try split layouts, big type, lists, tables, bento with varied spans, overlapping elements.
- Don't wrap everything in cards. Use whitespace, dividers, or background shifts to group.
- Responsive: design mobile and desktop deliberately; never just shrink.

## Radius
- One family: e.g. 4 (inputs, tags) / 8 (cards) / 9999 (pills). Nested radius = outer − padding.
- Sharp radii read technical/editorial; large radii read soft/consumer. Pick per tone; don't mix arbitrarily.

## Shadow & depth
- ≤ 3 elevation levels (raised, overlay, modal). Shadows soft, low-opacity, layered; tinted toward background hue.
- Prefer borders or surface tone shifts for flat/minimal looks. No shadow + border + gradient on the same card.
- Dark mode: elevation by lighter surface, not shadow.

## Motion
- Purpose: feedback, continuity, orientation. Not decoration.
- Durations: 100–150ms (micro: hover/press), 200–300ms (enter/exit), ≤ 500ms (page-level).
- Ease-out for entering, ease-in for exiting; avoid linear for UI; avoid elastic/bounce unless playful tone.
- Animate `transform` and `opacity` only; never width/height/top/left for UI transitions.
- One well-orchestrated moment (e.g. staggered page load) beats scattered effects.
- Always honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Iconography & imagery
- One icon set, one stroke weight, sized to the text it sits beside. No emoji as UI icons.
- Real or purpose-made imagery; consistent crop, ratio, and treatment.

## Copy
- Specific verbs and nouns. Ban: "Elevate", "Seamless", "Unleash", "Next-gen", "Revolutionize".
- Buttons say what happens ("Create invoice", not "Submit").
- Error messages: what happened + how to fix.
# Token System (3 tiers)

```
Primitive  → raw values, named by what they ARE      (--blue-600, --space-4, --radius-2)
Semantic   → named by PURPOSE, reference primitives  (--color-accent, --color-text-muted, --space-section)
Component  → named by COMPONENT, reference semantics (--button-bg, --card-padding)
```

Rules:
- Components consume **semantic or component** tokens only, never primitives or raw literals.
- Theming (dark mode, brand variants) = swapping the semantic layer; primitives and components stay.
- Keep primitive sets small. If a value isn't on the scale, question the design before adding it.

## Example (CSS variables)
```css
:root {
  /* primitive */
  --neutral-0:#fff; --neutral-50:#f7f6f3; --neutral-200:#e7e5e0; --neutral-600:#6b6a66; --neutral-900:#1c1b19;
  --brand-500:#d9480f; --brand-600:#b93d0c;
  --space-1:4px; --space-2:8px; --space-3:12px; --space-4:16px; --space-6:24px; --space-8:32px; --space-12:48px; --space-16:64px;
  --radius-1:4px; --radius-2:8px; --radius-full:9999px;
  --font-sans:"Söhne","Helvetica Neue",system-ui,sans-serif; --font-serif:"Newsreader",Georgia,serif;
  --text-sm:14px; --text-base:16px; --text-lg:20px; --text-xl:32px; --text-2xl:48px;
  --ease-out:cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); --dur-fast:120ms; --dur-base:220ms;

  /* semantic */
  --color-bg:var(--neutral-0); --color-surface:var(--neutral-50); --color-border:var(--neutral-200);
  --color-text:var(--neutral-900); --color-text-muted:var(--neutral-600);
  --color-accent:var(--brand-500); --color-accent-hover:var(--brand-600);
  --space-inline:var(--space-3); --space-stack:var(--space-4); --space-section:var(--space-16);
  --shadow-raised:0 1px 2px rgb(28 27 25 / .06), 0 2px 8px rgb(28 27 25 / .04);

  /* component */
  --button-bg:var(--color-accent); --button-bg-hover:var(--color-accent-hover); --button-radius:var(--radius-1);
  --button-pad:var(--space-2) var(--space-4);
  --card-bg:var(--color-surface); --card-radius:var(--radius-2); --card-pad:var(--space-6);
}
[data-theme="dark"] {
  --color-bg:#121110; --color-surface:#1c1b19; --color-border:#2c2a27;
  --color-text:#ecebe8; --color-text-muted:#a3a19c; --color-accent:#f76b2b;
}
```

## Tailwind / other stacks
Map the semantic layer into `theme.extend` (colors, spacing, borderRadius, fontSize) or the framework's theme object; avoid arbitrary values (`text-[13px]`, `#3b82f6`) in markup.

## Documenting
For a design system, keep a short table per tier: token, value, usage, do/don't. Component specs list: anatomy, variants, sizes, states, tokens used, a11y notes.

Goal: find what most hurts usability and perceived quality, ranked, with evidence. Review first; change code only if asked.

## 1. Measurable checks (run these, report numbers)
Adjust globs to the project.
```bash
# distinct hex colors (target: small, mostly via tokens)
rg -o --no-filename '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b' src | tr 'A-F' 'a-f' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
# distinct font sizes (target ≤ 6–8)
rg -o --no-filename 'font-size:\s*[^;]+|text-(xs|sm|base|lg|[0-9]?xl)|text-\[[^]]+\]' src | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
# radii, shadows, z-index, arbitrary Tailwind values
rg -o --no-filename 'border-radius:\s*[^;]+|rounded(-[a-z0-9]+)?' src | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
rg -o --no-filename 'box-shadow:\s*[^;]+|shadow(-[a-z]+)?' src | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
rg -o --no-filename '\w+-\[[^]]+\]' src | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -40
# font families, !important, inline styles
rg -o --no-filename 'font-family:\s*[^;]+' src | sort | uniq -c
rg -c '!important' src ; rg -c 'style=\{\{|style="' src
```
Thresholds (guidance): > ~12 distinct literal hex values, > 8 font sizes, > 3 radii, > 3 shadows, > 2 font families, or many arbitrary values ⇒ token debt.

Also check: contrast of real text/background pairs (WCAG AA 4.5:1 / 3:1), tab through for focus visibility, viewport 375 / 768 / 1280 for overflow, `prefers-reduced-motion` handling, image `alt`, form labels.

## 2. Prioritized checklist

**P0 — broken / blocking (fix first)**
- Text contrast below AA; invisible focus; keyboard traps.
- Layout breaks or horizontal scroll on mobile; overlapping/clipped content.
- Primary action unclear or hidden; missing error/loading/empty states that leave users stuck.
- Touch targets < 44px for primary controls; forms without labels.

**P1 — quality & consistency**
- No clear direction / generic AI look (see slop list in SKILL.md).
- Token debt (counts above); inconsistent spacing rhythm; mixed radius/shadow families.
- Weak hierarchy: too many equal-weight elements, too many font sizes/colors.
- Cards-in-cards, excessive borders, decorative gradients/glass.
- Motion on layout properties, no reduced-motion, durations > 500ms.

**P2 — polish**
- Copy clichés, placeholder names, emoji icons.
- Optical alignment, icon sizes vs text, `text-wrap: balance` on headings, tabular numerals.
- Micro-interactions on hover/press; consistent image treatment.

## Metrics  (colors N, font sizes N, radii N, shadows N, arbitrary values N, contrast failures N)
## P0 / P1 / P2  — each item: what, where (file:line or screen area), why it matters, concrete fix

name: taste-design
description: Semantic Design System Skill for Google Stitch. Generates agent-friendly DESIGN.md files that enforce premium, anti-generic UI standards — strict typography, calibrated color, asymmetric layouts, perpetual micro-motion, and hardware-accelerated performance.
allowed-tools:
  - "StitchMCP"
  - "Read"
  - "Write"

# Stitch Design Taste — Semantic Design System Skill

## Overview
This skill generates `DESIGN.md` files optimized for Google Stitch screen generation. It translates the battle-tested anti-slop frontend engineering directives into Stitch's native semantic design language — descriptive, natural-language rules paired with precise values that Stitch's AI agent can interpret to produce premium, non-generic interfaces.

The generated `DESIGN.md` serves as the **single source of truth** for prompting Stitch to generate new screens that align with a curated, high-agency design language. Stitch interprets design through **"Visual Descriptions"** supported by specific color values, typography specs, and component behaviors.

## Prerequisites
- Access to Google Stitch via [labs.google.com/stitch](https://labs.google.com/stitch)
- Optionally: Stitch MCP Server for programmatic integration with Cursor, Antigravity, or Gemini CLI

## The Goal
Generate a `DESIGN.md` file that encodes:
1. **Visual atmosphere** — the mood, density, and design philosophy
2. **Color calibration** — neutrals, accents, and banned patterns with hex codes
3. **Typographic architecture** — font stacks, scale hierarchy, and anti-patterns
4. **Component behaviors** — buttons, cards, inputs with interaction states
5. **Layout principles** — grid systems, spacing philosophy, responsive strategy
6. **Motion philosophy** — animation engine specs, spring physics, perpetual micro-interactions
7. **Anti-patterns** — explicit list of banned AI design clichés

## Analysis & Synthesis Instructions

### 1. Define the Atmosphere
Evaluate the target project's intent. Use evocative adjectives from the taste spectrum:
- **Density:** "Art Gallery Airy" (1–3) → "Daily App Balanced" (4–7) → "Cockpit Dense" (8–10)
- **Variance:** "Predictable Symmetric" (1–3) → "Offset Asymmetric" (4–7) → "Artsy Chaotic" (8–10)
- **Motion:** "Static Restrained" (1–3) → "Fluid CSS" (4–7) → "Cinematic Choreography" (8–10)

Default baseline: Creativity 9, Variance 8, Motion 6, Density 5. Adapt dynamically based on user's vibe description.

### 2. Map the Color Palette
For each color provide: **Descriptive Name** + **Hex Code** + **Functional Role**.

**Mandatory constraints:**
- Maximum 1 accent color. Saturation below 80%
- The "AI Purple/Blue Neon" aesthetic is strictly BANNED — no purple button glows, no neon gradients
- Use absolute neutral bases (Zinc/Slate) with high-contrast singular accents
- Stick to one palette for the entire output — no warm/cool gray fluctuation
- Never use pure black (`#000000`) — use Off-Black, Zinc-950, or Charcoal

### 3. Establish Typography Rules
- **Display/Headlines:** Track-tight, controlled scale. Not screaming. Hierarchy through weight and color, not just massive size
- **Body:** Relaxed leading, max 65 characters per line
- **Font Selection:** `Inter` is BANNED for premium/creative contexts. Force unique character: `Geist`, `Outfit`, `Cabinet Grotesk`, or `Satoshi`
- **Serif Ban:** Generic serif fonts (`Times New Roman`, `Georgia`, `Garamond`, `Palatino`) are BANNED. If serif is needed for editorial/creative contexts, use only distinctive modern serifs: `Fraunces`, `Gambarino`, `Editorial New`, or `Instrument Serif`. Serif is always BANNED in dashboards or software UIs
- **Dashboard Constraint:** Use Sans-Serif pairings exclusively (`Geist` + `Geist Mono` or `Satoshi` + `JetBrains Mono`)
- **High-Density Override:** When density exceeds 7, all numbers must use Monospace

### 4. Define the Hero Section
The Hero is the first impression and must be creative, striking, and never generic:
- **Inline Image Typography:** Embed small, contextual photos or visuals directly between words or letters in the headline. Images sit inline at type-height, rounded, acting as visual punctuation. This is the signature creative technique
- **No Overlapping:** Text must never overlap images or other text. Every element occupies its own clean spatial zone
- **No Filler Text:** "Scroll to explore", "Swipe down", scroll arrow icons, bouncing chevrons are BANNED. The content should pull users in naturally
- **Asymmetric Structure:** Centered Hero layouts BANNED when variance exceeds 4
- **CTA Restraint:** Maximum one primary CTA. No secondary "Learn more" links

### 5. Describe Component Stylings
For each component type, describe shape, color, shadow depth, and interaction behavior:
- **Buttons:** Tactile push feedback on active state. No neon outer glows. No custom mouse cursors
- **Cards:** Use ONLY when elevation communicates hierarchy. Tint shadows to background hue. For high-density layouts, replace cards with border-top dividers or negative space
- **Inputs/Forms:** Label above input, helper text optional, error text below. Standard gap spacing
- **Loading States:** Skeletal loaders matching layout dimensions — no generic circular spinners
- **Empty States:** Composed compositions indicating how to populate data
- **Error States:** Clear, inline error reporting

### 6. Define Layout Principles
- No overlapping elements — every element occupies its own clear spatial zone. No absolute-positioned content stacking
- Centered Hero sections are BANNED when variance exceeds 4 — force Split Screen, Left-Aligned, or Asymmetric Whitespace
- The generic "3 equal cards horizontally" feature row is BANNED — use 2-column Zig-Zag, asymmetric grid, or horizontal scroll
- CSS Grid over Flexbox math — never use `calc()` percentage hacks
- Contain layouts using max-width constraints (e.g., 1400px centered)
- Full-height sections must use `min-h-[100dvh]` — never `h-screen` (iOS Safari catastrophic jump)

### 7. Define Responsive Rules
Every design must work across all viewports:
- **Mobile-First Collapse (< 768px):** All multi-column layouts collapse to single column. No exceptions
- **No Horizontal Scroll:** Horizontal overflow on mobile is a critical failure
- **Typography Scaling:** Headlines scale via `clamp()`. Body text minimum `1rem`/`14px`
- **Touch Targets:** All interactive elements minimum `44px` tap target
- **Image Behavior:** Inline typography images (photos between words) stack below headline on mobile
- **Navigation:** Desktop horizontal nav collapses to clean mobile menu
- **Spacing:** Vertical section gaps reduce proportionally (`clamp(3rem, 8vw, 6rem)`)

### 8. Encode Motion Philosophy
- **Spring Physics default:** `stiffness: 100, damping: 20` — premium, weighty feel. No linear easing
- **Perpetual Micro-Interactions:** Every active component should have an infinite loop state (Pulse, Typewriter, Float, Shimmer)
- **Staggered Orchestration:** Never mount lists instantly — use cascade delays for waterfall reveals
- **Performance:** Animate exclusively via `transform` and `opacity`. Never animate `top`, `left`, `width`, `height`. Grain/noise filters on fixed pseudo-elements only

### 9. List Anti-Patterns (AI Tells)
Encode these as explicit "NEVER DO" rules in the DESIGN.md:
- No emojis anywhere
- No `Inter` font
- No generic serif fonts (`Times New Roman`, `Georgia`, `Garamond`) — distinctive modern serifs only if needed
- No pure black (`#000000`)
- No neon/outer glow shadows
- No oversaturated accents
- No excessive gradient text on large headers
- No custom mouse cursors
- No overlapping elements — clean spatial separation always
- No 3-column equal card layouts
- No generic names ("John Doe", "Acme", "Nexus")
- No fake round numbers (`99.99%`, `50%`)
- No fabricated data or statistics — never generate metrics, performance numbers, uptime percentages, response times, or any data that the user did not explicitly provide. "99.98% UPTIME SLA", "124ms AVG. RESPONSE", "18.5k DEPLOY CYCLES" are invented AI filler. If real data is not available, use clear placeholder labels like `[metric]` instead of making up numbers
- No fake system/metric sections — "SYSTEM PERFORMANCE METRICS", "KEY STATISTICS", "BY THE NUMBERS" dashboard cards filled with invented data are BANNED
- No `LABEL // YEAR` formatting — "SYSTEM // 2024", "METRICS // 2025" is a lazy AI convention, not real design typography
- No AI copywriting clichés ("Elevate", "Seamless", "Unleash", "Next-Gen")
- No filler UI text: "Scroll to explore", "Swipe down", scroll arrows, bouncing chevrons
- No broken Unsplash links — use `picsum.photos` or SVG avatars
- No centered Hero sections (for high-variance projects)

## Output Format (DESIGN.md Structure)

```markdown
# Design System: [Project Title]

## 1. Visual Theme & Atmosphere
(Evocative description of the mood, density, variance, and motion intensity.
Example: "A restrained, gallery-airy interface with confident asymmetric layouts
and fluid spring-physics motion. The atmosphere is clinical yet warm — like a
well-lit architecture studio.")

## 2. Color Palette & Roles
- **Canvas White** (#F9FAFB) — Primary background surface
- **Pure Surface** (#FFFFFF) — Card and container fill
- **Charcoal Ink** (#18181B) — Primary text, Zinc-950 depth
- **Muted Steel** (#71717A) — Secondary text, descriptions, metadata
- **Whisper Border** (rgba(226,232,240,0.5)) — Card borders, 1px structural lines
- **[Accent Name]** (#XXXXXX) — Single accent for CTAs, active states, focus rings
(Max 1 accent. Saturation < 80%. No purple/neon.)

## 3. Typography Rules
- **Display:** [Font Name] — Track-tight, controlled scale, weight-driven hierarchy
- **Body:** [Font Name] — Relaxed leading, 65ch max-width, neutral secondary color
- **Mono:** [Font Name] — For code, metadata, timestamps, high-density numbers
- **Banned:** Inter, generic system fonts for premium contexts. Serif fonts banned in dashboards.

## 4. Component Stylings
* **Buttons:** Flat, no outer glow. Tactile -1px translate on active. Accent fill for primary, ghost/outline for secondary.
* **Cards:** Generously rounded corners (2.5rem). Diffused whisper shadow. Used only when elevation serves hierarchy. High-density: replace with border-top dividers.
* **Inputs:** Label above, error below. Focus ring in accent color. No floating labels.
* **Loaders:** Skeletal shimmer matching exact layout dimensions. No circular spinners.
* **Empty States:** Composed, illustrated compositions — not just "No data" text.

## 5. Layout Principles
(Grid-first responsive architecture. Asymmetric splits for Hero sections.
Strict single-column collapse below 768px. Max-width containment.
No flexbox percentage math. Generous internal padding.)

## 6. Motion & Interaction
(Spring physics for all interactive elements. Staggered cascade reveals.
Perpetual micro-loops on active dashboard components. Hardware-accelerated
transforms only. Isolated Client Components for CPU-heavy animations.)

## 7. Anti-Patterns (Banned)
(Explicit list of forbidden patterns: no emojis, no Inter, no pure black,
no neon glows, no 3-column equal grids, no AI copywriting clichés,
no generic placeholder names, no broken image links.)
```

## Best Practices
- **Be Descriptive:** "Deep Charcoal Ink (#18181B)" — not just "dark text"
- **Be Functional:** Explain what each element is used for
- **Be Consistent:** Same terminology throughout the document
- **Be Precise:** Include exact hex codes, rem values, pixel values in parentheses
- **Be Opinionated:** This is not a neutral template — it enforces a specific, premium aesthetic

## Tips for Success
1. Start with the atmosphere — understand the vibe before detailing tokens
2. Look for patterns — identify consistent spacing, sizing, and styling
3. Think semantically — name colors by purpose, not just appearance
4. Consider hierarchy — document how visual weight communicates importance
5. Encode the bans — anti-patterns are as important as the rules themselves

## Common Pitfalls to Avoid
- Using technical jargon without translation ("rounded-xl" instead of "generously rounded corners")
- Omitting hex codes or using only descriptive names
- Forgetting functional roles of design elements
- Being too vague in atmosphere descriptions
- Ignoring the anti-pattern list — these are what make the output premium
- Defaulting to generic "safe" designs instead of enforcing the curated aesthetic

# Android Mobile Design

Master Material Design 3 (Material You) and Jetpack Compose to build modern, adaptive Android applications that integrate seamlessly with the Android ecosystem.

## When to Use This Skill

- Designing Android app interfaces following Material Design 3
- Building Jetpack Compose UI and layouts
- Implementing Android navigation patterns (Navigation Compose)
- Creating adaptive layouts for phones, tablets, and foldables
- Using Material 3 theming with dynamic colors
- Building accessible Android interfaces
- Implementing Android-specific gestures and interactions
- Designing for different screen configurations

## Detailed section: Core Concepts

Originally a 9201-byte section in this SKILL.md. Moved to `references/details.md` to fit Codex's 8 KB skill body cap.

## Quick Start Component

```kotlin
@Composable
fun ItemListCard(
    item: Item,
    onItemClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier
) {
    Card(
        onClick = onItemClick,
        modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        shape = RoundedCornerShape(12.dp)
    ) {
        Row(
            modifier = Modifier
                .padding(16.dp)
                .fillMaxWidth(),
            verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
        ) {
            Box(
                modifier = Modifier
                    .size(48.dp)
                    .clip(CircleShape)
                    .background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primaryContainer),
                contentAlignment = Alignment.Center
            ) {
                Icon(
                    imageVector = Icons.Default.Star,
                    contentDescription = null,
                    tint = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onPrimaryContainer
                )
            }

            Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(16.dp))

            Column(modifier = Modifier.weight(1f)) {
                Text(
                    text = item.title,
                    style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium
                )
                Text(
                    text = item.subtitle,
                    style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
                    color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
                )
            }

            Icon(
                imageVector = Icons.Default.ChevronRight,
                contentDescription = null,
                tint = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
            )
        }
    }
}
```

## Best Practices

1. **Use Material Theme**: Access colors via `MaterialTheme.colorScheme` for automatic dark mode support
2. **Support Dynamic Color**: Enable dynamic color on Android 12+ for personalization
3. **Adaptive Layouts**: Use `WindowSizeClass` for responsive designs
4. **Content Descriptions**: Add `contentDescription` to all interactive elements
5. **Touch Targets**: Minimum 48dp touch targets for accessibility
6. **State Hoisting**: Hoist state to make components reusable and testable
7. **Remember Properly**: Use `remember` and `rememberSaveable` appropriately
8. **Preview Annotations**: Add `@Preview` with different configurations

## Common Issues

- **Recomposition Issues**: Avoid passing unstable lambdas; use `remember`
- **State Loss**: Use `rememberSaveable` for configuration changes
- **Performance**: Use `LazyColumn` instead of `Column` for long lists
- **Theme Leaks**: Ensure `MaterialTheme` wraps all composables
- **Navigation Crashes**: Handle back press and deep links properly
- **Memory Leaks**: Cancel coroutines in `DisposableEffect`

# Mobile Touch Animation

Apply Disney's 12 animation principles to mobile gestures, haptics, and native app motion.

## Quick Reference

| Principle | Mobile Implementation |
|-----------|----------------------|
| Squash & Stretch | Rubber-banding, bounce on scroll limits |
| Anticipation | Peek before reveal, long-press preview |
| Staging | Sheet presentations, focus states |
| Straight Ahead / Pose to Pose | Gesture-driven vs preset transitions |
| Follow Through / Overlapping | Momentum scrolling, trailing elements |
| Slow In / Slow Out | iOS spring animations, Material easing |
| Arc | Swipe-to-dismiss curves, card throws |
| Secondary Action | Haptic pulse with visual feedback |
| Timing | Touch response <100ms, transitions 250-350ms |
| Exaggeration | Bounce amplitude, haptic intensity |
| Solid Drawing | Respect safe areas, consistent anchors |
| Appeal | 60fps minimum, gesture continuity |

## Principle Applications

**Squash & Stretch**: Implement rubber-band effect at scroll boundaries. Pull-to-refresh should stretch content naturally. Buttons compress on touch.

**Anticipation**: Long-press shows preview before full action. Drag threshold provides visual hint before item lifts. Swipe shows edge of destination content.

**Staging**: Use sheet presentations to maintain context. Dim and scale background during modal focus. Hero transitions connect views meaningfully.

**Straight Ahead vs Pose to Pose**: Gesture-following animations (drag, pinch) are straight ahead—driven by touch input. System transitions (push, present) are pose to pose—predefined keyframes.

**Follow Through & Overlapping**: Content continues moving after finger lifts (momentum). Navigation bar elements animate slightly after main content. Lists items settle with stagger.

**Slow In / Slow Out**: iOS uses spring physics—configure mass, stiffness, damping. Android Material uses standard easing: `FastOutSlowIn`. Never use linear for user-initiated motion.

**Arc**: Thrown cards follow parabolic arcs. Swipe-to-dismiss curves based on velocity vector. FAB expand/collapse follows natural arc path.

**Secondary Action**: Pair haptic feedback with visual response. Button ripple accompanies press. Success checkmark triggers light haptic.

**Timing**: Touch acknowledgment: <100ms. Quick actions: 150-250ms. View transitions: 250-350ms. Complex animations: 350-500ms. Haptic should sync precisely with visual.

**Exaggeration**: Pull-to-refresh stretches beyond natural—makes feedback clear. Error shake is pronounced. Success animations celebrate appropriately.

**Solid Drawing**: Respect device safe areas during animation. Maintain consistent transform origins. Account for notch/dynamic island in motion paths.

**Appeal**: Minimum 60fps, target 120fps on ProMotion displays. Gesture-driven animation must feel connected to finger. Interruptible animations essential.

## Platform Patterns

### iOS
```swift
// Spring animation with follow-through
UIView.animate(withDuration: 0.5,
               delay: 0,
               usingSpringWithDamping: 0.7,
               initialSpringVelocity: 0.5,
               options: .curveEaseOut)

// Haptic pairing
let feedback = UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .medium)
feedback.impactOccurred()
```

### Android
```kotlin
// Material spring animation
SpringAnimation(view, DynamicAnimation.TRANSLATION_Y)
    .setSpring(SpringForce()
        .setStiffness(SpringForce.STIFFNESS_MEDIUM)
        .setDampingRatio(SpringForce.DAMPING_RATIO_MEDIUM_BOUNCY))
    .start()
```

## Haptic Guidelines

| Action | iOS | Android |
|--------|-----|---------|
| Selection | `.selection` | `EFFECT_TICK` |
| Success | `.success` | `EFFECT_CLICK` |
| Warning | `.warning` | `EFFECT_DOUBLE_CLICK` |
| Error | `.error` | `EFFECT_HEAVY_CLICK` |

Haptics are secondary action—always pair with visual confirmation.

Applying padding to the parent container prevents the App Bar background from drawing into the system bar area. For example, for `TopAppBar`, choose only one of the following options: 1. **PREFERRED:** `TopAppBar(windowInsets = AppBarDefaults.topAppBarWindowInsets)` 2. `TopAppBar(windowInsets = WindowInsets.systemBars.exclude(WindowInsets.navigationBars))` 3. `TopAppBar(windowInsets = WindowInsets.systemBars.add(WindowInsets.captionBar))` 2. For components outside a Scaffold, use padding modifiers, such as `Modifier.safeDrawingPadding()` or `Modifier.windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing)`. ```kotlin Box( modifier = Modifier .fillMaxSize() .safeDrawingPadding() ) { Button( onClick = {}, modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.BottomCenter) ) { Text("Login") } } ```

However, the adaptive scaffolds (e.g. `NavigationSuiteScaffold`, `ListDetailPaneScaffold`) don't propagate PaddingValues to their inner contents. | `Android resource linking failed` | A resource, style parent, or attribute that does not exist at this `compileSdk` | The line is in the message — usually a new attribute against an old compileSdk |
| `Cannot fit requested classes in a single dex file` | Over 65,536 methods without multidex | Enable multidex (automatic on `minSdk >= 21`), then shrink with R8 rather than living with it |
| `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` | The installed app is signed with a different key | Uninstall first; on a user's device that means the signing identity changed — never ship that |
| `INSTALL_FAILED_TEST_ONLY` | The APK is flagged test-only, as IDE-run debug builds are | Install with `-t`, or build a real debug APK from the assemble task |
| `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE` | Lower versionCode than what is installed | Uninstall for local work; on Play there is no downgrade at all (Rule 9) |
| `ActivityNotFoundException` on a deep link | No component matches the intent, or the link is not verified | Resolve the intent from the shell, then check App Links verification (`security.md`) |
| `SecurityException: … PendingIntent … must be mutable/immutable` | Missing the mutability flag required from targetSdk 31 | `FLAG_IMMUTABLE` unless the receiver must fill in the intent (`sdk-upgrades.md`) |
| `ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException` | `startForegroundService()` without `startForeground()` inside the window | Post the notification first thing in `onCreate`, before any work (`background.md`) |
| `NetworkOnMainThreadException` / `IllegalStateException: Cannot access database on the main thread` | I/O on the UI thread (Rule 5) | Move to a background dispatcher; never use the "allow main thread" escape hatches |
| `IllegalStateException: Can not perform this action after onSaveInstanceState` | A fragment transaction after the state was saved | Do the transaction in a lifecycle-aware place; `commitAllowingStateLoss` hides the bug (`views.md`) |
| `ClassNotFoundException` / `NoSuchFieldException` only in release | R8 removed or renamed something reached by reflection | Add the narrowest keep rule and re-test the release build, not the debug one (`release.md`) |
| `TransactionTooLargeException` | More than the ~1 MB Binder budget crossed at once, usually saved state or an intent extra | Pass an id, load the payload on the other side (Rule 4) |
| ANR with `Input dispatching timed out` | The main thread was blocked past 5 s | Read the ANR trace's main-thread stack — the top frame is the block (`crashes.md`) |
| Anything else | Reproduce on one device, change one variable, and match the exact string | `build-failures.md` for build, `debug.md` for runtime |

## Limits That Force Designs

Constraints that have each killed a half-built Android design.

| Limit | Value | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| Dex methods per file | 65,536 | Multidex is automatic on `minSdk >= 21`; past that the real cost is startup and build time, so shrink dependencies instead of celebrating multidex |
| Binder transaction | ~1 MB, shared across the whole process | Saved state, intent extras and bound-service payloads all draw on it — pass ids, not blobs (Rule 4) |
| Input ANR | 5 s | Every main-thread operation budget derives from this; broadcasts, services and providers have their own shorter or longer ceilings (`crashes.md`) |
| Foreground service start | ~5 s from start to `startForeground()` | Notification construction happens before any initialization work |
| WorkManager periodic work | 15-minute minimum interval | Anything more frequent is either a foreground service or nothing |
| versionCode | Max 2,100,000,000, must strictly increase | Rules out timestamp schemes in milliseconds; a date-plus-counter scheme fits comfortably (`release.md`) |
| Bundle download size | Play caps the compressed download of the delivered app; larger payloads move to asset packs or on-demand delivery | Ship media as an asset pack rather than fighting the cap (`play-console.md`) |
| Notification channel | Immutable after creation, except by the user | Get importance right the first time; changing it means a new channel id and a migration |
| Activity result / permission request | Must be registered before the lifecycle reaches STARTED | Registration happens at field initialization, not inside a click handler (`lifecycle.md`) |

## Defaults That Decide Behavior

Android's defaults are chosen for compatibility, not for your app. Each of these has produced a bug that reads as an application defect.

| Default | Value | Why it bites |
|---|---|---|
| `android:allowBackup` | true | App data leaves the device through backup unless `dataExtractionRules` restrict it (`security.md`) |
| Configuration change | The Activity is destroyed and recreated | Anything held in the Activity is gone; `android:configChanges` suppresses recreation and creates a second, subtler class of bug (`lifecycle.md`) |
| `collectAsState` on a Flow | Keeps collecting while the app is in the background | `collectAsStateWithLifecycle` is the default choice on Android; the plain version burns battery and hits dead views (`architecture.md`) |
| Room queries | Throw on the main thread — unless the escape hatch is enabled | Enabling `allowMainThreadQueries` converts a crash into an ANR (`data.md`) |
| HTTP client timeouts | OkHttp connect/read/write default to 10 s, with **no** overall call timeout | A stalled response can hang a request indefinitely; set `callTimeout` explicitly (`networking.md`) |
| Bitmap config | `ARGB_8888` → 4 bytes per pixel | A 4000×3000 photo is ~48 MB decoded, whatever the JPEG weighed — always decode with a target size (`performance.md`) |
| `WebView` | JavaScript disabled, but file access and mixed content settings are permissive on older targets | Enable exactly what the page needs; a JavaScript interface is a remote-code surface (`security.md`) |
| App Standby bucket | Assigned by usage, invisible to the app | The same code runs on schedule on your desk and hours late on a device the user rarely opens (`background.md`) |
| OEM battery management | Additional, undocumented, and off-spec | Background work verified on a Pixel can be killed outright on several popular skins (`devices.md`) |

## Output Gates

Before emitting a Gradle file, a manifest entry, a screen, or a release command:

- Is the layer named — build, install, runtime, or store — and does the fix act on that layer (Rule 1)?
- Do the versions in this snippet form one valid set (AGP, Gradle, JDK, Kotlin, Compose BOM), and is the assumed `target_sdk` stated when it is unset (Rules 2, 3)?
- Does every new state holder answer "survives rotation?" and "survives process death?" (Rule 4)?
- Is anything on the main thread that touches disk, network, database, image decode, or crypto (Rule 5)?
- Does any new permission, foreground service type, or exported component carry the manifest declaration *and* the Play declaration it will need (`permissions.md`, `play-console.md`)?
- Would this survive R8 — is anything reached by reflection covered by a keep rule (Rule 8)?
- Is any command destructive (`adb uninstall`, `pm clear`, wiping an emulator, `--rm` on a build directory, halting a rollout)? Then it names exactly what dies and ships with a confirmation step, never inside a copy-paste block of read-only commands.
- Did anything durable come out of this — a release, a toolchain set, a device, a measured number, a non-obvious cause, a declaration text, a decision? Then it is written to its box in `memory-template.md`, with its `## Boxes` line, in this same turn.

## Configuration

User-dependent variables. Defaults apply until the user states a preference; store them in `~/Clawic/data/android/config.yaml`.

# Mochi Hop

An original Game Boy Advance homebrew platformer made for **Retra**. You play Mochi, a squishy
pink rice-cake with a leaf on top. Hop across pastel cloud islands, candy caves and a starry
night, collect stars and rescue the little sprout friends, who then follow you around.

All code, art, music and level designs are original and live in this directory. No third-party
assets are used and no devkitPro is needed.

## Controls

| Button | Action |
| --- | --- |
| D-Pad | Move (on the map: pick a level) |
| A | Jump. Hold for a higher jump. Hold while stomping to bounce higher. |
| B | Run (on the map: back to the title) |
| START | Pause menu (Resume / Retry / World Map); confirm on menus |

## Levels

| # | World | Name | Stars |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-1 | Cloud Meadow | Fluffy Fields | 40 |
| 1-2 | Cloud Meadow | Breezy Bridges | 38 |
| 2-1 | Candy Caves | Gumdrop Grotto | 43 |
| 2-2 | Candy Caves | Sugar Shafts | 38 |
| 3-1 | Starry Night | Twinkle Path | 34 |
| 3-2 | Starry Night | Moonlit Summit | 43 |

Every level has 3 sprouts, at least one checkpoint flag, and a goal star. Clearing a level
unlocks the next one. Clearing 3-2 for the first time plays the credits ("Made for Retra").

Hazards: grumpy raindrops (walk, stompable), bees (fly, stompable), spiky urchins (cannot be
stomped), thorn spikes, and pits. Mochi has 3 hearts. Running out of hearts or falling into a pit
sends you back to the last checkpoint with full hearts, and you keep the stars you have collected.
Touching a checkpoint also refills your hearts. There is no game over.

## Building

Requirements: `arm-none-eabi-gcc`/`objcopy` (tested with 14.2) and Python 3 with Pillow.

def blob(w, h, cx, cy, a, bt, bb, p=2.4):
    def inside(x, y):
        dx = (x + 0.5 - cx) / a
        yy = y + 0.5 - cy

/** Creates and remembers a [HazeState] for coordinating Haze sources and effects. */
@Composable
public fun rememberHazeState(): HazeState = remember { HazeState() }

/** Shared state that associates [hazeSource] content with source-backed Haze effects. */
@Stable
public class HazeState {
  internal var positionStrategy: HazePositionStrategy by mutableStateOf(HazePositionStrategy.Auto)

  private val _areas = mutableStateListOf<HazeArea>()
  internal val areas: List<HazeArea> get() = _areas

  private val sourceDemand = mutableStateSetOf<Any>()

  internal val hasSourceDemand: Boolean
    get() = sourceDemand.isNotEmpty()

  internal fun addSourceDemand(key: Any) {
    sourceDemand += key
  }

  internal fun removeSourceDemand(key: Any) {
    sourceDemand -= key
  }

  internal fun addArea(area: HazeArea) {
    _areas += area
  }

  internal fun removeArea(area: HazeArea) {
    _areas -= area
  }
}

internal fun resolvePositionStrategy(
  configured: HazePositionStrategy,
  areas: List<HazeArea>,
  windowId: Any?,
): HazePositionStrategy = when (configured) {
  HazePositionStrategy.Auto -> {
    if (areas.any { it.windowId != null && it.windowId != windowId }) {
      HazePositionStrategy.Screen
    } else {
      HazePositionStrategy.Local
    }
  }
  else -> configured
}

@Stable
internal class HazeCoordinates(
  localPosition: Offset = Offset.Unspecified,
  screenPosition: Offset = Offset.Unspecified,
) {
  internal var localPosition: Offset by mutableStateOf(localPosition)
    internal set

  internal var screenPosition: Offset by mutableStateOf(screenPosition)
    internal set

  internal fun positionFor(strategy: HazePositionStrategy): Offset = when (strategy) {
    HazePositionStrategy.Local,
    HazePositionStrategy.Auto,
    -> localPosition
    HazePositionStrategy.Screen -> screenPosition
  }

  internal fun boundsFor(strategy: HazePositionStrategy, size: Size): Rect? {
    val position = positionFor(strategy)
    return if (position.isSpecified && size.isSpecified) Rect(position, size) else null
  }
}

/**
 * Returns `true` if either [HazeCoordinates.localPosition] or [HazeCoordinates.screenPosition]
 * is [Offset.Unspecified].
 */
internal val HazeCoordinates.isUnspecified: Boolean
  get() = localPosition.isUnspecified || screenPosition.isUnspecified

@Stable
internal class HazeArea {

  internal val coordinates: HazeCoordinates = HazeCoordinates()

  internal var layoutCoordinates: LayoutCoordinates? = null
    private set

  private var coordinateTransformValues: FloatArray? = null

  internal var coordinateVersion: Int by mutableIntStateOf(0)
    private set

  internal fun updateLayoutCoordinates(coordinates: LayoutCoordinates) {
    layoutCoordinates = coordinates
    val transform = coordinates.transformToScreenOrRoot()
    if (coordinateTransformValues?.contentEquals(transform.values) != true) {
      coordinateTransformValues = transform.values.copyOf()
      coordinateVersion++
    }
  }

  internal fun clearLayoutCoordinates() {
    layoutCoordinates = null
    coordinateTransformValues = null
  }

  internal var size: Size by mutableStateOf(Size.Unspecified)
    internal set

  internal var zIndex: Float by mutableFloatStateOf(0f)
    internal set

  internal var key: Any? by mutableStateOf(null)
    internal set

  internal var windowId: Any? = null
    internal set

  internal val preDrawListeners = mutableStateSetOf<OnPreDrawListener>()

@Stable
public fun <Style> Modifier.hazeEffect(
  factory: HazeEffectFactory<Style>,
  input: HazeInput,
  style: Style,
  sampling: HazeSampling = HazeSampling.Default,
  expandLayerBounds: Boolean = true,
): Modifier = composed(
  "dev.chrisbanes.haze.hazeEffect",
  factory,
  input,
  style,
  sampling,
  expandLayerBounds,
) {
  val effect = Modifier then TypedHazeEffectNodeElement(
    factory = factory,
    input = input,
    style = style,
    sampling = sampling,
    expandLayerBounds = expandLayerBounds,
    lifecycle = LocalLifecycleOwner.current.lifecycle,

    effect.graphicsLayer() then ForegroundContentInvalidationElement

    effect

}

/**
 * Applies Blur to an explicit [input].
 *
 * [style] is an opaque, shareable program. Resolution starts from [HazeBlurDefaults.style], then
 * replays [LocalHazeBlurStyle], then [style]. Later writes win. Each modifier node owns its Blur
 * runtime, delegate, retained output, performance-mode configuration, cache, and lifecycle resources.
 *
 * @param input Source-backed content or this modifier's own content.
 * @param style Explicit Blur Style replayed after [LocalHazeBlurStyle].
 * @param performanceMode Rendering-fidelity policy, or `null` to inherit [LocalHazePerformanceMode].
 * @param expandLayerBounds Whether Blur may expand its capture layer by the resolved radius.
 */
@Stable
public fun Modifier.hazeBlur(
  input: HazeInput,
  style: HazeBlurStyle = HazeBlurStyle,
  performanceMode: HazePerformanceMode? = null,
  expandLayerBounds: Boolean = true,
): Modifier = hazeEffect(
  factory = HazeBlurFactory,
  input = input,
  style = BlurConfiguration(style, performanceMode),
  expandLayerBounds = expandLayerBounds,
)

@Poko
internal class BlurConfiguration(
  val style: HazeBlurStyle,
  val performanceMode: HazePerformanceMode?,
)

}

  /**
   * Default blur radius. Larger values produce a stronger blur effect.
   */
  public val blurRadius: Dp = 20.dp

  /**
   * Noise factor.
   */

  /**
   * Default edge treatment used by [hazeBlur].
   */
  public val blurredEdgeTreatment: BlurredEdgeTreatment = BlurredEdgeTreatment.Rectangle

  /**
   * Complete default Blur Style.
   *
   * This Style is replayed before composition-local and explicit Styles.
   */
  public val style: HazeBlurStyle = HazeBlurStyle {
    blurEnabled(isBlurEnabledByDefault())
    blurRadius(blurRadius)
    noiseFactor(noiseFactor)
    backgroundColor(Color.Transparent)
    colorEffects(emptyList())
    fallbackColorEffect(null)
    alpha(1f)
    mask(null)
    progressive(null)
    blurredEdgeTreatment(blurredEdgeTreatment)
  }

  /**
   * Default value for Blur enablement. This function only returns `true` on
   * platforms where we know blurring works reliably.
   *
   * This is not the same as everywhere where it technically works. Some platforms may
   * still need extra invalidation workarounds for reliable redraws.
   *
   * The devices excluded by this function may change in the future.
   */
  public fun isBlurEnabledByDefault(): Boolean = platformIsBlurEnabledByDefault()
}

# Retra app — design direction and tokens

```
Direction: Playful-soft "cute 2D under liquid glass" for GBA players (Pokémon fans first), optimized for getting back into a game in one tap.
Type: Fredoka (display, rounded) / Nunito (body). Palette: tinted neutrals ("cloud cream" light, "night indigo" dark) + Mochi pink accent (+ success / warning / danger).
Signature: Mochi, the squishy rice-cake mascot, living on a pastel sky, with glossy glass surfaces (specular top rim) and a floating glass dock whose indicator stretches like a liquid drop between tabs.
Density: balanced (airy on Home, denser in My Games / Settings).  Motion: subtle springs, one orchestrated moment per screen (staggered entrance), squish on press.
```

## Atmosphere
A calm, pastel sky that drifts very slowly behind everything (three soft light pools, 40 s loop, static
with reduced motion). Content sits on glass: translucent fill, a top-lit sheen, a 1 dp specular rim that
fades from bright at the top to nearly nothing at the bottom, and a soft shadow tinted toward the
background hue. Real backdrop blur (Haze) is only used where content actually scrolls under a surface
(dock, sticky headers, sheets, player menu) — blurring a smooth gradient is invisible, so cards are
cheap translucent glass. Below API 31 blur degrades to a denser frosted tint.

Mochi carries the emotion: happy on Home, sleepy in empty states, surprised on errors, bouncing while
loading. Everything else stays quiet so Mochi and the game art can be the colour.

## Tokens (code: `app/src/main/kotlin/app/retra/ui/theme/Tokens.kt`)

### Colour — semantic layer (light / dark)
| Token | Light "cloud cream" | Dark "night indigo" | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sky` | `#FBF5F1` | `#15132B` | window background base |
| `skyGlowA/B/C` | `#FFD3E1` / `#FFE6C7` / `#D7E4FF` | `#3B2C66` / `#2A3A6E` / `#4A2A55` | ambient light pools |
| `glassFill` | white 62 % | `#2C2950` 62 % | glass surface tint |
| `glassFillStrong` | white 86 % | `#2C2950` 90 % | frosted fallback / sheets |
| `glassRim` | white 95 % → 10 % | white 32 % → 4 % | specular rim gradient |
| `ink` | `#2B2130` | `#F4EFFB` | primary text (14.3 : 1 / 16.0 : 1) |
| `inkMuted` | `#6B5E70` | `#B9B0CE` | secondary text (5.6 : 1 / 8.8 : 1) |
| `accent` | `#C7366B` | `#FF8FB4` | Mochi pink: primary actions, active states |
| `onAccent` | `#FFFFFF` (5.0 : 1) | `#2A0E1D` (8.4 : 1) | text on accent |
| `accentSoft` | `#FFE1EA` | `#4A2846` | selected chips, soft containers |
| `success` | `#23794F` | `#7FE0AE` | "You have it", verified |
| `warning` | `#965C0A` | `#F6C56E` | CRC mismatch, beta |
| `danger` | `#C4364A` | `#FF8F9C` | delete, errors |
| `shadow` | `#7A4A60` @ 14 % | black @ 40 % | tinted elevation |

Catalog entries bring their own pastel `accent`, used only as a card wash, never for text.

### Type (7 sizes)
| Token | Font | Size / line | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | Fredoka | 32 / 38 | SemiBold 600 |
| `title` | Fredoka | 24 / 30 | SemiBold 600 |
| `headline` | Fredoka | 20 / 26 | Medium 500 |
| `bodyStrong` | Nunito | 16 / 22 | ExtraBold 800 |
| `body` | Nunito | 16 / 23 | Regular 400 |
| `label` | Nunito | 14 / 18 | SemiBold 600 |
| `caption` | Nunito | 12 / 16 | SemiBold 600 |

### Space (4 dp grid)
`xxs 4 · xs 8 · s 12 · m 16 · l 24 · xl 32 · xxl 48`. Screen gutter 20 dp (m + xxs).

### Radius (one family, continuous rounding)
`small 12` (chips, inputs, thumbnails) · `medium 20` (cards) · `large 28` (hero, sheets, dock) · `pill` (buttons).
Nested radius = outer − padding.

### Elevation (3 levels)
`raised` 6 dp (cards) · `floating` 16 dp (dock, FAB-like buttons) · `overlay` 28 dp (sheets, dialogs). Shadow colour = `shadow` token; in dark the glass gets lighter instead of darker shadows.

### Motion (one spring family, damping 0.82)
`snappy` stiffness 1400 (press feedback) · `smooth` 500 (indicator, chips, layout) · `gentle` 200 (screen-level, sheets).
Press = scale 0.96 on `snappy`. List entrance = fade + 16 dp rise, 40 ms stagger, max 8 items staggered.
Idle loops (sky drift 40 s, Mochi breathing 2.4 s) stop entirely with reduced motion (system animator
scale 0 or the in-app toggle); springs become snaps.

## Components
* **GlassSurface** — fill + sheen + rim + tinted shadow; `blur = true` only for surfaces over scrolling content.
* **Dock** — floating 64 dp glass pill, 5 tabs, liquid indicator (leading edge `snappy`, trailing edge `smooth`, so it stretches then settles).
* **Buttons** — pill; primary = accent fill; secondary = glass; tertiary = text. ≥ 48 dp tall; squish on press; disabled = 38 % alpha.
* **GameCover** — bundled art → last screenshot → generated cover (pastel stripes/dots seeded by CRC32 + title + game code).
* **Sheets** — in-window glass sheet with drag handle, scrim 32 %, back gesture closes.
* **Empty / error / loading** — always Mochi + one sentence + one action. No spinners except the patch progress ring.

## Accessibility
Text ≥ 4.5 : 1 against glass-on-sky, touch targets ≥ 48 dp, every icon-only button has a TalkBack
label, game controls expose a single "Game controls" node, reduced motion honoured everywhere.

## Never
Emoji as icons; purple→blue gradients; neon glows; gradient text; random blobs; cards in cards;
bounce on everything; fake numbers; lorem ipsum; offering commercial ROM downloads.

package app.retra.ui.components

import androidx.compose.foundation.background
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxScope
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.staticCompositionLocalOf
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.draw.clip
import androidx.compose.ui.draw.drawWithCache
import androidx.compose.ui.draw.shadow
import androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Offset
import androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Size
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Brush
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Outline
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Shape
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.drawOutline
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.drawscope.Stroke
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.drawscope.translate
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.Dp
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import app.retra.ui.theme.Elevation
import app.retra.ui.theme.Radius
import app.retra.ui.theme.Retra
import app.retra.ui.theme.RetraColors
import dev.chrisbanes.haze.HazeInput
import dev.chrisbanes.haze.HazeState
import dev.chrisbanes.haze.blur.HazeBlurStyle
import dev.chrisbanes.haze.blur.HazeColorEffect
import dev.chrisbanes.haze.blur.hazeBlur

/** The HazeState whose source is the scrolling screen content (null in previews/tests without it). */
val LocalHazeState = staticCompositionLocalOf<HazeState?> { null }

/**
 * Liquid-glass surface: translucent fill, top-lit sheen, specular rim (bright top, fading bottom),
 * a faint inner border and a soft tinted shadow.
 *
 * [blur] = true samples and blurs the content behind (Haze; API 31+). Use it only where content
 * scrolls underneath (dock, headers, sheets). Below API 31 Haze falls back to a denser frosted tint.
 */
@Composable
fun GlassSurface(
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    shape: Shape = Radius.mediumShape,
    elevation: Dp = Elevation.raised,
    blur: Boolean = false,
    strong: Boolean = false,
    wash: Color? = null,
    content: @Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit,
) {
    val c = Retra.colors
    val haze = LocalHazeState.current
    val fill = if (strong) c.glassFillStrong else c.glassFill
    val blurStyle = remember(c, strong) { glassBlurStyle(c, strong) }
    Box(
        modifier
            .then(if (elevation > 0.dp) Modifier.shadow(elevation, shape, clip = false, ambientColor = c.shadow, spotColor = c.shadow) else Modifier)
            .clip(shape)
            .then(
                if (blur && haze != null) Modifier.hazeBlur(HazeInput.Sources(haze), blurStyle)
                else Modifier.background(fill),
            )
            .then(if (wash != null) Modifier.background(wash) else Modifier)
            .glassHighlights(shape, c),
        content = content,
    )
}

private fun glassBlurStyle(c: RetraColors, strong: Boolean) = HazeBlurStyle {
    blurRadius(if (strong) 32.dp else 24.dp)
    noiseFactor(0.04f)
    backgroundColor(c.sky)
    colorEffects(listOf(HazeColorEffect.tint((if (strong) c.glassFillStrong else c.glassFill).copy(alpha = if (c.isDark) 0.62f else 0.55f))))
    fallbackColorEffect(HazeColorEffect.tint(c.glassFillStrong))
}

/** Draws the sheen + specular rim + inner border on top of the content's background. */
fun Modifier.glassHighlights(shape: Shape, c: RetraColors, rimWidth: Dp = 1.dp): Modifier = drawWithCache {
    val outline = shape.createOutline(size, layoutDirection, this)
    val rimPx = rimWidth.toPx()
    val sheen = Brush.verticalGradient(
        0f to c.glassSheen,
        0.42f to c.glassSheen.copy(alpha = c.glassSheen.alpha * 0.18f),
        1f to Color.Transparent,
    )
    val rim = Brush.verticalGradient(0f to c.glassRimTop, 0.5f to c.glassRimBottom, 1f to c.glassRimBottom.copy(alpha = c.glassRimBottom.alpha * 2.5f))
    val innerInset = rimPx * 2.5f
    val innerOutline = shape.createOutline(Size(size.width - innerInset * 2, size.height - innerInset * 2), layoutDirection, this)
    val inner = Brush.verticalGradient(0f to Color.White.copy(alpha = if (c.isDark) 0.06f else 0.35f), 0.3f to Color.Transparent)
    onDrawWithContent {
        drawOutlineSheen(outline, sheen)
        drawContent()
        drawOutline(outline, rim, style = Stroke(rimPx * 2))
        translate(innerInset, innerInset) { drawOutline(innerOutline, inner, style = Stroke(rimPx)) }
    }

    drawRect(brush, topLeft = Offset.Zero, size = Size(size.width, size.height * 0.6f))

import androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas

import app.retra.ui.theme.Retra
import kotlin.math.PI
import kotlin.math.cos
import kotlin.math.sin

/**
 * The pastel sky behind every screen: a base colour lit by three soft light pools that drift on a
 * 40 s loop (updated ~15 times a second — the motion is far too slow to need more). Static when
 * motion is reduced.
 */
@Composable
fun AmbientSky(modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    val c = Retra.colors
    val reduce = Retra.reduceMotion
    var phase by remember { mutableFloatStateOf(0.18f) }
    if (!reduce) {
        LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
            val start = withFrameMillis { it }
            var last = 0L
            while (true) {
                withFrameMillis { now ->
                    if (now - last >= 66) {
                        last = now
                        phase = (((now - start) % 40_000L) / 40_000f + 0.18f) % 1f
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Canvas(modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
        drawRect(c.sky)
        val t = phase * 2f * PI.toFloat()
        val w = size.width
        val h = size.height
        val r = maxOf(w, h)
        glow(c.skyGlowA, Offset(w * (0.15f + 0.08f * cos(t)), h * (0.08f + 0.05f * sin(t))), r * 0.75f, 0.95f)
        glow(c.skyGlowB, Offset(w * (0.95f + 0.06f * sin(t + 1.3f)), h * (0.42f + 0.06f * cos(t + 1.3f))), r * 0.62f, 0.85f)
        glow(c.skyGlowC, Offset(w * (0.25f + 0.07f * sin(t + 2.6f)), h * (0.98f + 0.04f * cos(t + 2.6f))), r * 0.7f, 0.9f)
    }
}

private fun DrawScope.glow(color: Color, center: Offset, radius: Float, strength: Float) {
    drawCircle(
        brush = Brush.radialGradient(
            0f to color.copy(alpha = strength),
            0.45f to color.copy(alpha = strength * 0.45f),
            1f to color.copy(alpha = 0f),
            center = center,
            radius = radius,
        ),
        radius = radius,
        center = center,
    )
}

data class DockItem(val label: String, val icon: ImageVector, val selectedIcon: ImageVector = icon)

/**
 * Floating glass dock. The indicator is a liquid drop: when moving to another tab, its leading edge
 * springs ahead (stiff) and the trailing edge follows (softer), so it stretches and then settles.
 */
@Composable
fun Dock(
    items: List<DockItem>,
    selected: Int,
    onSelect: (Int) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    val c = Retra.colors
    val reduce = Retra.reduceMotion
    GlassSurface(
        modifier.height(68.dp).widthIn(max = 460.dp),
        shape = Radius.pillShape,
        elevation = Elevation.floating,
        blur = true,
    ) {
        BoxWithConstraints(Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(6.dp)) {
            val count = items.size
            val itemWidthPx = constraints.maxWidth.toFloat() / count
            val left = remember { Animatable(selected.toFloat()) }
            val right = remember { Animatable(selected.toFloat() + 1f) }
            LaunchedEffect(selected) {
                val target = selected.toFloat()
                val movingRight = target > left.value
                val fast = if (reduce) snap<Float>() else spring(0.72f, Motion.SNAPPY)
                val slow = if (reduce) snap<Float>() else spring(Motion.DAMPING, 260f)
                launch { left.animateTo(target, if (movingRight) slow else fast) }
                launch { right.animateTo(target + 1f, if (movingRight) fast else slow) }
            }
            Canvas(Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
                val l = left.value * itemWidthPx
                val r = right.value * itemWidthPx
                val inset = 4.dp.toPx()
                val h = size.height
                val stretch = ((r - l) / itemWidthPx - 1f).coerceIn(0f, 2f)
                // Squeeze vertically a little while stretched, like a drop of liquid.
                val vInset = stretch * 4.dp.toPx()
                drawRoundRect(
                    brush = Brush.verticalGradient(listOf(c.accentSoft, c.accentSoft.copy(alpha = 0.85f))),
                    topLeft = Offset(l + inset, vInset),
                    size = Size((r - l - inset * 2).coerceAtLeast(0f), h - vInset * 2),
                    cornerRadius = CornerRadius((h - vInset * 2) / 2),
                )
                drawRoundRect(
                    color = Color.White.copy(alpha = if (c.isDark) 0.10f else 0.55f),
                    topLeft = Offset(l + inset + 6.dp.toPx(), vInset + 3.dp.toPx()),
                    size = Size((r - l - inset * 2 - 12.dp.toPx()).coerceAtLeast(0f), 3.dp.toPx()),
                    cornerRadius = CornerRadius(2.dp.toPx()),
                )
            }
            Row(Modifier.fillMaxSize().selectableGroup(), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceEvenly) {
                items.forEachIndexed { i, item ->
                    DockButton(item, i == selected, { onSelect(i) }, Modifier.weight(1f))
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun DockButton(item: DockItem, selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier) {
    val c = Retra.colors
    val source = remember { MutableInteractionSource() }
    val reduce = Retra.reduceMotion
    val lift by animateFloatAsState(if (selected) 1f else 0f, Motion.smooth(reduce), label = "lift")
    val density = LocalDensity.current
    Box(
        modifier
            .fillMaxHeight()
            .pressScale(source, 0.9f)
            .semantics { this.selected = selected }
            .clickable(interactionSource = source, indication = null, role = Role.Tab, onClick = onClick),
        contentAlignment = Alignment.Center,
    ) {
        Column(horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally, modifier = Modifier.graphicsLayer { translationY = with(density) { (-1).dp.toPx() } * lift }) {
            Icon(
                if (selected) item.selectedIcon else item.icon,
                contentDescription = null,
                tint = if (selected) c.onAccentSoft else c.inkMuted,
                modifier = Modifier.size(24.dp),
            )
            Text(item.label, style = RetraType.caption, color = if (selected) c.onAccentSoft else c.inkMuted, maxLines = 1)
        }
    }
}
